engine.name: Composition & regime
engine.brief: From D2/D9/D10/D14 + atmo -> composition class + bulk regime (rocky/icy/carbon/iron/ocean/gas-giant/magma-ocean/stripped-core) + base palette. ALSO outputs the body "type" as a DERIVED LABEL (a name read off the result), never as an upstream input.

dossier.mechanism: Equilibrium condensation + accretion chemistry decides what a body is MADE of, and bulk mass/density decides its REGIME. Three knobs set the material budget: (1) C/O ratio of the feeding disk — if C/O ≳ 0.8–1 (vs solar ~0.55), CO locks up oxygen and the condensation sequence flips from silicates+water-ice to graphite/SiC/diamond (carbon planet); (2) iron vs silicate partitioning — set by disk metallicity and by post-accretion mantle stripping (giant impacts or iron-rich inner-disk enrichment), giving a core mass fraction (CMF) from ~0.3 Earth-like up to ~0.7 Mercury/super-Mercury; (3) volatile/ice budget — set by where the body accreted relative to the frost line (inside = bone-dry rock, beyond = ice-rock to ocean-world). Bulk mass+radius then sorts the body into a REGIME along the mass-radius relation and the ~1.6 R⊕ / ~4–5 M⊕ radius valley: rocky terrestrial → ocean/water world → sub-Neptune (H/He or steam envelope) → gas/ice giant; and the heat overlay adds magma-ocean (T_eq above the silicate solidus, ~1500–2000 K) and stripped-core (envelope lost to escape) endmembers. The composition class + regime is read off the result as a derived TYPE LABEL — never assumed up front. Base palette follows the dominant condensed material (basalt grey-brown, ferric red, graphite/tar black with diamond-facet specular, water-ice white-blue, ammonia/methane gas tints).

inputs.name: volatileFraction (D2)
inputs.note: frost-line ice budget; in code derived from orbitAU/frostLineAU inside deriveComposition, then exposed as the scalar.

inputs.name: ironFraction (D9)
inputs.note: core iron → CMF → density. Scalar carries it, but it is itself derived from stellar metallicity + a stripping RNG; the underlying metallicity is system-graph, not a body scalar.

inputs.name: carbonToOxygen (D10)
inputs.note: the carbon-planet switch at C/O>0.8 (Kuchner-Seager swap point). Scalar suffices to gate the class.

inputs.name: massGravity (D14)
inputs.note: sets crater/shield scale; but a single gravity scalar cannot by itself place a body on the radius-valley regime axis — see mass+radius below.

inputs.name: tempEq (D1)
inputs.note: gates magma-ocean (above silicate solidus) and volatile state (ice vs liquid vs vapor) of the same bulk composition.

inputs.name: atmoComposition (D4)
inputs.note: n2-o2 / co2 / h2-he / none — distinguishes a thick-envelope sub-Neptune/gas-giant from a bare rocky regime, and tints the base palette.

inputs.name: atmoDensity (D5)
inputs.note: envelope mass — the rocky-vs-gas-giant regime is really an envelope-fraction question; D5 stands in for it.

inputs.name: bulk mass AND radius (→ density, CMF, radius-valley position)
inputs.note: The regime split (rocky/ocean/sub-Neptune/giant) is a mass-RADIUS / bulk-density classification (radius valley ~1.6 R⊕). A single D14 gravity scalar collapses mass and radius into one number and cannot recover density or CMF; code computes a `density` field internally but never feeds it back to choose the regime. Needs mass + radius as a pair, or density itself, as a carried field.

inputs.name: stellar metallicity [Fe/H] + frost-line AU + orbit AU
inputs.note: deriveComposition's ACTUAL inputs (PhysicsEngine.js:341) are metallicity, orbitAU, frostLineAU — system/star-graph quantities. The L0 scalar vector exposes only the OUTPUTS (D2/D9/D10). Fine for per-body rendering, but the engine cannot be re-run or perturbed from the scalar vector alone; the generative provenance lives in the dropped system graph.

inputs.name: giant-impact / mantle-stripping flag (super-Mercury, stripped-core)
inputs.note: High-CMF iron worlds and stripped-cores are a COLLISION-history / escape-history outcome (sibling impacts, XUV stripping). Currently faked by an RNG scatter term inside deriveComposition; the real driver is system-graph collision history + D6 retention, which a per-body scalar cannot carry.

outputs.name: compositionClass
outputs.note: derived LABEL: rocky/silicate, iron-rich, carbon, ice-rock, ocean, gas-giant, magma-ocean, stripped-core. In code = surfaceType {silicate|iron-rich|ice-rock|carbon} via a threshold cascade (PhysicsEngine.js:367-377) — regime endmembers are missing from that cascade.

outputs.name: ironFraction (D9)
outputs.note: emitted scalar; downstream → D13 magnetic field, mineralogy palette.

outputs.name: carbonToOxygen (D10)
outputs.note: emitted scalar; gates F42 carbon crust at >0.8.

outputs.name: volatileFraction (D2)
outputs.note: emitted scalar; gates ice/ocean features and frost.

outputs.name: density
outputs.note: computed (baseDensity = 3500 + ironFraction*5000 - volatileFraction*2000) but currently UNUSED downstream — should drive the regime classification it is ideally suited for.

outputs.name: basePalette
outputs.note: base albedo/color + specular character per dominant material: basalt, ferric red, graphite-tar black + diamond facet glint, water-ice, gas tints. Governs the lowest layer every other engine paints over.

outputs.name: bulkRegime
outputs.note: rocky / ocean / sub-Neptune / gas-giant / magma-ocean / stripped-core — selects which whole downstream feature stack is even physically possible (solid-surface vs gas-deck).

featureMap: Base surface palette / albedo for ALL solid-surface presets (Rocky, Ocean, Mars, Venus, Eyeball, Frozen, Europa)
F42 carbon crust (graphite/SiC/diamond/tar) — gated by carbonToOxygen>0.8
Iron-rich metal-sheen surface character (stripped-core / super-Mercury)
F41 magma ocean material (silicate melt) — the molten endmember of the rocky class under extreme T_eq
Gas-giant vs ice-giant base envelope tint (Jovian/Saturnian/Neptunian/Sub-Neptune presets) — the gas-vs-rock regime fork

Whole-body archetype assignment (the planet-archetypes.js ARCHETYPES table: impact-airless, tectonic-terrestrial, volcanic, exotic-carbon, gas-giant…) which currently gates EVERY downstream feature's membership

cheapApprox.description: Pure per-body arithmetic, no simulation, exactly as deriveComposition already does — runs in microseconds. Step 1 (material budget): C/O = clamp(0.55 + 0.3*metallicity + scatter); ironFraction = clamp(0.28 + 0.15*metallicity + stripScatter); volatileFraction from frostRatio = orbitAU/frostLineAU (piecewise: <0.5 dry, 0.5-1 transition, >1 ice-rich). Step 2 (density): density = 3500 + ironFraction*5000 - volatileFraction*2000 (kg/m^3). Step 3 (REGIME — the fix): replace the discrete surfaceType cascade with a soft classification over a 3-axis material simplex (rock / ice / iron, plus the C/O override) crossed with a regime axis from bulk density + radius vs the ~1.6 R⊕ radius-valley threshold and envelope-fraction (D5): density>6000 → iron-rich; C/O>0.8 → carbon (override); radius>~1.6 R⊕ AND H/He envelope → sub-Neptune/gas-giant; volatile>~0.4 AND T_eq in liquid band → ocean; T_eq>silicate-solidus(~1500-2000K) → magma-ocean; else rocky. Emit class as the ARGMAX label but ALSO emit the continuous membership weights so the palette is a blend, not a hard swap. Step 4 (palette): lerp base albedo/specular between material endpoints by those weights (e.g. tar-black↔diamond-glint by C/O strength; grey-basalt↔ferric-red by oxidation/iron; add ice-white by volatile). Baked-field option: precompute a small 2D/3D LUT (density × T_eq × C/O → palette RGBA + class id) as a tiny texture sampled once per body — pure texture fetch, zero ALU, if even the arithmetic is grudged.

epochBehavior.note: Composition + regime is set at accretion and is the substrate every later epoch edits — it runs first, once per body, and does not re-run per epoch. The ONE exception that is genuinely epoch-coupled is the magma-ocean endmember: it is a present-T_eq state of the rocky class, so if an epoch model ever cooled a body, the same composition would re-label magma-ocean→rocky. Treat that as a cheap re-evaluation of the class label against current T_eq, not a re-derivation of the material budget.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: This is the textbook type-demotion site. (1) deriveComposition (PhysicsEngine.js:367-377) hard-classifies surfaceType via a threshold IF-cascade into 4 discrete strings {carbon, iron-rich, ice-rock, silicate} — the regime endmembers (ocean, sub-Neptune, gas-giant, magma-ocean, stripped-core) are MISSING, so those bodies get their regime hard-assigned elsewhere by named PRESET rather than derived from drivers. (2) planet-archetypes.js encodes named ARCHETYPES (exotic-carbon, gas-giant, volcanic…) each with a hand-listed `bodies`/`presets` set, and EVERY downstream feature declares membership by archetype STRING. So feature presence is gated by a discrete type label, not by the continuous driver that should switch it (carbon crust should appear when C/O>0.8 for ANY body, not only when the preset == 'Carbon (high C/O)'; the F42 comment even admits 'every other preset derives ratio 0 outright' — i.e. the driver is correct but the membership is still gated by the type name as a belt-and-suspenders hard-code). (3) The computed `density` field is discarded instead of driving the rocky↔gas-giant regime fork, so that fork is currently a preset choice, not a physics output. Fix: emit continuous class-membership weights + density-based regime score; let downstream features read the driver/field threshold directly and drop the archetype-string gate to a derived label.
loadBearingClaims: The rocky/ocean/sub-Neptune/gas-giant REGIME split is fundamentally a mass-RADIUS / bulk-density classification (radius valley ~1.6 R⊕, transition ~4-5 M⊕), and the current single D14 gravity scalar cannot carry it — mass and radius are collapsed into one number, and the internally-computed density is never used. (If regime can in fact be recovered from D14+D5 alone, the underSupplied flag on mass+radius is wrong.)

The C/O>0.8 carbon-planet swap point and the graphite/SiC/diamond condensation flip are real published thresholds (Kuchner-Seager 2005; carbide-interior work), so gating F42 on D10 is sound — but the exact 0.8 cutoff is a modeling choice, not a hard observed line (disk C/O ≳ 1 is the more commonly cited threshold).

Mercury-grade high-CMF (~0.7) iron worlds and stripped-cores are a COLLISION/ESCAPE-history outcome, not a smooth function of metallicity; faking them with an RNG scatter term on ironFraction will under-produce the bimodal super-Mercury population and cannot be reproduced from the per-body scalar (provenance is in the dropped system graph).

The density formula (3500 + ironFraction*5000 - volatileFraction*2000, clamped 1000-8000) is a crude linear stand-in; real bulk density is a nonlinear EOS function of mass (gravitational compression), so this will mis-rank regime near the rocky/sub-Neptune boundary if used as the regime discriminator without a mass-dependent compression term.

Treating magma-ocean as a present-T_eq STATE of the rocky composition class (rather than its own composition) is physically correct for dry lava planets like K2-141b, but assumes the silicate-solidus temperature is roughly composition-independent (~1500-2000 K); a carbon or iron crust would have a very different melt point, so the magma label must be computed AFTER the material class, not before.

verdicts.claim: The rocky/ocean/sub-Neptune/gas-giant REGIME split is fundamentally a mass-RADIUS / bulk-density classification (radius valley ~1.6 R⊕, ~4-5 M⊕), and the single D14 gravity scalar cannot carry it; internally-computed density is never used for regime.
verdicts.reasoning: Astrophysics confirmed: the radius valley (Fulton gap) at ~1.5-2.0 R⊕ separating rocky super-Earths from sub-Neptunes is a real, well-established mass-radius/bulk-density phenomenon (multiple sources). Code confirmed: in PlanetGenerator.js _pickType (lines 321, 697-853) the regime/type is chosen by RNG rolls over orbital zones (e.g. `if (roll < 0.4) return 'gas-giant'`), NOT from bulk density. composition.density (PhysicsEngine.js:380-381) is returned and consumed ONLY by ring/Roche physics (PlanetGenerator.js:517 → rocheLimit), never by the regime fork. A single D14 gravity scalar indeed cannot recover mass+radius separately or place a body on the radius-valley axis. underSupplied flag is justified. Minor caveat: ~1.6 R⊕ is a representative midpoint; the literature gap is a 1.5-2.0 band, so the precise number is a modeling choice, not refuting the claim.

verdicts.claim: C/O>0.8 carbon-planet swap (graphite/SiC/diamond flip, Kuchner-Seager 2005) is a real published threshold, so gating F42 on D10 is sound — but 0.8 is a modeling choice and ≳1 is the more commonly cited threshold.
verdicts.reasoning: First half is solidly confirmed: C/O ≳ 0.8 flips the condensation sequence to graphite/SiC/TiC with CO locking up oxygen (Kuchner & Seager 2005; Bond et al. 2010), so gating the carbon class on D10 is physically sound, and the code (PhysicsEngine.js:369 `if (carbonToOxygen > 0.8)`) implements exactly this. However the dossier's hedge that '≳1 is the more commonly cited threshold' is overstated/inaccurate: the literature most commonly cites C/O ≳ 0.8 as the carbon-rich onset (Bond et al. 2010 established 0.8 'more precisely'), with 0.8 being the standard quoted figure, not 1.0. I mark the COMPOSITE claim refuted because that specific sub-assertion is wrong, though the load-bearing part (0.8 gate is sound) is correct.

verdicts.claim: Mercury-grade high-CMF (~0.7) iron worlds / stripped-cores are a collision/escape-history outcome, not a smooth function of metallicity; faking them with RNG scatter on ironFraction under-produces the bimodal super-Mercury population and cannot be reproduced from the per-body scalar.
verdicts.reasoning: Astrophysics confirmed: super-Mercuries form via giant impacts / mantle stripping (Denman et al. 2024 MNRAS 529:2577 'Formation of super-Mercuries via giant impacts'; Forming Mercury by Giant Impacts). High-velocity collisions, often multiple, are required — explicitly a collision-history outcome, not a metallicity function. Code confirmed: ironFraction = clamp(0.28 + 0.15*metallicity + (rng-0.5)*0.1) (PhysicsEngine.js:350-352) — a smooth metallicity term plus tiny ±0.05 RNG scatter, capped at 0.6, which cannot even reach Mercury's ~0.68 CMF, let alone produce a bimodal population. The provenance (collision history) genuinely lives in the dropped system graph. Claim holds.

verdicts.claim: The density formula (3500 + ironFraction*5000 - volatileFraction*2000, clamped 1000-8000) is a crude linear stand-in; real bulk density is a nonlinear EOS function of mass (gravitational compression), so it will mis-rank regime near the rocky/sub-Neptune boundary if used as the discriminator without a mass-dependent compression term.
verdicts.reasoning: Code matches the formula verbatim (PhysicsEngine.js:380-381, clamp 1000-8000). Astrophysics confirmed: bulk density is genuinely nonlinear in mass due to self-compression (Vinet / 3rd-order Birch-Murnaghan EOS; Seager et al. 2007; Grasset et al. 2009) — as mass rises, matter compresses above zero-pressure density, eventually causing a radius maximum. The formula has NO mass term at all (only iron/volatile fractions), so it cannot capture gravitational compression and would indeed mis-rank near the boundary. Note this is partly hypothetical for the CURRENT code, since density is not used as the regime discriminator today — the claim is correctly framed as a warning about the proposed fix that would use it.

verdicts.claim: Treating magma-ocean as a present-T_eq STATE of the rocky class (not its own composition) is correct for dry lava planets like K2-141b, but assumes silicate-solidus (~1500-2000 K) is roughly composition-independent; a carbon/iron crust melts very differently, so the magma label must be computed AFTER the material class.
verdicts.reasoning: Physically sound: lava worlds like K2-141b are dry silicate bodies whose dayside exceeds the silicate solidus — a thermal STATE, not a distinct bulk composition, so re-evaluating the label against current T_eq (per epochBehavior) is correct. The caveat is also valid: silicate solidus (~1500-2000 K) differs sharply from a carbon-phase or iron melt point, so applying one solidus to all classes would mislabel carbon/iron bodies; computing magma AFTER the material class is the right ordering. Confidence medium because the exact solidus band is composition- and pressure-dependent even within silicates (peridotite vs basalt), but the structural claim is correct. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: (typeDemotionNote) deriveComposition hard-classifies into 4 discrete strings missing regime endmembers; planet-archetypes.js gates every downstream feature by archetype STRING; computed density is discarded instead of driving the regime fork.
verdicts.reasoning: All three sub-claims verified in code. (1) PhysicsEngine.js:367-377 is exactly a 4-branch IF-cascade emitting {carbon, iron-rich, ice-rock, silicate}; ocean/sub-Neptune/gas-giant/magma-ocean/stripped-core are absent. (2) planet-archetypes.js: every FEATURE row declares an `archetypes: [...]` string array (craters, bands, jets, etc.), and downstream membership is gated by that string — confirmed across the table. (3) Regime fork is RNG/zone-based in _pickType, and density only feeds ring/Roche physics. One precision note: density is NOT literally 'discarded' (it is used for rings via PlanetGenerator.js:517), so the word 'unused/discarded downstream' is mildly overstated — but the load-bearing assertion (density never drives the regime fork) is correct.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time feasible and hides no offline sim, no iterative relaxation, and no per-pixel global solve. It is pure per-body scalar arithmetic, run ONCE per body at generation time (epochBehavior mode:'once'), not per-pixel or per-frame — the code already does exactly this in deriveComposition (PhysicsEngine.js:341-383) in microseconds. Step 1 (C/O, ironFraction, volatileFraction) is clamped linear/piecewise arithmetic. Step 2 (density) is a single linear expression. Step 3 (the proposed regime fix) is a soft classification over a 3-axis simplex plus threshold comparisons (density>6000, C/O>0.8, radius vs 1.6 R⊕, T_eq vs solidus) — all O(1) comparisons and a softmax/argmax over a handful of axes, no iteration. Step 4 (palette) is a handful of lerps between material endpoints. The baked-field fallback (a tiny 3D LUT density×T_eq×C/O → RGBA+classId sampled once per body) is a single texture fetch with zero ALU. NO closed-form/cheap claim here conceals a hidden EOS integration: the dossier is HONEST that real bulk density needs a nonlinear EOS and explicitly flags the linear formula as a crude stand-in that will mis-rank near the boundary (loadBearingClaim 4) — it does not pretend the linear formula is physically exact, it proposes it as a deliberately cheap discriminator. The only genuinely epoch-coupled piece (magma-ocean re-label vs current T_eq) is itself just a cheap per-body threshold re-check, not a re-simulation. The single real architectural gap is informational, not computational: regime cannot be placed without mass+radius (or density) carried as a field, because D14 collapses them — that is an input-provisioning fix, not a cost-class violation.

verify.notes: Code grounding verified against /home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/generation/PhysicsEngine.js (deriveComposition lines 341-383; density 380-381; surfaceType cascade 367-377) and /home/ax/projects/well-dipper/planet-archetypes.js (per-feature `archetypes:[...]` string gating, 245 lines) and /home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/generation/PlanetGenerator.js (_pickType RNG/zone regime selection lines 321,697-853; composition.density consumed only by ring/Roche physics at 517). Astrophysics claims confirmed via published literature: carbon-planet C/O≳0.8 condensation flip (Kuchner & Seager 2005, Bond et al. 2010); radius valley/Fulton gap 1.5-2.0 R⊕ (Fulton 2017 lineage); super-Mercury via giant impacts (Denman et al. 2024 MNRAS 529:2577); nonlinear self-compression EOS (Seager et al. 2007, Grasset et al. 2009). Net: 4 of 6 load-bearing claims hold cleanly at high confidence; 1 refuted on an overstated sub-assertion (the '≳1 is more commonly cited' hedge contradicts the actual literature, which cites 0.8); the typeDemotionNote 'density discarded' wording is mildly overstated (density IS used, for rings, just not for regime) but its load-bearing core is correct. The dossier is unusually honest about its own limitations and does not disguise an offline solve as cheap.

engine.name: Body figure
engine.brief: From D7/D8/D14 + orbit + tidal -> overall body shape: sphere / triaxial / Roche-distorted / comet-tail / degenerate. (Illumination is split out to the E2-illumination sidecar.)

dossier.mechanism: The overall shape ("figure") of a self-gravitating body is the equilibrium surface where self-gravity, rotational centrifugal potential, and the primary's tidal potential balance against material strength. Four real processes set it: (1) Self-gravity vs. material strength — below the "potato radius" (~200 km for icy, ~300-400 km for rocky bodies; Lineweaver & Norman 2010) strength wins and the body keeps an irregular collisional/accretional shape; above it self-gravity rounds it into a hydrostatic figure. (2) Rotation — a rounded fluid body spinning slowly is an oblate Maclaurin spheroid; past the bifurcation at c/a≈0.583 (T/|W|>0.1375; Chandrasekhar, Jacobi sequence) it goes triaxial (Jacobi ellipsoid), and rubble piles disrupt at the ~2.2 h spin barrier (critical density-dependent period sqrt(3π/Gρ)). (3) Tides — a synchronously locked body is raised into a prolate/triaxial figure with its long axis pointing at the primary; the static tidal bulge amplitude scales with the fluid Love number h2 (0-2.5) and the tidal parameter (M_primary/M_body)(R_body/a)^3. (4) Roche regime — inside the fluid Roche limit d≈2.44 R_p(ρ_p/ρ_s)^(1/3) tidal stress exceeds self-gravity and the body is pulled into an extreme Roche ellipsoid → tidal stream / disruption. A 5th, non-equilibrium regime: actively sublimating volatile bodies (comets) are sculpted by anisotropic mass loss into bilobate/contact-binary/cometary-tail shapes rather than any equilibrium figure. The engine selects regime from drivers and emits the body's base ellipsoid axes (a,b,c) + a low-frequency irregularity field, before any T2+ terrain engine adds relief.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Primary driver: sets whether the body clears the potato radius (strength-vs-gravity round-off) and the self-gravity term in every balance. A scalar gravity carries this fine.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Spin rate sets oblateness (Maclaurin flattening f≈(5/4)ω²R³/GM·... ) and the Maclaurin→Jacobi bifurcation / spin-barrier disruption. Scalar is adequate.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Selects the synchronous/prolate regime (long axis toward primary) vs. free rotation. As a scalar lock-fraction it works, but it does NOT carry the bulge ORIENTATION relative to the primary — that needs the system graph (see below).

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Hard-zeroed in current pipeline. Strong tidal heating lowers effective rigidity → raises fluid Love number h2 → larger tidal/rotational figure (Io is plausibly relaxing toward a more fluid triaxial shape). With D12=0 the engine cannot soften a body's figure under heating; all bodies are treated as cold/rigid. This is a dropped driver the figure regime genuinely needs.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction / composition (ice vs rock)
inputs.note: Sets bulk density ρ_s, which enters the potato radius threshold, the spin-barrier period sqrt(3π/Gρ), and the Roche limit ρ ratio. Iron fraction is a usable proxy for density; D10 carbonToOxygen / D2 volatileFraction refine ice-vs-rock.

inputs.name: orbit: semi-major axis a, primary mass M_p, primary radius R_p
inputs.note: REQUIRED for the tidal term (M_p/M_body)(R_body/a)^3 and the Roche limit d=2.44 R_p(ρ_p/ρ_s)^(1/3). The L0 graph computes star/sibling/moon/ring relationships but does NOT expose them to the per-body pipeline. A per-body scalar 'tidalLock' fraction cannot reconstruct distance-to-primary or primary density, so the magnitude of the tidal bulge and the Roche proximity are currently un-derivable — they must be faked or hard-set. This is the single biggest under-supply.

inputs.name: tidal bulge sub-primary direction vector
inputs.note: The prolate long axis must point at the primary; that is a direction in the body frame, not a scalar. Needed so the bulge faces the right way (and, with D7, so the substellar/sub-primary point lines up with E2-illumination's eyeball-climate and any substellar-magma editor). A scalar interface cannot carry this orientation.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory (impact flux / collisional history)
inputs.note: For sub-potato-radius bodies, governs how battered/irregular the base shape is (heavy collisional history → more lumpy, possible large facets / giant-impact flat faces).

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction + D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Gate the cometary/sublimation-sculpted regime: high volatile fraction + temp above sublimation threshold → anisotropic-mass-loss shapes (bilobate, neck, tail-source) instead of an equilibrium figure.

inputs.name: E? collisional/accretion history field (giant-impact record)
inputs.note: True irregular shapes (contact binaries, giant-impact basins that flatten one hemisphere) come from discrete collision events, not a scalar. No upstream engine currently emits an impact-event list; the irregularity must be approximated by seeded noise rather than derived from real history.

outputs.name: baseEllipsoidAxes
outputs.note: The three principal semi-axes (a≥b≥c) of the body's base figure, plus the orientation quaternion (long axis → primary for locked bodies, spin axis → c). This is the canvas every downstream terrain/relief engine displaces from.

outputs.name: figureRegime
outputs.note: Continuous regime weights, NOT a discrete enum: {irregular, oblateSpheroid, triaxialJacobi, prolateTidal, rocheStretched, cometSculpted}. Downstream engines read the dominant + blend.

outputs.name: flatteningField / displacement basis
outputs.note: Low-spatial-frequency radial displacement field encoding rotational oblateness + tidal bulge + (for small bodies) seeded large-scale lumpiness; feeds the vertex/heightfield base before T2 craters/tectonics.

outputs.name: equatorialBulge / tidalBulge
outputs.note: Visible equatorial fattening (fast rotators) and sub-primary/anti-primary bulge pair (locked bodies).

outputs.name: rocheTail / tidalStream
outputs.note: For bodies inside/near the Roche limit: elongated teardrop / leading-trailing stream geometry.

outputs.name: cometTailSource / bilobateNeck
outputs.note: For volatile-sublimating bodies: bilobate two-lobe-plus-neck geometry and active-region placement that the atmosphere/coma engine reads as jet/tail sources.

outputs.name: effectiveRadiusScalar
outputs.note: A single mean-radius scalar for cheap downstream consumers that ignore the ellipsoid (back-compat).

featureMap: Body silhouette / overall roundness (sphere vs potato)
Equatorial bulge of fast rotators (oblateness)
Triaxial/elongated moons (Jacobi & tidally-locked prolate shapes; Phobos/Mimas-like)
Sub-primary tidal bulge and its orientation toward the primary
Roche-stretched / teardrop bodies and tidal streams near a primary
Cometary bilobate nucleus + neck + jet/tail source regions
Degenerate/disrupted-body geometry (contact binaries, rubble-pile lumps)

cheapApprox.description: Everything here is a per-body O(1) analytic computation done ONCE at body init (or per-epoch), producing 3 axis scalars + an orientation + a couple of noise seeds — no simulation, no iteration. Steps: (1) Density ρ from composition drivers. (2) Potato test: roundness r = smoothstep(R_potato(ρ), 1.3·R_potato, R_body) where R_potato≈ (icy)200km/(rocky)350km scaled by sqrt(strength/ρ). r→0 keeps an irregular base; r→1 rounds it. (3) Rotational oblateness via the standard fluid flattening f ≈ (5/4)·(ω²R³/GM) clamped; convert to Maclaurin (a,a,c). (4) Bifurcation gate: compute the spin parameter Ω̂²=ω²/(πGρ); if it crosses the Jacobi threshold (T/|W|>0.1375, c/a<0.583) blend a→two-unequal-equatorial axes (triaxial). If Ω̂² exceeds the ~2.2h spin-barrier value, flag disruption/elongation. (5) Tidal bulge (needs orbit a, M_p): height fraction ≈ h2·(M_p/M_body)·(R_body/a)³, h2 chosen from a rigidity proxy (raise h2 toward 2.5 as D12 tidalHeating rises — once un-zeroed). Add as a prolate term along the sub-primary axis for locked bodies. (6) Roche test: ratio q = a_orbit / [2.44 R_p (ρ_p/ρ)^(1/3)]; q<1 → exaggerate the prolate axis into a teardrop (closed-form stretch) and emit rocheTail. engine.name: Compositional province
engine.brief: composition + gross structure -> whole-disk latitudinal/hemispheric PROVINCE field (e.g. Titan Xanadu, Io zonation). Province is set EARLY (T1); the surface-chemistry PALETTE is a separate terminal engine (E12-palette, T5).

dossier.mechanism: Whole-disk compositional/structural PROVINCE field: the early, large-scale partition of a body's surface into a small number of distinct regions whose boundaries are set by global, low-spatial-frequency forcings rather than local terrain. Four real planetary-science generators dominate, and which one applies is itself decided by drivers, not by a body "type": (1) LATITUDINAL VOLATILE COLD-TRAPPING — temperature is the master control on condensed-volatile stability; insolation falls from equator to pole, so volatiles sublimate from warm zones and redeposit in cold zones, producing latitudinal banding (Io: equatorial SO2 frost cold-trap belt + warm sulfur plains, with red-brown radiation-altered plains poleward of ~±30°; Pluto/Triton seasonal N2 banding; polar caps generally). The pattern is gated by axial tilt (D3), tempEq (D1), volatile budget (D2), and atmospheric transport (D5). (2) TIDAL-LOCK ZONATION — a synchronously rotating body has a permanent substellar point, giving a radially symmetric "eyeball": a hot substellar province (lava pool at the substellar point for hot eyeballs, or a liquid "pupil" for temperate ones) grading through concentric terminator rings to a frozen antistellar province. This is the D7-driven province geometry, modulated by D1, D2, D5. (3) HEMISPHERIC/DICHOTOMOUS provinces from exogenic asymmetry — leading vs trailing hemisphere asymmetry from prograde dust sweep-up (leading) vs corotating-magnetosphere plasma/ion bombardment (trailing), the Iapetus archetype, where an initial dark leading-hemisphere coating runs away via thermal ice migration into an extreme two-province globe. This is a SYSTEM-GRAPH-driven mechanism (needs orbit sense, ring/dust sources, magnetosphere). (4) BULK-CHEMISTRY provinces — for carbon-rich bodies (C/O >= ~0.9, D10) the surface mineralogy partitions into carbide/graphite terrains that look nothing like silicate worlds, a composition-set province independent of latitude. E12-province runs EARLY (T1) and lays down the coarse field that all later chemistry/relief engines paint within; it sets WHERE provinces are, while the separate T5 palette engine sets what color/material each province reads as.

cheapApprox.description: Closed-form province SELECTOR + steered low-frequency noise for boundaries, all in one fragment pass; no offline sim. Step 1 (selector, branchless on drivers): compute a few scalar gates from the driver vector and pick the dominant province scheme as a weighted blend: zonalWeight = (1-D7)*saturate(D2)*saturate(volatileStability(D1,D3)); eyeballWeight = D7; dichotomyWeight = exogenicAsym (currently 0 because system-graph is unsupplied — see load-bearing); chemWeight = smoothstep(0.85,1.0,D10). Step 2 (province field as analytic latitude/angle functions): LATITUDINAL — provinceId from banded thresholds on |lat| whose band edges are functions of insolation peak latitude L_peak = f(D3) and a cold-trap edge latitude phi_ct = asin-style closed form from energy balance T(lat) ~ T_eq*cos(lat)^0.25 crossed against the volatile condensation temperature implied by D1 (this gives the Io-type ±30 transition for free, the boundary MOVING with the drivers). TIDALLY-LOCKED — province is a radial function of substellar angle theta = acos(dot(n, subStellarDir)): theta<r_hot -> substellar province, r_hot<theta<r_cold -> ring(s), else antistellar; r_hot,r_cold are closed-form from D1/D5 (thicker atmo D5 -> larger warm pupil). CHEMISTRY — global override flag. Step 3 (boundary realism): perturb every threshold by 2-3 octaves of domain-warped value noise (amplitude ~ a few degrees of latitude/angle) so seams are fractal, not ruler-straight; warp amplitude scales DOWN with D5 (thick atmosphere smears toward smooth zonal bands; airless bodies get crisp lobate frost edges). Step 4 (megablock, optional): one large Worley/voronoi cell biased by a hashed seed, gated on D11 low resurfacing, stamps an ancient-block provinceId. Output provinceId (categorical) + provinceWeight (smoothstep blend across each perturbed boundary). All evaluable per-fragment or baked once to a low-res equirect lookup (e.g. 512x256) sampled by later tiers. The ONLY part that secretly wants a simulation is true runaway thermal-migration dichotomy (Iapetus) and real volatile-transport equilibrium — both are replaced here by their SETTLED end-state closed forms (a sharp great-circle seam; a fixed band latitude), which is the legitimate borrow-the-scaling approach, not a time-step.

epochBehavior.note: Province is set EARLY (T1) and is intended to be laid down once at the body's first epoch as the substrate all later tiers paint within. The one legitimate per-epoch case is editor-like: if a later epoch flips a driver regime (e.g. an atmosphere is acquired/lost, changing D5, or D11 resurfacing wipes a hemisphere), the province field can be RE-RUN for that epoch and the new field supersedes the old as the host substrate — but within a single body's settled history it runs once.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: High risk that the current code hard-codes provinces by discrete body 'type' (e.g. an enum like ICE_MOON -> always polar caps, IO_TYPE -> always equatorial volcanic belt, TIDALLY_LOCKED -> fixed eyeball radii, CARBON_PLANET -> dark surface). Every one of these should DERIVE from drivers: the ±30 cold-trap edge must be a continuous function of D1/D3/D2 (so a higher-obliquity or warmer body moves or loses the band), the eyeball hot/cold radii must come from D1/D5 (so a thicker atmosphere grows the warm pupil and can erase the frozen antistellar cap), and 'carbon planet' must be a smoothstep on D10 rather than a boolean class. Two demotions are currently UNAVOIDABLE without interface changes: (a) the Io equatorial volcanic province cannot emerge because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed, so any Io-like body would be mis-generated as a passive frost world — this is a dropped-driver demotion, not a code-cleanliness one; (b) leading/trailing dichotomy is forced to a single 'symmetric' outcome because orbit sense, dust donors, and parent-magnetosphere corotation are not exposed to the per-body pipeline, so the engine literally cannot place an Iapetus-type seam from scalars alone.
loadBearingClaims: The Io ±30-degree compositional transition (equatorial SO2/sulfur cold-trap province vs poleward red-brown radiation-altered plains) is real and latitude-controlled [OBS], BUT it fundamentally depends on D12 tidal heating to drive the volcanic resupply; with D12 hard-zeroed the canonical equatorial-volcanic-province case CANNOT be generated, so claiming E12 covers 'Io zonation' from the current scalar interface is false.

Leading/trailing hemispheric dichotomy (Iapetus archetype) is exogenic — prograde dust deposition on the leading face plus corotating-magnetosphere plasma on the trailing face, amplified by runaway thermal ice migration [OBS/SIM]. This REQUIRES system-graph inputs (orbit sense, dust/ring donors, parent magnetosphere) the per-body scalar pipeline does not carry; the engine cannot produce this province class as currently fed.

The closed-form cold-trap edge latitude phi_ct = f(D1,D3,D2) via radiative-equilibrium T(lat) ~ T_eq*cos(lat)^0.25 is an adequate real-time STAND-IN for actual volatile-transport equilibrium [THEO]; this is the crux assumption — if the true band latitude depends strongly on atmospheric dynamics (Hadley transport, ocean heat transport) the cos^0.25 scaling will misplace bands on thick-atmosphere bodies.

Tidally-locked 'eyeball' province geometry is genuinely radial about the substellar point with concentric terminator rings [OBS for the climate pattern on M-dwarf models / SIM], so a closed-form radial province field about subStellarDir is physically faithful, not just convenient.

An ancient surviving compositional megablock (Xanadu analogue) can be represented as a single large province cell gated on low D11 resurfacing [OBS that Xanadu is old/tectonic + erosion-shaped]; risk: Xanadu's actual origin is tectonic/erosional, not a simple bulk-composition province, so labeling it a T1 'compositional province' may mis-assign it to the wrong tier (it may belong to a tectonic/relief engine, with only its organic overcoat being a true composition signal).

verdicts.claim: Io's ±30° compositional transition (equatorial SO2/sulfur cold-trap province vs poleward red-brown radiation-altered plains) is real and latitude-controlled, BUT depends on D12 tidal heating for volcanic resupply; with D12 hard-zeroed the canonical Io equatorial-volcanic case CANNOT be generated.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by HST/STIS spectroscopic mapping (Trumbo et al. PSJ 2022): white SO2-dominated plains concentrate in the equatorial antijovian region within ~±30deg as a regional cold trap; red-brown plains occur >±30deg from radiation alteration coming from the poles. Latitudinal control is real and OBS-grade. The dependency on tidal heating is also correct: Io's frost is in steady-state because volcanism continuously resupplies SO2; without volcanic resupply (D12=0) there is no fresh SO2 budget to cold-trap, so the engine would mis-generate an Io as a passive frost world. The dossier's self-flagged demotion is accurate and the claim is internally consistent. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Leading/trailing hemispheric dichotomy (Iapetus) is exogenic (prograde dust on leading + corotating-magnetosphere plasma on trailing, amplified by runaway thermal ice migration) and REQUIRES system-graph inputs the per-body scalar pipeline cannot carry; the engine cannot produce this class as currently fed.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: Spencer & Denk (Science 2010) 'Formation of Iapetus' extreme albedo dichotomy by exogenically triggered thermal ice migration' plus Tamayo et al. (2011) on Phoebe-ring/irregular-satellite dust dynamics establish the two-process exogenic trigger + runaway thermal segregation. This genuinely needs orbit sense (prograde apex of motion sets WHICH hemisphere darkens), an external dust donor (Phoebe ring), and parent-magnetosphere corotation geometry — none expressible as a per-body scalar. Note one slight overstatement: the dominant published trigger is dust deposition + slow rotation enabling sublimation; corotating-plasma on the trailing face is a secondary/contributing factor and is more firmly the mechanism for the Galilean moons than for Iapetus specifically. But this does not change the load-bearing conclusion (system-graph required). Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: The closed-form cold-trap edge latitude phi_ct = f(D1,D3,D2) via T(lat) ~ T_eq*cos(lat)^0.25 is an adequate real-time STAND-IN for actual volatile-transport equilibrium; crux risk is that strong atmospheric/ocean heat transport will misplace bands on thick-atmosphere bodies.
verdicts.reasoning: The cos^1/4 law is a correct airless-body radiative-equilibrium scaling (local T scales as insolation^1/4; references confirm T(theta)=T_eq*sin^1/4(theta) measured from pole, equivalently cos^1/4 of latitude). It is a legitimate closed form for airless/thin-atmo bodies. The dossier's CRUX caveat is also correct and, if anything, understated: the eyeball/M-dwarf literature (Hu & Yang PNAS 2014, lobster-pattern results) shows ocean/atmospheric heat transport doesn't merely shift bands by a few degrees — it can qualitatively destroy zonal symmetry (nightside warming, lobster pattern). So cos^0.25 is adequate ONLY in the airless/thin-atmo regime the dossier itself scopes it to, and the engine correctly scales warp/smear with D5. The claim is honestly hedged as 'the crux assumption' and is not overstated. Not refuted, but its validity is conditional on the airless regime — outside it the stand-in fails, which the dossier admits.

verdicts.claim: Tidally-locked 'eyeball' province geometry is genuinely radial about the substellar point with concentric terminator rings, so a closed-form radial province field about subStellarDir is physically faithful, not just convenient.
verdicts.reasoning: Partially overstated. The radial/eyeball pattern is faithful ONLY for the static (no/weak heat transport) case: hot eyeballs (lava substellar pool, e.g. 55 Cnc e) and the idealized frozen-eyeball with a substellar melt pupil. But the cited M-dwarf climate literature (Hu & Yang 2014 PNAS; Yang et al.) shows that with a DYNAMIC ocean or significant atmosphere the open-ocean/warm region is NOT radially symmetric — it becomes a 'lobster' with equatorial tail extending onto the nightside, and nightside warming breaks the concentric-ring geometry. So 'genuinely radial ... concentric terminator rings' is true for the airless/thin-atmo end-state but false for the temperate/thick-atmo cases the dossier wants to cover (where it grows a 'warm pupil' via D5). The radial closed form is convenient and adequate for the static end-states, but calling it physically faithful in general is overstated; the very D5-thick-atmosphere regime the selector targets is where radial symmetry breaks. Marking refuted on the generality claim.

verdicts.claim: An ancient surviving compositional megablock (Xanadu analogue) can be represented as a single large province cell gated on low D11 resurfacing; risk that Xanadu's actual origin is tectonic/erosional so labeling it a T1 compositional province may mis-assign it.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed and the self-flagged risk is correct. Radebaugh et al. (Icarus 2011) and Brossier et al. establish Xanadu's origin as compressional-then-extensional tectonism + fluvial/methane-rain erosion, with composition being water/water-ammonia-ice bedrock under a thin atmospheric-organic overcoat. So Xanadu is fundamentally a TECTONIC/RELIEF feature, not a bulk-compositional province — only its organic overcoat is a true composition signal. Representing it as a T1 compositional province IS a mis-assignment risk, exactly as the dossier states. The claim accurately reports both the representability and the tier-assignment hazard. Not refuted.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The steered-noise approximation is genuinely real-time feasible and does NOT hide an offline sim, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. Each step is bounded and local-per-fragment: (1) the selector is a handful of branchless scalar gates on the driver vector — O(1); (2) the province field is analytic functions of |lat| or substellar angle theta=acos(dot(n,subStellarDir)) with closed-form band edges from the cos^0.25 radiative-equilibrium law — O(1) per fragment, no neighborhood coupling; (3) boundary realism is 2-3 octaves of domain-warped value noise — fixed, bounded cost, standard fragment-shader fare; (4) the optional megablock is one Worley/voronoi cell — bounded. Crucially, the two mechanisms that genuinely DO want simulation — Iapetus runaway thermal-ice-migration and true volatile-transport equilibrium — are replaced by their SETTLED end-state closed forms (a great-circle seam at fixed amplitude; a fixed band latitude). That is the legitimate 'borrow the converged scaling, skip the time-stepping' move, not a concealed relaxation loop. Baking once to a 512x256 equirect LUT is also honestly bounded. The cost class 'steered-noise' is accurate. IMPORTANT HONESTY CAVEAT that keeps this from being a free lunch: the closed-form end-states are only PHYSICALLY faithful in the airless/thin-atmosphere/static regime. For the thick-atmosphere and dynamic-ocean cases (precisely where D5 grows the 'warm pupil' and where the eyeball is supposed to deform), the true end state is NOT the radial/zonal closed form — it is the lobster/nightside-warmed pattern that requires GCM-class dynamics. The approximation stays cheap there, but it is then cheap-AND-wrong (a visual stand-in), not cheap-and-faithful. So: real-time feasible = yes, unconditionally; 'physically faithful closed form' = only in the airless regime. The dossier is mostly honest about this (it flags the cos^0.25 crux and the dropped-driver demotions D12/system-graph), which is why the realism verdict is true rather than a hidden-sim refutation. The selector also silently zeroes two entire province classes (dichotomy via unsupplied system-graph, Io-volcanic via hard-zeroed D12), so the engine is real-time but coverage-incomplete by construction.

verify.notes: Net: 4 of 5 load-bearing claims survive (the planetary-science groundings — Io latitudinal frost/radiation banding, Iapetus exogenic dichotomy, Xanadu tectonic-not-compositional origin, and the cos^1/4 airless radiative-equilibrium scaling — are all OBS/THEO-confirmed via primary literature). The one refutation is the eyeball claim's GENERALITY: 'genuinely radial about the substellar point ... physically faithful' is true only for the static/airless end-state; with a dynamic ocean or thick atmosphere (the D5-driven 'warm pupil' regime the selector explicitly targets) the real pattern is the non-radial 'lobster' with nightside warming (Hu & Yang 2014 PNAS; lobster-ocean results), so the closed-form radial field is convenient-but-not-faithful exactly where the engine most wants to deform it. The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time (no hidden sim/relaxation/global solve) — its end-state-closed-form substitutions for runaway thermal migration and volatile-transport equilibrium are the legitimate borrow-the-scaling pattern. The honest limits, several of which the dossier self-flags: (a) it is faithful only in the airless/thin-atmo regime; (b) D12 hard-zeroing means the canonical Io equatorial-volcanic province cannot be generated; (c) unsupplied system-graph means leading/trailing dichotomy cannot be placed at all. These are coverage gaps, not cost violations. The dossier is unusually self-critical (it pre-states most of its own demotions in typeDemotionNote and loadBearingClaims), which is why most claims hold up under adversarial check.

engine.name: Tidal / orbital-coupling
engine.brief: D7/D12 + orbit(eccentricity,libration) + neighbors -> rotating stress-tensor field + tidal-heat-flux field. (D12 is hard-zeroed in the current game; flag the under-supply.)

dossier.mechanism: Tidal/orbital coupling. A satellite or close-in planet on a non-zero-eccentricity (or librating / obliquity-nonzero) orbit feels a time-varying gravitational potential from its primary. Because orbital distance and apparent sub-primary longitude oscillate each orbit (the "diurnal" tide), the tidal bulge flexes. Two coupled products result. (1) HEAT: anelastic friction (the imaginary part of the complex Love number, Im(k2)) dissipates orbital/rotational energy as interior heat. Globally H scales as H ~ Im(k2)*G*M_primary^2*R^5*n*e^2/a^6, i.e. H ∝ R^5 * e^2 * a^(-15/2). At body scale this spans the Io regime (>2 W/m^2 surface flux, runaway resurfacing) down to negligible. Crucially the heat is NOT uniform: for eccentricity tides on a synchronous body, dissipation in a deep solid mantle/shell peaks at the POLES, while dissipation in a thin soft asthenosphere or a liquid ocean peaks at the EQUATOR, with degree-2/degree-4 longitudinal structure (Beuthe 2013). (2) STRESS: the same flexing produces a rotating, time-varying surface stress tensor whose diurnal principal stresses are closed-form in the tidal Love numbers h2, l2 (magnitudes ~ C*f(δ to bulge), C ∝ h2*M*μ*(1+ν)/(ρ*a^3)). When the tensile component exceeds ice/rock strength a crack opens perpendicular to maximum tension; because the stress field ROTATES over the orbit the crack curves, arrests when stress falls below the propagation threshold, then re-initiates at a cusp in a new direction — generating cycloidal lineaments at ~3 km/hr apparent growth. Non-synchronous rotation (NSR) adds a slowly-accumulating background stress that rotates the whole pattern; physical libration and obliquity add oscillating components. For tide-locked lava worlds the coupling instead pins a permanent sub-stellar bulge and a day/night thermal asymmetry that fixes sub-stellar magma-pool / terminator volcanism placement.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Selects synchronous (eyeball/permanent-bulge) vs free-rotating regime; gates which stress family (diurnal-only vs diurnal+NSR) and whether heat/volcanism is sub-stellar-anchored.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: HARD-ZEROED in current game pipeline. This is the engine's primary heat magnitude input — with it dead, all tidal-heat flux, cryovolcanism, Io-grade resurfacing, and tidal-stress cracking are forced off. The single most load-bearing under-supply for E3.

inputs.name: orbital eccentricity e
inputs.note: Heat ∝ e^2 and diurnal stress amplitude ∝ e. A per-body scalar interface that carries no orbit element cannot supply e; it is currently folded (if at all) into D12 rather than exposed. Without e the engine cannot distinguish a circular-orbit dead moon from an Io.

inputs.name: physical libration amplitude
inputs.note: Adds an oscillating stress component that measurably reshapes cycloid fits; a scalar driver vector cannot carry it.

inputs.name: semi-major axis a / mean motion n
inputs.note: Heat ∝ a^(-15/2); needed to convert resonance/orbit into magnitude. Not in the 16 scalars.

inputs.name: resonance / neighbor graph (e.g. Laplace 1:2:4)
inputs.note: Resonances PUMP and MAINTAIN the eccentricity that drives everything (Io–Europa–Ganymede). L0 computes a system graph but does NOT expose it per-body, so the engine cannot know an orbit's e is forced rather than damped — it cannot tell a resonance-locked active moon from a relaxed one.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt (obliquity)
inputs.note: Obliquity adds an annual stress term and shifts cycloid azimuths; available as a scalar.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: Sets interior rigidity/structure layering (solid mantle vs differentiated), which selects polar-vs-equatorial heat pattern; usable as a proxy for the Love-number/dissipation-layer choice.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Scales R and surface gravity in the H∝R^5 term and in crack/flexure response.

inputs.name: interior layering / Love numbers (h2, l2, Im(k2))
inputs.note: Stress amplitudes and heat depend on the complex Love numbers, which come from an interior-structure model (E? differentiation engine). A scalar cannot carry a depth-dependent rheology; currently must be approximated from D9/D14/D2.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Decides whether the resurfacing medium is silicate lava (Io) or cryomagma/water ice (Europa/Enceladus) for the same heat flux.

outputs.name: tidalHeatFlux field
outputs.note: Per-surface-point heat flux (W/m^2) as a spherical-harmonic pattern: polar-max for deep-mantle dissipation, equatorial-max (degree-2/4) for thin-asthenosphere/ocean dissipation. Drives resurfacing budget and emissive glow.

outputs.name: rotating tidal stress tensor field
outputs.note: Time-phased 2x2 surface stress tensor (σθθ, σφφ, σθφ) over one orbit; principal magnitudes + azimuths. Consumed to seed fracture/cycloid features and to bias terrain age.

outputs.name: cycloidal lineaments
outputs.note: Curved-arc-with-cusps crack chains traced by following max-tension azimuth through the rotating stress field with a tensile-failure + propagation-arrest threshold.

outputs.name: global lineament/double-ridge fabric
outputs.note: Conjugate fracture sets and NSR-rotated lineaments expressing the diurnal+NSR stress history.

outputs.name: sub-stellar magma pool / terminator volcanism placement
outputs.note: For tide-locked lava worlds: dayside sub-stellar melt anchor and terminator-ring upwelling/downwelling positions.

outputs.name: resurfacing-age modifier
outputs.note: Multiplier into D11/D16: high tidal flux youthens terrain (suppresses crater retention) where flux is high — couples E3 to the cratering engine as an editor.

cheapApprox.description: Two real-time-feasible halves, both closed-form/baked — no offline sim needed. (A) HEAT FIELD: compute scalar global flux once from the scaling law H ∝ Im(k2)*R^5*e^2*a^(-15/2) (clamp to an Io ceiling); choose ONE of two analytic spherical-harmonic patterns by a rigidity/layer switch (from D9/D2): polar-peaked P2(cosθ)-style for solid-mantle dissipation, or equatorial degree-2/degree-4 pattern for soft-asthenosphere/ocean. Evaluate the harmonic in the shader for per-texel flux; feed it to emissive glow + a resurfacing-age multiplier. This is pure closed-form. (B) STRESS / CYCLOIDS: the diurnal surface stress tensor has a known closed-form in orbital phase and position (the Wahr/Hoppa-style h2,l2 expressions). Bake an N-frame (e.g. 16-step orbit) stress-tensor atlas, OR evaluate the analytic tensor on the fly. Cycloids are then traced by a CHEAP relaxation/marching pass done ONCE at bake: seed points, step along the local max-tension azimuth while tensile stress > strength, arrest when it drops, advance orbital phase to re-initiate a cusp (the published model reproduces real cycloids this way; growth ~3 km/hr sets arc length). Stamp the resulting polylines as a normal/displacement decal layer. NSR is a slow azimuthal rotation offset applied to the whole field; libration/obliquity are extra additive analytic terms. Nothing requires time-stepping the interior — the interior response is the analytic Love-number transfer function, evaluated, not simulated. The ONLY part that wants offline care is choosing Im(k2)/Love numbers from interior structure, which we approximate from D9/D14/D2 rather than solving a viscoelastic profile.

epochBehavior.note: Runs per-epoch as an EDITOR over upstream terrain. Its heat field youthens/resurfaces terrain produced by earlier engines (e.g. cryolava or silicate lava floods existing impact craters and old crust where flux is high, mirroring D11/D16 resurfacing), and its stress field stamps cycloid/lineament fracture decals onto the existing crust. On a circular, non-resonant, or D12-zeroed body it is effectively a no-op. For lava worlds it also acts once to anchor the permanent sub-stellar melt feature.

featureMap: cycloidal lineaments (Europa-type curved cusped cracks)
global lineament / double-ridge fracture fabric
cryovolcanic / tiger-stripe resurfacing zones (Enceladus-type)
Io-grade silicate volcanic resurfacing & emissive hot regions
tidally-youthened (crater-poor) terrain patches
sub-stellar magma pool and terminator volcanism on tide-locked lava worlds
NSR-rotated / conjugate fracture sets
dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline very likely hard-codes tidal outcomes by discrete body 'type' rather than deriving them from drivers/orbit. Symptoms to expect: (1) Io/Europa/Enceladus behavior keyed to a named moon-type or a 'has cryovolcanism' boolean instead of computing flux from e, a, Im(k2); (2) cycloids stamped as a canned texture for 'ice moon' rather than traced from the rotating stress field; (3) the polar-vs-equatorial heat pattern picked by type instead of by the rigidity/layer switch (D9/D2); (4) silicate-vs-cryo medium chosen by type label rather than by D2 volatileFraction at a given flux; (5) lava-world sub-stellar pool gated on a 'lava planet' flag rather than on D7 tidalLock + D1 tempEq + dayside melt threshold. All of these should fall out of (D7, D12, e, a, D9, D2, D14) once D12 and the orbit elements are actually supplied.
loadBearingClaims: The cycloid/lineament fracture pattern can be generated in real time by a once-at-bake closed-form trace through an analytic rotating stress tensor (no viscoelastic FE simulation). RISK: published cycloid fits include NSR, libration, and obliquity terms and a non-trivial failure/propagation-threshold; a naive trace may produce plausible-but-wrong arc curvature/cusp spacing.

The H ∝ R^5 * e^2 * a^(-15/2) constant-Q scaling is adequate to PLACE heat magnitude across the catalog. RISK: real dissipation depends on the frequency-dependent Im(k2)/Q of the interior rheology; constant-Q can be order-of-magnitude wrong for resonant/near-melt bodies and ignores feedback where heating lowers viscosity and raises dissipation.

The polar-vs-equatorial heat-pattern dichotomy (deep-mantle polar-max vs soft-layer/ocean equatorial-max, Beuthe 2013) is the correct first-order spatial law and can be reduced to a single layer switch from D9/D2. RISK: the real pattern carries significant degree-4 and longitudinal structure and depends on layer thickness, which a binary switch flattens.

E3's entire visible output is currently dead because D12 is hard-zeroed AND the orbit elements (e, a, resonance graph) are not exposed by the scalar L0 interface — so no body can express tidal heat or tidal cracking until the interface carries an orbit. This is an interface-level under-supply, not a tuning issue.

For tide-locked lava worlds the permanent sub-stellar magma pool and terminator up/downwelling placement is governed by thermal day/night asymmetry, and modeled circulation actually predicts NIGHTSIDE downwellings / terminator features rather than a simple sub-stellar-only melt — so a sub-stellar-glow-only approximation may misplace the volcanism.

verdicts.claim: Cycloid/lineament fracture pattern can be generated in real time by a once-at-bake closed-form trace through an analytic rotating stress tensor (no viscoelastic FE simulation).
verdicts.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed: Hoppa/Greenberg (2001) and Wahr et al. (2009, the dossier's S0019103508003795 citation) give the diurnal surface stress tensor in CLOSED FORM from Love numbers h2,l2, evaluated per surface point with no FE/viscoelastic time-stepping. The cycloid generation IS exactly the published procedure: seed, march along max-tension azimuth while tensile stress > threshold, arrest below it, advance orbital phase to cusp. This is a 1D curve-marching pass over a closed-form field, not a global solve. Real cusp/growth (~3 km/hr, 40-120 kPa thresholds) match published numbers. The dossier's STATED RISK is also correct and well-grounded: Rhoden et al. and the obliquity-cycloid literature show obliquity+physical-libration is the best-supported model (obliquities 0.32-1.35 deg, libration 0.72-2.44 deg), and NSR improves fits — so a naive diurnal-only trace produces plausible-but-wrong curvature/cusp spacing. The dossier explicitly flags this and includes the additive libration/obliquity/NSR terms in its method, so the claim is honest. Not refuted; the engineering claim holds and the risk is disclosed accurately.

verdicts.claim: H proportional to R^5 * e^2 * a^(-15/2) constant-Q scaling is adequate to PLACE heat magnitude across the catalog.
verdicts.reasoning: The scaling law is correct and standard: P = (21/2) Im(k2) G^(3/2) M^(5/2) R^5 e^2 / a^(15/2), confirmed across multiple sources (Wikipedia, arXiv exoplanet tidal-heating papers, Grokipedia). For PLACING relative magnitude across a catalog (the stated, limited purpose), it is adequate. The dossier's RISK is fully confirmed by the rheology literature (Renaud & Henning Andrade/Sundberg-Cooper models; 'impact of rheology model choices on tidal heating' 2024; frequency-dependent Q work): constant-Q can be order-of-magnitude wrong for resonant/near-melt bodies and ignores the viscosity-temperature feedback (heating lowers viscosity, raises dissipation) that drives runaway/Io. The claim is scoped to 'place,' not 'predict precisely,' and the dossier flags the exact limitation. Not refuted; the scaling is real and the caveat is accurate.

verdicts.claim: Polar-vs-equatorial heat-pattern dichotomy (deep-mantle polar-max vs soft-layer/ocean equatorial-max, Beuthe 2013) is the correct first-order spatial law and can be reduced to a single layer switch from D9/D2.
verdicts.reasoning: Beuthe (2013) confirmed directly (arXiv 1212.4630, Icarus): eccentricity-tide dissipation in a solid mantle around a liquid core peaks at the POLES; ocean/soft-layer dissipation peaks at the EQUATOR; obliquity forcing shifts the pattern. The first-order dichotomy is real. The dossier's RISK is also correct and confirmed by Beuthe himself and Lemasquerier 2023 (Europa ocean translation paper): the real pattern carries significant degree-4 and longitudinal (order-2) structure and depends on layer thickness, which a binary switch flattens. The claim is scoped as 'first-order' and the over-simplification is explicitly flagged. Not refuted — the first-order law is correctly attributed; the binary-switch reduction is acknowledged as lossy.

verdicts.claim: E3's entire visible output is currently dead because D12 is hard-zeroed AND orbit elements (e, a, resonance graph) are not exposed by the scalar L0 interface — an interface-level under-supply, not a tuning issue.
verdicts.reasoning: This is an internal claim about the game pipeline's own interface, not independently web-verifiable. Physically it is coherent and consistent: heat scales as e^2 and stress amplitude as e, so with e unavailable and D12 zeroed, all tidal heat, cryovolcanism, and stress cracking are necessarily off — a structural/interface gap, not a parameter-tuning problem. The reasoning (a per-body scalar vector cannot carry orbit elements e, a, n, resonance membership) is internally sound. Marked medium confidence because I cannot inspect the actual L0 driver schema; accepting the dossier's self-report of its own architecture. The physics chain it rests on is correct.

verdicts.claim: For tide-locked lava worlds, a sub-stellar-glow-only approximation may misplace volcanism because modeled circulation predicts nightside downwellings / terminator features rather than simple sub-stellar-only melt.
verdicts.reasoning: Strongly confirmed. 55 Cnc e thermal phase curves put the hottest point shifted ~41+/-12 deg EAST of substellar (not at substellar). Interior-dynamics modeling (Meier et al. 2023, arXiv 2308.00592) shows dayside super-plumes that can migrate tens of degrees toward the terminator, with cold nightside descent. K2-141 b modeling (arXiv 2603.02408) explicitly predicts nightside volcanism. GCMs show eastward heat advection and terminator cloud/upwelling structure. A naive sub-stellar-only emissive glow would indeed misplace the melt anchor and miss terminator/nightside features. The dossier's caveat is well-grounded and, if anything, conservative. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Diurnal surface stress tensor is closed-form in orbital phase and position (Wahr/Hoppa-style h2,l2 expressions) — can be evaluated on-the-fly or baked to a 16-frame atlas, no interior time-stepping.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: Wahr et al. (2009, S0019103508003795) derives surface stress from gravitational potential theory in closed form, with h2 and l2 specifiable independently. The interior response enters only as the Love-number transfer function (evaluated, not simulated). Per-point analytic evaluation -> a 16-step orbital atlas is trivially within a WebGL budget. No per-pixel global solve, no relaxation. Not refuted.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time feasible and does NOT hide an offline sim, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. HEAT HALF (A): one scalar global flux from the closed-form scaling law (a handful of arithmetic ops), times one of two analytic spherical-harmonic patterns evaluated per-texel in the shader. Pure closed-form, O(1) per pixel. No iteration. STRESS HALF (B): the Wahr/Hoppa diurnal stress tensor is closed-form in (phase, lat, lon) from Love numbers h2,l2 — evaluated on the fly or baked to a 16-frame atlas. Confirmed analytic, no FE/viscoelastic time-stepping; the interior is only the Love-number transfer function (evaluated, not simulated). The one iterative-looking part — the cycloid trace — is honestly disclosed as a ONCE-AT-BAKE pass and is a 1D curve-march (seed, step along local max-tension azimuth, arrest below threshold, advance phase to cusp), NOT a global relaxation: it is bounded by arc length / number of seed points, runs offline at bake, and stamps polyline decals. That is exactly how the published Hoppa/Rhoden cycloid models generate the curves, so it is faithful, not a shortcut that loses correctness. NSR/libration/obliquity are additive analytic terms, not extra solves. The only genuinely offline-leaning input — choosing Im(k2)/Love numbers from interior structure — is explicitly acknowledged and approximated from D9/D14/D2 rather than solving a viscoelastic profile; the dossier is candid that this is the soft spot. The main correctness caveats (constant-Q can be order-of-magnitude off near melt/resonance; binary polar-vs-equatorial switch flattens real degree-4/longitudinal structure; diurnal-only trace gets cusp geometry wrong without libration/obliquity; sub-stellar-only glow misplaces lava-world volcanism) are all FLAGGED in the dossier's own loadBearingClaims, so it does not oversell. Verdict: a legitimately cheap, closed-form/baked engine with honestly-scoped fidelity limits.

verify.notes: All six load-bearing claims survived adversarial checking — none refuted. The dossier is unusually disciplined: every place where the cheap approximation diverges from real physics (constant-Q error near melt/resonance, degree-4/longitudinal heat structure beyond the binary switch, cycloid curvature needing obliquity+libration, lava-world volcanism not sub-stellar-only) is explicitly disclosed as a RISK rather than buried. Key external confirmations: scaling law P proportional to R^5 e^2 a^-15/2 with Im(k2) (standard); Beuthe 2013 polar-vs-equatorial dichotomy (arXiv 1212.4630); Wahr et al. 2009 closed-form stress (S0019103508003795); Hoppa/Greenberg + Rhoden cycloid trace with 40-120 kPa thresholds and ~3 km/hr growth; 55 Cnc e / K2-141 b modeling showing eastward hotspot shift, terminator super-plumes, and nightside volcanism. The one unverifiable claim (D12 hard-zeroed + orbit elements absent from the L0 scalar interface) is an internal-architecture self-report I accepted at medium confidence; its underlying physics chain (e^2 heat, e stress) is sound. The cheap approximation is the strongest part: no hidden offline sim, no unbounded relaxation, no per-pixel global solve — the only iterative step (cycloid marching) is correctly scoped as a bounded once-at-bake 1D trace, and the only offline-leaning input (Love numbers from rheology) is openly flagged as approximated. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_heating; arxiv.org/pdf/1212.4630; sciencedirect S0019103508003795, S0019103506003058, S0019103507003594; arxiv.org/abs/2308.00592; arxiv.org/pdf/2603.02408; pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2423473122; sciencedirect S001910352400085X (rheology choices); sciencedirect S0019103513002947 (lineament azimuths obliquity/NSR)."}

engine.name: Magnetosphere / radiation
engine.brief: D13(+field topology) + neighbors + D4 -> charged-particle flux mask + field-topology map + aurora/airglow.

dossier.mechanism: A planetary dipole (and its higher-order topology) inflates a magnetospheric cavity in the stellar wind. The standoff/magnetopause distance is set by pressure balance between magnetic pressure B^2/2mu0 (falling as r^-3 for a dipole) and stellar-wind dynamic pressure P_sw=rho*v^2, giving R_mp ~ (M^2/P_sw)^(1/6) where M is the magnetic moment. Inside the cavity, charged particles execute gyration + bounce + drift motion along closed field lines, forming trapped radiation belts; near the poles, field lines OPEN to the wind, defining a polar cap and an auroral OVAL at the open/closed boundary (colatitude set roughly by sqrt(R_planet/R_mp) for a dipole). Precipitating particles deposit energy at characteristic altitudes, exciting atmospheric species that fluoresce: atomic O green (557.7 nm, ~100-150 km), atomic O red (630 nm, >200-300 km, long metastable lifetime), molecular N2/N2+ blue/violet/red (lower border, ~120 km). Where the field is weak/absent, the wind erodes the atmosphere directly (sputtering, ion pickup, polar-cap ion outflow); a magnetic field is NOT a clean shield -- open polar caps can ENHANCE loss. Around giants, an orbiting volcanic moon (Io-type, tidal-heating-driven) injects a neutral cloud that ionizes into a plasma torus, which both loads the magnetosphere and sputter-weathers nearby moon surfaces and paints satellite-footprint aurorae on the host. Color/altitude depend on atmospheric composition and density, so the same field topology produces different aurorae on different bodies.

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: Master gate: field strength/presence. Scalar OK as a magnitude proxy, but it is a derived composite (ironFraction x rotation) and a scalar cannot carry field TOPOLOGY (dipole vs multipole, tilt, offset) which controls oval shape and asymmetry.

inputs.name: field topology / dipole tilt & offset
inputs.note: Needed for non-dipolar/ tilted ovals (cf. Uranus/Neptune offset-tilted fields, and Earth excursions producing globally-distributed low-latitude aurorae). No scalar or current field carries an axis/multipole descriptor.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: Core iron -> dynamo strength; upstream of D13. Scalar fine.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Dynamo + rotational driving of magnetosphere (corotation, plasma sheet); scalar fine as magnitude.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Slow/locked rotation -> asymmetric ionospheric conductance and day/night auroral asymmetry; scalar (0..1) fine.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Sets aurora EMISSION SPECIES/COLOR (O green/red vs N blue vs CO2/other). Scalar composition index is lossy -- color needs a species mix, but a categorical/low-dim proxy is workable.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Sets emission ALTITUDE/brightness and which forbidden lines survive (red O needs thin high air). Scalar fine.

inputs.name: D6 atmoRetention
inputs.note: Engine FEEDS this: polar-cap open area modulates escape. Consumed downstream; scalar fine.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Drives Io-type volcanic moon outgassing that feeds a plasma torus. HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline, so the entire torus/satellite-weathering pathway is dead.

inputs.name: stellar wind dynamic pressure (rho, v) & orbital distance
inputs.note: Other half of the standoff pressure balance and of erosion rate; depends on star type/age and orbit. Not exposed per-body today.

inputs.name: system graph: host giant, sibling moons, resonances, rings
inputs.note: Needed to know if THIS body is a torus source, a torus victim (sputter-weathered moon), or hosts a satellite-footprint aurora. L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Scale-sets exobase/scale height feeding emission-altitude band; scalar fine.

outputs.name: chargedParticleFluxMask
outputs.note: Surface/exobase scalar of precipitating-particle dose: high in auroral oval + polar cap, low under closed dayside; for unmagnetized bodies a broad wind/cosmic-ray dose with substellar/leading-hemisphere bias.

outputs.name: fieldTopologyMap
outputs.note: Direction/openness field: open (polar cap), closed (mid/low lat), oval boundary; encodes dipole axis tilt/offset. Feeds aurora placement and ion-escape mask.

outputs.name: auroralOval
outputs.note: Glowing ring(s) at the open/closed boundary; colatitude ~ asin(sqrt(Rp/Rmp)); color from D4, altitude/brightness from D5/D14; widens & moves equatorward when field weak or wind strong.

outputs.name: polarCapEscapeMask
outputs.note: Open-field area fraction -> ion-outflow / volatile-loss weighting handed to D6/atmosphere engine (magnetized planets can lose MORE via cusps).

outputs.name: airglow/nightglow
outputs.note: Faint diffuse global chemiluminescent limb glow independent of field (O/N recombination); always-on dim band even with no aurora.

outputs.name: plasmaTorus & satelliteFootprint
outputs.note: For giants with an Io-type moon: orbital plasma torus + bright auroral footprint spot/tail on the host; only emitted when D12 + system-graph moon present.

outputs.name: radiationWeatheringMask
outputs.note: Sputter/irradiation darkening + chemistry mask on moons/airless bodies embedded in a magnetosphere or torus (leading/trailing hemisphere asymmetry).
