Terminator/substellar glow asymmetry on tidally locked worlds

cheapApprox.description: Everything is analytic over the unit sphere -- no offline sim. (1) STANDOFF: Rmp = k*(M^2/Psw)^(1/6) with M from D9*D8 (proxy for D13) and Psw from star/orbit (default constant if system-graph absent). (2) OVAL PLACEMENT: auroral colatitude theta_a = asin(sqrt(Rp/Rmp)) about the magnetic axis (axis from topology input, default = spin axis). In the fragment shader compute magnetic latitude lambda_m from the surface normal vs magnetic axis; flux mask = smoothstep band centered at (90-theta_a) for the oval PLUS a filled cap poleward of it, mirrored both poles, scaled by D13. Add 1-2 octaves of curl/flow noise advected in magnetic-longitude to give the oval its rayed, curtained shimmer (animated by time). (3) COLOR: layered by sampled altitude band -> low N2 blue/violet, mid O green (557.7), high O red (630), with weights from D4 species proxy and D5 density (thin air unlocks red). (4) AIRGLOW: constant faint additive limb term (Fresnel/rim) modulated by D5, independent of D13. (5) WEAK/NO FIELD: as D13->0, theta_a->90 so the band collapses to a global low-latitude wash + substellar/leading-hemisphere bias from wind direction -- naturally reproduces 'no oval, diffuse glow.' (6) TORUS/FOOTPRINT/WEATHERING: gated by D12>0 AND a system-graph moon flag; torus = a billboarded/ring emissive in orbit space, footprint = an extra bright spot injected into the host flux mask at the moon's magnetic-conjugate longitude; moon weathering = a baked leading/trailing hemisphere darkening ramp. All per-pixel, single pass, a handful of noise taps -- fits a real-time WebGL budget.

epochBehavior.note: Primary outputs (oval, airglow, flux mask) are a thin emissive/overlay PASS composited over whatever the terrain/atmosphere engines produced -- it edits the rendered body by adding glow + a dose mask, not new geometry. Field/standoff parameters can be solved ONCE per body (quasi-static dipole). The radiationWeatheringMask is a genuine editor on an UPSTREAM engine's output: it darkens/chemically alters an existing moon-surface albedo/texture (analogous to lava flooding a crater). Aurora animation is per-frame shader time, not per-epoch.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline almost certainly switches aurorae on/off by a discrete 'has magnetic field' / planet-type flag (e.g. 'gas giant gets aurora, rocky doesn't') and likely fixes aurora color to Earth green. Both should be DERIVED: oval geometry from Rmp(M,Psw) and theta_a (continuous, so weak fields give a wide low-latitude wash rather than a binary present/absent oval), and color from D4 species + D5 density (a CO2 or carbon-planet atmosphere should NOT glow Earth-green). The plasma-torus/satellite-footprint feature is presumably a hard-coded 'Jupiter-like' decoration; it should instead fire whenever D12>0 and the system graph reports a close volcanic moon, for ANY giant. Polar caps as escape zones are likely cosmetic-only; they should feed D6 retention as a continuous open-area term (with the counterintuitive sign: more open cap = MORE loss).
loadBearingClaims: The R_mp ~ (M^2/P_sw)^(1/6) sixth-root pressure-balance scaling is the right closed form and is robust enough to PLACE the magnetopause from a scalar field proxy (real data show the relation is noisier/less straightforward than the clean power law -- Samsonov 2020 -- but it is adequate for procedural placement).

Auroral colatitude theta_a = asin(sqrt(Rp/Rmp)) correctly maps field strength -> oval radius for a dipole; the exact constant and the open-flux geometry are approximations and break for strongly non-dipolar or tilted fields.

A magnetic field does NOT simply shield the atmosphere; magnetized planets can lose MORE volatiles through open polar caps/cusps (Egan/Blackman-style result) -- so the polarCapEscapeMask feeding D6 must use the counterintuitive sign, which is easy to get backwards.

Aurora color is genuinely set by atmospheric species + altitude (O 557.7 green / O 630 red / N2 blue), so a scalar D4 is lossy; a non-O2/N2 atmosphere should produce a non-Earth palette, and hard-coding green is wrong.

The entire plasma-torus / satellite-footprint / moon-radiation-weathering pathway depends on D12 tidalHeating, which is HARD-ZEROED in the current pipeline AND on a system graph that L0 does not expose per-body -- so this whole visible feature class is currently unreachable, not merely approximated.

verdicts.claim: Magnetopause standoff R_mp ~ (M^2/P_sw)^(1/6) sixth-root pressure-balance scaling is the right closed form, adequate for procedural placement (noisier in reality per Samsonov 2020).
verdicts.reasoning: Independently confirmed. Pressure balance between dipole magnetic pressure (B^2/2mu0, falling as r^-6 for a dipole so the algebra yields the 1/6 root on M^2/P) and solar-wind dynamic pressure gives R ~ P_d^(-1/6) regardless of IMF orientation (standard result; arXiv:1110.5209). The dossier is also CORRECT and appropriately humble that real data deviate: observed exponents are 5-6.6 not exactly 6 (Shue 1998 N=6.6, Lin 2010 N=5.26, Dusik 2010 N=4.8, MHD N=5.2), and Samsonov 2020 (the cited GRL) explicitly questions how straightforward the relation is. For PROCEDURAL placement the clean power law is fine. Claim stands as written including its hedge.

verdicts.claim: Auroral colatitude theta_a = asin(sqrt(Rp/Rmp)) maps field strength to oval radius for a dipole; constant/geometry are approximations that break for strongly non-dipolar/tilted fields.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. The open/closed boundary colatitude for an aligned dipole is alpha_0 = arcsin( (Rp/r_m)^(1/2) ), exactly the dossier form (arXiv:1503.05711 on close-in exoplanet environments; standard last-closed-field-line result). Polar-cap open-area fraction = 1 - cos(alpha_0), consistent with the polarCapEscapeMask design. The dossier correctly flags that this is a dipole approximation that breaks for tilted/multipolar fields. Stands.

verdicts.claim: A magnetic field does NOT simply shield the atmosphere; magnetized planets can lose MORE volatiles through open polar caps/cusps; polarCapEscapeMask must use the counterintuitive sign (more open cap = MORE loss).
verdicts.reasoning: Directionally confirmed but the dossier OVERSIMPLIFIES the sign as monotonic. The physics (Egan, Jarvinen, Ma & Brain 2019 MNRAS; Gunell et al. 2018 A&A 'Why an intrinsic magnetic field does not protect a planet against atmospheric escape') is that ion escape is NON-MONOTONIC in field strength: there is a field value of MAXIMUM outflow. Weak fields ENHANCE escape (the dossier's point is right here); but beyond the peak, stronger fields REDUCE escape via closed-field-line trapping. So 'a B-field is not a clean shield' and 'open caps enhance loss' are correct, and getting the weak-field sign backwards is indeed the easy mistake to make. But 'more open cap = MORE loss' as a flat continuous sign is only valid on the rising branch. Not refuted (the core, surprising claim is sound and well-sourced), but the implementation note should encode the peak/turnover, not a pure monotonic ramp. Flagging as a quality caveat rather than a refutation.

verdicts.claim: Aurora color is set by atmospheric species + altitude (O 557.7 green / O 630 red / N2 blue); scalar D4 is lossy; non-O2/N2 atmospheres need a non-Earth palette; hard-coding green is wrong.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed in detail. Green = atomic O 1S->1D 557.7 nm (~100-150/400 km); red = atomic O 1D->3P 630 nm, restricted to >~300 km because at lower altitude collisional quenching deactivates the long-lived metastable before it radiates (the dossier's 'thin high air unlocks red' is exactly right); blue/violet from N2+ (428 nm) and N2 at lower border. Color is genuinely composition- and altitude-dependent, so a scalar composition index is lossy and Earth-green is not universal. Stands.

verdicts.claim: The plasma-torus / satellite-footprint / moon-radiation-weathering pathway depends on D12 tidalHeating (HARD-ZEROED) and a system graph L0 does not expose per-body, so the whole feature class is currently unreachable.
verdicts.reasoning: The PHYSICS is fully confirmed: tidal heating (Laplace resonance Io-Europa-Ganymede) drives Io volcanism -> neutral cloud -> ionized Io plasma torus (~1 ton/s SO2) -> Io flux tube produces the auroral footprint at the magnetic-conjugate point; torus ions sputter-weather nearby surfaces (Bagenal 2020/2024; A&A 2025 Juno footprint). The conjugate-longitude footprint and leading/trailing weathering asymmetry are real, closed-form-mappable phenomena. The pipeline-state claims (D12 hard-zeroed; system graph not exposed per-body) are internal assertions about the codebase I cannot independently verify from public sources -- taken at face value they make the feature class unreachable, which is a self-consistent and plausible statement. Marked medium confidence because the unreachability is an unverifiable internal claim, not because the physics is wrong.

verdicts.claim: Field topology (dipole tilt/offset, multipole) cannot be carried by a scalar D13; needed for tilted/offset ovals (Uranus/Neptune) and low-latitude excursion aurorae.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Uranus far-field ~ offset dipole tilted ~60deg from spin axis; Neptune ~ offset-tilted dipole displaced ~0.55 R_N, inclined ~47deg; both have extraordinarily large non-dipolar (multipole, AH5 fifth-order) components within a few planetary radii that directly shape the UV aurora distribution. A scalar magnitude cannot encode an axis, offset, or multipole order, so oval shape/asymmetry is genuinely under-supplied by D13 alone. The under-supplied input flags are physically justified.

verdicts.claim: Type-demotion: aurora present/absent and color should be DERIVED (continuous theta_a, color from D4/D5) rather than a binary planet-type flag with fixed green.
verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the confirmed physics: theta_a(Rmp) is continuous, so weak fields legitimately give a wide low-latitude wash rather than a binary oval, and color genuinely tracks species+altitude. The recommendation to derive rather than gate is sound. This is a design-quality assertion, not a falsifiable physics claim, and it aligns with everything verified above.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The 'closed-form' label is honest: I find NO hidden offline sim, NO unbounded iterative relaxation, and NO per-pixel global solve. Step-by-step: (1) Standoff R_mp = k*(M^2/Psw)^(1/6) is O(1) algebra solved ONCE per body (correctly tagged quasi-static). (2) Oval placement in the fragment shader is the genuinely load-bearing per-pixel step and it is purely local: magnetic latitude = acos(dot(surfaceNormal, magAxis)) -- a handful of ALU ops, NO neighbor sampling, NO field-line integration -- fed into a smoothstep band + poleward cap. This is the standard cheap-aurora technique and it does fit a real-time WebGL budget. (3) Altitude-banded color is a per-pixel blend (note: there is no true altitude in a thin emissive shell, so 'sampled altitude band' is a faked radial proxy/layered shells -- a fidelity fudge, not a cost problem). (4) Fresnel/rim airglow is one dot product. (5) Weak-field limit is the SAME formula (theta_a->90), free. (6) Torus = billboard/emissive ring; footprint = a single Gaussian bright spot injected at the closed-form magnetic-conjugate longitude; moon weathering = a BAKED leading/trailing ramp -- all cheap, gated, no iteration. The shimmer is explicitly '1-2 octaves of curl/flow noise' = a few taps. The ONE real limitation, which the dossier itself discloses: the analytic theta_a band assumes a centered or OFFSET dipole; it does NOT field-line-trace, so it cannot reproduce a TRUE inner multipole (Uranus/Neptune AH5). The offset-tilted-dipole far-field case IS still closed-form (shift axis origin), so the approximation covers the standard textbook regime and honestly flags where it breaks. Within its stated scope it is real-time feasible, not a concealed solve.

verify.notes: Dossier survives adversarial review. All seven load-bearing physics claims independently confirmed against current literature; none refuted. The cheap approximation is genuinely closed-form/per-pixel and fits a WebGL budget with no hidden iteration or global coupling. Two QUALITY caveats (not refutations) worth surfacing to the implementer: (1) The polar-cap escape sign is non-monotonic in reality (Egan 2019 / Gunell 2018): weak field ENHANCES loss but past a peak stronger field SUPPRESSES it via closed-line trapping. The dossier's 'more open cap = MORE loss' is right on the rising branch but a pure monotonic ramp will mis-model strong-field bodies; encode the turnover. (2) 'sampled altitude band' for color has no true altitude in a surface/shell shader -- it must be faked via radial offset or layered emissive shells; cheap, but a fidelity approximation the dossier glosses. (3) The analytic oval cannot do true inner multipoles (Uranus/Neptune); the dossier discloses this honestly. Internal pipeline-state claims (D12 hard-zeroed, system graph not exposed) are unverifiable from outside the codebase but self-consistent. Key sources: arXiv:1110.5209 (1/6 scaling), Samsonov 2020 GRL (deviations), arXiv:1503.05711 (asin-sqrt colatitude), Egan 2019 MNRAS + Gunell 2018 A&A (escape non-monotonicity), Bagenal 2020 + A&A 2025 (Io torus/footprint), Royal Soc 2020 / PMC7658782 (Uranus/Neptune offset-tilted multipole aurora).

engine.name: Atmosphere / climate
engine.brief: D4/D5/D8/D1/D3 -> bands/storms/clouds/haze + wind field + sky optics. Terminal surface for gas giants; forcing + sky for terrestrials.

dossier.mechanism: Atmospheric general circulation driven by the differential deposition of stellar (and, for giants, internal) heat, organized by planetary rotation. Three regimes, selected by drivers not by body-type: (1) RAPID ROTATORS / giants (D8 high) — strong Coriolis + the beta-effect funnel an inverse turbulent energy cascade into alternating east-west zonal jets; jet number/width is set by the Rhines scale L_R ~ pi*sqrt(U/beta), beta = 2*Omega*cos(phi)/a, so faster rotation => more, narrower bands (Jupiter ~dozen jets, Saturn fewer/faster). Belt/zone albedo contrast tracks rising (cloudy, bright zone) vs sinking (clear, dark belt) limbs. (2) SLOW / superrotating (D8 low — Venus/Titan-like): weak Coriolis widens the Hadley cell to pole-to-pole; eddy + thermal-tide momentum convergence at the equator sustains a single broad superrotating jet; banding collapses to near-uniform haze. (3) TIDALLY LOCKED (D7=1): permanent substellar heating drives day-to-night overturning — substellar upwelling + convective cloud cap, an eastward equatorial jet with a downwind hot-spot shift, and (if volatiles present, D2/D1) an 'eyeball' open-water/ice pattern. Cloud SPECIES and sky color come from D4/D1: condensation temperature picks the cloud (H2O, NH3, CH4, silicate/Fe for hot giants), and gas Rayleigh scattering vs aerosol/haze (tholins for CH4+UV, dust for thin dry atmospheres) sets sky tint and limb optics. D5 scales wind transport, opacity and haze depth; D6/D13 gate whether an atmosphere exists at all (cosmic-shoreline retention).

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Master regime selector via Rhines scale (jet count/width) and Coriolis strength.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Switches to substellar/eyeball circulation; couples to orbital period (a system-graph quantity scalar can't supply rotation rate for).

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Sets cloud condensation level / which volatile condenses; master habitability+volatile gate.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: A scalar cannot carry a species mixture (N2/CO2/CH4/H2/NH3 fractions). Cloud species, haze chemistry (tholins need CH4+UV), and Rayleigh cross-section all need a small composition vector, not one number.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Scales wind speed, opacity/optical depth, haze column, pressure-gated weather.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt
inputs.note: Seasonal band migration, polar hood/cap forcing, hemispheric asymmetry.

inputs.name: D6 atmoRetention
inputs.note: Existence gate: below cosmic shoreline => no appreciable atmosphere => engine emits bare-rock sky.

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: Gates retention against stellar-wind/UV stripping; co-determines whether D6 budget survives.

inputs.name: stellar spectrum / luminosity / orbital distance
inputs.note: Insolation pattern, day-night substellar geometry, UV flux (drives haze photochemistry AND escape) all need the star node + orbit; not exposed to the per-body pipeline today. D1 partially proxies bolometric insolation but not spectral shape or sub-stellar direction.

inputs.name: surface land/ocean + topography field
inputs.note: Cloud forcing, monsoon/orographic banding, and eyeball open-water mask need a 2D surface field from the hypsography/hydrology engines; a scalar driver cannot carry it. Currently the climate sky is computed body-globally with no surface feedback.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Hard-zeroed in current pipeline. An Io/Europa-grade interior heat source would add a bottom heating term (plumes, sublimation atmospheres) the engine cannot currently see.

outputs.name: windField
outputs.note: 2D zonal+meridional velocity on the sphere (u,v) used to advect cloud/dust textures and orient streaks.

outputs.name: bandMask / belt-zone albedo field
outputs.note: Latitudinal alternating bright-zone/dark-belt pattern + amplitude; terminal surface texture for gas giants.

outputs.name: cloudCoverField
outputs.note: Fractional cloud cover + species tag (H2O/NH3/CH4/silicate) per region, incl. substellar convective cap for locked worlds.

outputs.name: hazeOpticalDepth
outputs.note: Aerosol column (tholin/dust/sulfuric) -> limb darkening/brightening, sky saturation.

outputs.name: skyColor / atmospheric scattering params
outputs.note: Rayleigh coefficients + aerosol Mie tint feeding the atmosphere/sky shader (blue thick clear, orange tholin/dust, etc.).

outputs.name: storms / vortices
outputs.note: Discrete long-lived ovals/cyclones (GRS-type) seeded at jet shear boundaries; polar hexagon/vortex for fast rotators.

outputs.name: polarCaps/hoods forcing
outputs.note: Seasonal polar cloud hood / condensation cap forcing handed to surface (CO2/H2O frost), gated by D3+D1.

outputs.name: terminatorRing
outputs.note: For tidally locked: substellar cloud eye + ring of condensation at the day-night terminator.

cheapApprox.description: Closed-form regime + steered procedural noise, all per-pixel in a fragment shader; NO offline GCM. (1) REGIME SELECT from drivers: compute Rossby-like control from D8 and D7. (2) BAND FIELD: jet count N ~ clamp(round(k*sqrt(Omega_norm)),1,~20) from a Rhines proxy (N grows with sqrt rotation); build latitude bands as a phase function bands(phi)=sin(N*latitudeWarp(phi)); warp latitude by cumulative jet-profile so bands narrow toward poles. Belt vs zone albedo = sign of band gradient; modulate brightness by D4-selected cloud color. Zonal wind u(phi)=A*cos(N*phi) scaled by D5; this u advects a flow-aligned domain-warped fBm (curl-noise) to make turbulent cloud filaments and von-Karman-style wakes along shear lines — the classic real-time Jupiter look. (3) STORMS: Poisson-disk seed a few vortices at |du/dphi| maxima; render as analytic rotating Gabor/spiral kernels, count+size scaled by D5 and D8. (4) SLOW/SUPERROTATION branch (D8 low): N->1, widen Hadley to a single equatorial bright jet, raise haze opacity, desaturate banding. (5) LOCKED branch (D7): replace latitude bands with a substellar-centered radial field — Gaussian cloud cap at the substellar point, eastward hot-spot offset (rotate cap downwind by a fixed angle), terminator condensation ring; eyeball ice mask = step(D1 vs freezing) over substellar angle. (6) SKY/HAZE: closed-form single-scattering — Rayleigh beta(lambda) from a D4-derived mean molecular scattering scalar (blue when clear+dense), plus an aerosol Mie tint LUT keyed by composition class (tholin orange / dust tan / sulfuric pale / clear blue); optical depth from D5*hazeColumn. (7) EXISTENCE GATE: cosmic-shoreline test S_insol vs v_esc^4 (proxy via D1 and D14) AND-ed with D6/D13 — if it fails, output bare-rock sky (no bands/clouds/haze). Everything is analytic + a couple of octaves of animated noise: a few hundred ALU ops/pixel, no buffers to relax. Optional: bake the band/haze base into a small equirect texture per body at gen time (baked-field) and only animate the noise overlay, to amortize across frames.

epochBehavior.note: The atmosphere is a terminal SURFACE for gas giants (recompute its look if drivers shift across an epoch, e.g. cooling changes cloud species) and a continuous FORCING layer for terrestrials. Per-epoch it can act as an editor on host surface fields: deposits/forces polar frost caps, lays down wind-streak and dune-orienting shear (handed to the aeolian engine), and sets the eyeball ice/ocean mask that the hydrology/surface engine reads. The live wind+cloud animation itself runs every frame at render time, but the static band/haze/storm-seed layout is solved once per epoch from the then-current driver vector.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Likely hard-coded by discrete body 'type' today: (a) a fixed 'gas-giant' look (Jupiter-banded palette) applied whenever class==giant, rather than deriving jet COUNT/WIDTH from D8 via Rhines and cloud COLOR from D4/D1 condensation — a slow giant should superrotate into ~1 band, a hot giant should show silicate/Fe clouds, not NH3 white; (b) 'terrestrial with atmosphere' getting a default blue sky regardless of D4 (a CH4+UV world should be tholin-orange, a thin dry world dust-tan, a dense-clear world deep blue); (c) tidal-lock eyeball/substellar circulation toggled by a habitability flag instead of emerging from D7+D1+D2; (d) storms/great-spot placed as a decorative type feature instead of seeded at driver-derived jet-shear maxima; (e) sky color chosen from a per-type LUT rather than from a composition->scattering computation. The fix is to make every visible outcome a continuous function of (D8,D7,D1,D4,D5,D6,D13), so identical 'types' diverge when their drivers differ.
loadBearingClaims: Jet count/width follows the Rhines scale (N grows ~ sqrt of rotation rate, narrowing toward poles): solid for Jupiter/Saturn cloud-tracking, but the exact closed-form mapping from D8 to integer N for arbitrary exoplanets is a THEO/SIM extrapolation that may mis-count bands for in-between rotators.

The belt(dark)=sinking/clear, zone(bright)=rising/cloudy albedo rule is the textbook picture but the real belt/zone vertical circulation is genuinely debated (Juno shows ammonia/dynamics complications), so the brightness mapping is a defensible simplification, not settled fact.

A single closed-form regime switch at some D8 threshold cleanly separates banded vs superrotating worlds — real transition is gradual and also depends on atmospheric thermal inertia/optical depth (D5), so a hard threshold will look wrong near the boundary.

Sky color can be reduced to Rayleigh-beta(from a scalar) + an aerosol Mie tint LUT — adequate visually, but collapsing D4 to one scattering scalar drops composition-dependent absorption bands (e.g. methane's red absorption giving Uranus/Neptune cyan) that a true color needs.

D6/D13 + a cosmic-shoreline insolation-vs-escape^4 test is sufficient to gate atmosphere existence — the relation is empirical/dispersed with large scatter and recent hydrodynamic-escape revisions, so borderline bodies may be mislabeled as airless or air-bearing.

verdicts.claim: Jet count/width follows the Rhines scale, with N growing ~ sqrt of rotation rate and bands narrowing toward poles (closed-form D8->integer N mapping).
verdicts.reasoning: The Rhines-scale mechanism is well established: jet width ~ sqrt(U/beta), beta=2*Omega*cos(phi)/a, and the inverse-cascade-halted-by-Rossby-waves picture is textbook for Jupiter/Saturn multi-jet vs Uranus/Neptune single-jet-per-hemisphere (confirmed across multiple sources). The dossier's OWN hedge is honest and correct: the exact closed-form D8->integer N mapping is a THEO/SIM extrapolation that can mis-count for in-between rotators. One genuine physics imprecision the dossier glosses: Rhines width depends on BOTH beta (rotation) AND U (RMS wind speed), so 'N grows ~ sqrt(rotation)' holds U fixed; with D5 also scaling U, N is not a pure function of D8. The dossier partly acknowledges this (D5 scales wind). Not refuted because the claim is presented WITH the correct caveat and the directional physics is sound.

verdicts.claim: belt(dark)=sinking/clear, zone(bright)=rising/cloudy albedo rule is a defensible simplification, not settled fact.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed and arguably UNDERSTATED in the dossier's favor (i.e., the dossier is appropriately humble). Juno microwave data show the classic shallow picture (bright cloudy zones = upwelling) REVERSES below ~10 bar, and the belt/zone vertical circulation is genuinely debated (stacked opposing cells, ammonia-opacity vs temperature ambiguity). The dossier explicitly labels this a defensible simplification not settled fact, which the literature supports. Correctly grounded; the visual mapping is fine for a renderer.

verdicts.claim: A single closed-form regime switch at some D8 threshold cleanly separates banded vs superrotating worlds.
verdicts.reasoning: The dossier itself flags this as wrong-near-the-boundary: the real banded->superrotating transition is gradual and depends on thermal inertia / optical depth (D5), not a hard D8 threshold. Literature on slowly-rotating/tidally-locked superrotation (Showman & Polvani; recent 2025 mechanism papers) confirms the transition is governed by multiple non-dimensional numbers (Rossby, radiative/advective timescale ratio), not a single rotation cutoff. The claim as stated (with its caveat) is accurate; a hard threshold WILL look wrong near the boundary, which the dossier admits. Not refuted because it is correctly hedged, but the underlying 'clean switch' modeling choice is a real fidelity limitation.

verdicts.claim: Sky color reducible to Rayleigh-beta(scalar) + aerosol Mie tint LUT; collapsing D4 to one scattering scalar drops composition-dependent absorption bands.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Uranus/Neptune cyan is produced by METHANE ABSORBING RED light (plus haze-layer thickness differences per 2022 Oxford work), NOT by Rayleigh scattering. A single Rayleigh scalar + Mie tint LUT cannot reproduce absorption-band color; the dossier correctly identifies this as a true-color gap. The underSupplied flag on D4 (needs a composition vector, not a scalar) is well justified. Self-criticism is accurate and load-bearing.

verdicts.claim: D6/D13 + cosmic-shoreline insolation-vs-escape^4 test is sufficient to gate atmosphere existence; borderline bodies may be mislabeled.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed with nuance the dossier mostly captures. Zahnle & Catling's shoreline scales with CUMULATIVE XUV (not bolometric) ~ v_esc^4; the 2025 'revisited' (Oxford) work shows it is a TRANSITION ZONE with large scatter (volatile fraction, composition, stellar activity), defines it at 90%/50%/1% retention probabilities, and finds composition-dependent escape powers (CH4 ~ F_XUV*R^-0.7) rather than a universal ^4. The dossier proxies the test with D1 (bolometric tempEq) + D14 instead of true cumulative XUV history -- a real, acknowledged simplification. Its hedge ('borderline bodies may be mislabeled') is exactly right. Not refuted; the empirical relation supports the gate as a coarse but defensible classifier.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time WebGL feasible and does NOT hide an offline GCM, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. Every step is local and bounded: (1) regime select = a few scalar comparisons on drivers; (2) band field = analytic sin/phase function of warped latitude + a couple octaves of fBm/curl-noise -- domain warping (iquilezles) and curl noise are standard, cheap, derivative-available shader primitives, and real-time GPU-noise gas giants are a shipped technique (Seed of Andromeda); (3) storms = a fixed small count of analytic Gabor/spiral kernels Poisson-seeded at shear maxima -- O(few) per pixel, no iteration; (4)/(5) slow/locked branches are just different analytic fields (single jet / substellar Gaussian + downwind rotation + terminator ring + step() ice mask); (6) sky = closed-form SINGLE-scattering Rayleigh + a small Mie tint LUT lookup -- no multiple-scattering integral, no light-transport solve; (7) existence gate = one inequality. The stated cost (a few hundred ALU ops/pixel, no buffers to relax) is plausible. The one HONEST cost the dossier names -- fragment-shader gas giants are fill-rate-limited at close range -- is real but bounded, and the offered amortization (bake band/haze base into a small equirect per body at gen time, animate only the noise overlay) is a legitimate real-time optimization, not a smuggled offline sim. Caveats that do NOT break feasibility but reduce fidelity: the 'closed-form Rhines N' is an empirical fit not a derived law; the hard D8 regime threshold mis-renders near transitions; the single Rayleigh scalar cannot do methane-absorption color (an absorption-band term or per-channel coefficients would be cheap to add and should be); surface-feedback (clouds over land/ocean, monsoon/orographic banding, eyeball mask) is absent because the 2D surface field is underSupplied -- the dossier flags this. None of these introduce iteration or global coupling; they are accuracy limits, not performance traps. Verdict: real-time feasible as described.

verify.notes: Adversarial verification outcome: I could NOT refute any of the five load-bearing claims -- each is directionally correct per current literature AND each ships with an honest, accurate caveat (this dossier is unusually self-critical; the hedges are not decorative, they match the actual state of the science). The cheap approximation is the genuinely strong part: it is all local/analytic/bounded with no hidden offline GCM or relaxation; domain warping + curl noise + closed-form single-scattering are established real-time WebGL techniques. Most material fidelity gaps (all acknowledged by the dossier itself, not discovered against it): (1) D4 collapsed to one Rayleigh scalar cannot reproduce absorption-band colors -- Uranus/Neptune cyan comes from methane absorbing red light, not Rayleigh; a cheap per-channel absorption term should be added. (2) Rhines N as a closed-form function of D8 alone ignores the U (wind-speed/D5) dependence -- N is not purely a function of rotation. (3) Hard D8 regime threshold will mis-render the gradual banded->superrotating transition (also D5/optical-depth dependent). (4) Cosmic shoreline is empirically a transition ZONE with composition-dependent escape powers (not a clean v_esc^4 line), and the dossier proxies cumulative XUV with bolometric D1 -- coarse but acceptable as a gate. (5) No surface feedback (clouds/monsoon/orographic/eyeball mask) because the 2D surface field is underSupplied. The typeDemotionNote critique (replacing per-body-type LUTs with continuous functions of D8/D7/D1/D4/D5/D6/D13) is sound and is the right architectural direction. Sources: Rhines/zonal-jet scaling (arxiv 1306.2418, iopscience PSJ ae6da7); belt/zone Juno reversal (PMC7067733, Leicester/Juno 2021); superrotation/Matsuno-Gill/hotspot offset (Showman & Polvani 1103.3101, arxiv 2510.21680); cosmic shoreline revisited (iopscience 1538-4357/adfe69, Oxford 2025); Uranus/Neptune methane color (NASA, Oxford 2022); procedural feasibility (iquilezles domain warping, Seed of Andromeda GPU-noise gas giant).

engine.name: Lithospheric-stress / tectonic-grain
engine.brief: D11/D12/D14 + composition + despin -> structural-grain field + relief (ranges, rifts, scarps, plateaus, grooves, tessera). Despin/TPW can produce a 2nd generation of lineaments (epoch-relevant).

dossier.mechanism: Lithospheric stress and tectonic grain. A planet's surface relief is the integrated record of where the brittle outer shell has been pulled apart (extension -> normal faults, grabens, rifts), pushed together (compression -> thrust faults, lobate scarps, fold-and-thrust belts, wrinkle ridges), and sheared (strike-slip). These stresses come from a small set of GLOBAL, geometrically-predictable sources plus a regional one: (1) DESPINNING -- as a body's spin slows (tidal braking, especially toward synchronous lock), its rotational equatorial bulge relaxes; the shell must re-fit a more spherical figure, producing a latitude-banded stress field (Melosh 1977): E-W normal faulting near the poles, mid-latitude strike-slip, and N-S-trending thrust faulting at the equator, with the dominant pattern set by elastic shell thickness. (2) GLOBAL CONTRACTION/EXPANSION -- interior cooling shrinks the radius, putting the whole shell into compression (Mercury's lobate scarps, ~0.06% areal strain, ~<1 km radius loss); interior heating/differentiation expands it, opening extensional grooves (Ganymede grooved terrain). A small radial strain (0.05-0.1%) biases the despin pattern, shifting fault provinces toward equator (expansion) or pole (contraction). (3) TIDAL/DIURNAL + NON-SYNCHRONOUS-ROTATION STRESS on tidally worked icy shells -- builds the dense lineament networks and cycloids of Europa/Ganymede; superposed crack sets at rotating azimuths record shell migration over the interior. (4) MANTLE-CONVECTION / DOWNWELLING regional stress -- thickens crust into plateaus and complex polygonal fabrics (Venus tessera/crustal plateaus). The TECTONIC REGIME itself (mobile-lid plate tectonics vs. single stagnant-lid shell) is gated by whether convective driving stress exceeds lithospheric yield strength; larger radius/gravity raises fault strength faster than buoyancy, pushing big rocky bodies toward stagnant-lid. The engine's job is to lay down a structural-GRAIN field (a tensor/orientation + magnitude of principal stress over the sphere) and convert it, via an Anderson-faulting rule, into relief features whose orientation, sense, and density read out the body's spin history, thermal history, and interior.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory
inputs.note: Resurfacing budget vs impact flux sets how much tectonic fabric survives vs is buried; old stagnant surfaces preserve grain, young resurfaced ones overprint it.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Master driver for icy-shell lineament networks, grooves, expansion-driven grabens, and despin-coupled stress. HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline -> Europa/Ganymede/Io-grade tectonic grain cannot be produced at all. This is the single biggest gap for E6.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets isostatic relief ceiling (max mountain/scarp height scales ~1/g), fault-plane mechanics, AND the stagnant-lid vs mobile-lid regime gate (higher g -> stronger faults -> stagnant lid).

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Lock state implies a despinning history -> the latitude-banded despin stress field; substellar tidal bulge orientation.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Current spin sets present equatorial-bulge magnitude; the DELTA from primordial fast spin to current rotation drives the despin stress amplitude. Single scalar carries 'now' but not the history delta (see underSupplied note on despin amplitude).

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Time available for cumulative strain, multiple superposed tectonic generations, and relaxation of bulge.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction / D10 carbonToOxygen
inputs.note: Composition -> lithospheric rheology/yield strength. High C/O (carbide/graphite crust: SiC, graphite) gives a different brittle/ductile response and relief style than silicate; weak graphite vs strong SiC changes scarp morphology.

inputs.name: interior thermal-history / radius-change sign+magnitude
inputs.note: Whether the body is net-contracting (cooling) or net-expanding (heating/differentiation), and by how much, is not a current L0 scalar. It must be DERIVED from D12+D14+D16+D9, or added. Sign of radial strain flips the entire feature set (scarps vs grabens).

inputs.name: primordial-spin / despin amplitude (Δbulge)
inputs.note: Melosh despin stress depends on (initial spin^2 - final spin^2) and elastic shell thickness, not the present rotation alone. A single rotation scalar cannot carry the historical despin amplitude or the shell thickness needed to pick the fault-province pattern.

inputs.name: orbital/tidal context (eccentricity, parent, resonance)
inputs.note: Diurnal tidal stress amplitude (Europa-type lineaments) and non-synchronous-rotation crack-set rotation need eccentricity + parent-body + resonance state from the per-system graph, which L0 computes but does NOT expose to the per-body pipeline.

inputs.name: crustal-thickness / lithosphere field from interior engine
inputs.note: Tessera/plateau relief and isostatic compensation need a crustal-thickness field; if no interior/differentiation engine emits one, E6 must synthesize it proceduralLY from drivers.

outputs.name: structuralGrainField
outputs.note: Per-texel principal-stress orientation (a 2D director/line field on the sphere) + magnitude + faulting-regime tag (normal/strike-slip/thrust). The master 'grain' that downstream weathering, drainage, and shading engines align to.

outputs.name: reliefDisplacement
outputs.note: Tectonic component of the height field: ridge/range crests, rift/graben floors, scarp steps, plateau uplift, groove corrugation. Bounded by the gravity-set isostatic ceiling.

outputs.name: faultDensityField
outputs.note: Spatial density + multi-generation overprint count of lineaments; high on tidally worked icy shells and old stagnant lids.

outputs.name: mountainRanges_ridges
outputs.note: Linear compressional belts (fold-and-thrust), N-S trending despin equatorial belts, wrinkle ridges.

outputs.name: rifts_grabens
outputs.note: Extensional troughs from contraction-relief, expansion, or polar despin normal-fault provinces.

outputs.name: scarps
outputs.note: Lobate thrust scarps (contraction) and normal-fault scarps; height scales with strain and 1/gravity.

outputs.name: plateaus_tessera
outputs.note: Crustal-thickening highlands with complex polygonal/ridge-and-groove fabric (downwelling/pulsating-continent style).

outputs.name: grooves_lineamentNetworks
outputs.note: Dense ridged/grooved terrain and crack networks on tidally heated icy shells (Europa/Ganymede), GATED by D12 which is currently zeroed.

outputs.name: secondGenLineaments
outputs.note: A superposed, rotated set of lineaments from a later despin/TPW epoch overprinting the first (epoch-relevant editor output).

cheapApprox.description: Closed-form steering field + steered noise + a thin bounded relaxation, all GPU-friendly; NO offline time-stepping. STEP 1 (closed-form global stress field): evaluate the Melosh despun-shell solution analytically per texel from latitude. It gives a smooth axisymmetric tensor: azimuthal stress more compressive than meridional, so faulting regime is a pure function of latitude (poles->normal, mid->strike-slip, equator->thrust), with a single shell-thickness parameter picking how wide each province is. Add a global isotropic radial-strain scalar epsilon (sign from contraction/expansion derivation) that shifts province boundaries and adds uniform compression (scarps) or tension (grabens). This is ~a dozen FLOPs/texel and directly yields the principal-stress DIRECTOR field + regime tag. STEP 2 (regime gate, closed-form): compute a dimensionless ratio of convective driving stress to lithospheric yield (scaling with D14 gravity, D9/D10 rheology, D16 age) to pick mobile-lid (a few large coherent provinces, possible plate-boundary great-circles) vs stagnant-lid (pervasive distributed grain). STEP 3 (grain texture): generate lineaments as domain-warped, anisotropic ridged/billow noise whose ORIENTATION is locked to the Step-1 director field and whose AMPLITUDE/regime sets profile (asymmetric lobate step for thrust, symmetric trough for graben, en-echelon offset for strike-slip). Tidal icy-shell networks (when D12>0) use a second director field from an analytic diurnal+NSR tidal-stress closed form (tension trajectories -> arcuate/cycloidal cracks), again steered noise. STEP 4 (plateaus/tessera): place a few low-frequency crustal-thickness blobs (Worley/FBM mask from a downwelling seed set), uplift isostatically (height capped by 1/g), then overlay the Step-3 grain at higher density inside them -> complex polygonal fabric for free. STEP 5 (optional bounded relaxation, <=8-16 Jacobi iterations): smooth the height field toward isostatic equilibrium so range crests/roots look compensated; strictly bounded, not a convergent sim. STEP 6 (second generation): for a despin/TPW epoch, re-evaluate Step 1 with a rotated pole/axis and BLEND a fainter overprint set -> superposed rotated lineaments. Everything is per-texel analytic or fixed-iteration; no PDE solve, no plate-motion integration.

epochBehavior.note: Runs per-epoch and edits the existing height/structure field rather than from scratch. First pass writes the primary grain. A later despin/TPW or thermal-regime-change epoch re-runs Steps 1-3 with a rotated stress axis and/or flipped radial-strain sign, BLENDING a second, rotated, fainter lineament generation onto the host terrain (e.g. new equatorial thrust belt cuts across older polar grabens; contraction scarps overprint an earlier expansion-groove field). It also acts as host for downstream editors (lava floods rift floors; weathering aligns to its grain).

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline almost certainly assigns tectonic look-and-feel by discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'icy moon' -> grooves, 'rocky planet' -> mountains, 'Mercury-like' -> scarps) rather than deriving it from the stress field. Demotion targets: (1) faulting regime/feature class should come from the Melosh latitude-banded stress field + radial-strain sign, NOT a type flag -- the SAME body shows polar grabens AND equatorial thrust belts simultaneously. (2) Mobile-lid vs stagnant-lid should fall out of the gravity/rheology/age stress-ratio gate, not be hard-set per type. (3) Groove/lineament terrain is hard-coded to 'icy moon' but is really a function of D12 tidalHeating (currently zeroed, which is exactly why it can only be faked by type) -- restoring D12 lets a warm rocky or carbide body also fracture. (4) Relief amplitude is likely a per-type constant where it should scale with 1/gravity (D14) and accumulated strain (D16). (5) Tessera/plateau presence should derive from a downwelling/crustal-thickening criterion (crust < ~2/5 lithosphere -> compression), not a 'Venus-like' tag.
featureMap: Mountain ranges / linear fold-and-thrust belts
Rifts and grabens (extensional troughs)
Lobate thrust scarps (Mercury-style)
Wrinkle ridges
Plateaus and tessera (Venus crustal-plateau highlands)
Grooved/ridged terrain (Ganymede-style)
Lineament networks and cycloids (Europa-style)
Strike-slip offsets / en-echelon ridge sets
Structural grain that aligns drainage, dunes, and weathering downstream
loadBearingClaims: The Melosh despun-shell stress solution can be evaluated CLOSED-FORM per-texel (function of latitude + shell thickness + small radial strain) to give a usable principal-stress director field and Anderson faulting regime -- i.e. the global tectonic grain genuinely needs no PDE solve. If the real solution requires nontrivial Legendre/elastic-shell series that don't reduce to a cheap shader expression, the closed-form claim weakens (still bakeable to a 1D latitude LUT, but the 'analytic per-texel' framing is the risk).

Real-time relief that LOOKS isostatically compensated can be had from <=8-16 bounded Jacobi smoothing iterations rather than a convergent relaxation; if crests/roots look wrong without true convergence this slips toward an offline cost.

D12 tidalHeating being hard-zeroed makes an entire feature class (Europa/Ganymede grooves + cycloid lineament networks) UNREACHABLE except by type-faking -- so restoring D12 is a prerequisite, not an enhancement. (Confidence high this is correct; the load-bearing risk is whether the rest of the team agrees to un-zero it.)

Tectonic REGIME (mobile-lid plate tectonics vs stagnant-lid) is gated by a gravity/rheology/age stress ratio and can be reduced to a single dimensionless gate in real time; the published result that higher radius/gravity favors stagnant-lid via increased FAULT STRENGTH (not buoyancy) is the basis -- if that scaling is more regime-dependent/episodic than a clean monotonic gate, the binary gate oversimplifies (episodic-lid is a real third state).

Despin stress amplitude depends on the (primordial-spin^2 - current-spin^2) DELTA and elastic shell thickness, which a single rotation scalar cannot carry -- so without a derived/added despin-amplitude + shell-thickness input, the engine can pick the PATTERN (from latitude) but not its correct MAGNITUDE, risking under/over-expressed grain.

verdicts.claim: The Melosh despun-shell stress solution can be evaluated CLOSED-FORM per-texel (function of latitude + shell thickness + small radial strain) to give a usable principal-stress director field and Anderson faulting regime; no PDE solve needed.
verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED by primary literature. Vening Meinesz (1947), on which Melosh (1977) builds, shows the despinning thin-shell stress tensor components are proportional to simple trigonometric functions of colatitude (cos^2 theta and similar). Melosh's own result gives province boundaries at FIXED latitudes (e.g. strike-slip equatorward of 48 deg, normal/graben trending E-W poleward), with the pattern set by a single shell-thickness parameter. This is genuinely a smooth axisymmetric tensor expressible as a handful of trig terms per texel; worst case it bakes to a trivial 1D latitude LUT. The dossier's own hedge (if it needed nontrivial Legendre series it would weaken) does NOT bite here: the membrane/thin-shell approximation reduces the elastic-shell problem to closed-form trig in colatitude, not a numerically-evaluated Legendre sum. The 'analytic per-texel' framing is sound. Note: Beuthe (2008/2010) shows that VARIABLE-thickness shells require coupled 4th-order PDEs, so the closed form is only exact for the constant-thickness idealization the dossier actually uses -- acceptable for a real-time approximation.

verdicts.claim: Real-time relief that LOOKS isostatically compensated can be had from <=8-16 bounded Jacobi smoothing iterations rather than a convergent relaxation.
verdicts.reasoning: PARTIALLY supportable, with a real caveat the dossier itself flags. The claim is narrowly correct as stated: it explicitly asks only for a COSMETIC, bounded, NON-convergent smoothing pass, not true isostatic equilibrium. 8-16 Jacobi passes are trivially GPU-cheap and will plausibly make crests/roots read as 'compensated' to the eye. The risk: the flexure/biharmonic literature explicitly notes Jacobi 'does not ensure convergence for all wavenumbers' and is 'usually abandoned' for high-rigidity flexure in favor of Gauss-Seidel+SOR or multigrid. Consequence -- fixed low iteration counts attenuate only SHORT-wavelength roughness; true LONG-wavelength regional compensation (the visually dominant signal for big ranges/plateaus) would need many more iterations or multigrid. So the look will be approximate. But because the dossier scopes this as bounded cosmetic smoothing and not equilibrium, it does NOT hide an offline convergent sim. Not refuted, but the 'looks compensated' guarantee is soft for large features.

verdicts.claim: D12 tidalHeating being hard-zeroed makes Europa/Ganymede grooves + cycloid lineament networks UNREACHABLE except by type-faking, so restoring D12 is a prerequisite not an enhancement.
verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED. The literature is unambiguous that Europa/Ganymede grooves, lineaments, and cycloids are produced by diurnal tidal stress (from orbital eccentricity / tidal heating) plus non-synchronous-rotation stress on a tidally worked icy shell (Greenberg, Hoppa, Hurford; cycloids = tensile cracks from diurnal tidal stress). With the tidal driver zeroed, the physical generator of that entire feature class is absent, so the only way to produce 'icy moon grooves' is to hard-key them to a body type -- which is exactly the type-faking the dossier diagnoses. The engineering claim (it's a prerequisite gap, not a polish item) follows directly. The dossier's stated residual risk is purely organizational (whether the team agrees to un-zero D12), which is honest.

verdicts.claim: Tectonic regime (mobile-lid vs stagnant-lid) is gated by a gravity/rheology/age stress ratio reducible to a single dimensionless real-time gate, with higher radius/gravity favoring stagnant-lid via increased FAULT STRENGTH (not buoyancy).
verdicts.reasoning: The cited physics is real but the 'clean monotonic binary gate' is an oversimplification the dossier itself acknowledges. O'Neill & Lenardic (2007) DO show increasing radius raises lithospheric resistive (fault) strength faster than convective driving stress, pushing large bodies toward stagnant/episodic lid -- so the fault-strength-dominance basis is correctly cited. BUT this is genuinely contested: Valencia et al. (2006/2007) argued the OPPOSITE (larger super-Earths more likely to have plate tectonics), and review work concludes 'no linear trend can be observed' because outcome depends on heat sources and pressure-dependent viscosity. Critically, episodic/intermittent-lid is a well-established THIRD state, not a binary. So a single monotonic gate will mis-call bodies near the boundary and cannot represent episodic-lid. The dossier flags exactly this ('episodic-lid is a real third state'), so the claim is not refuted as written -- but treating the gate as a clean binary in production would be physically wrong; it should at minimum emit a three-way classification with a fuzzy boundary.

verdicts.claim: Despin stress AMPLITUDE depends on (primordial-spin^2 - current-spin^2) delta and elastic shell thickness, which a single rotation scalar cannot carry; without a derived despin-amplitude + shell-thickness input the engine can pick the PATTERN but not the correct MAGNITUDE.
verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED. The despinning stress arises from relaxation of the rotational/equatorial bulge, whose change scales with the difference of squared spin rates (flattening ~ omega^2), so the driving strain depends on the spin DELTA (initial minus final), not present spin alone. Melosh further shows the resulting fault-province PATTERN is governed by elastic shell thickness. Therefore a lone present-rotation scalar fixes neither the amplitude (needs primordial spin) nor the province widths (needs shell thickness). The dossier's input-gap diagnosis (these are underSupplied / must be derived or added) is physically correct, and the consequence -- pattern recoverable, magnitude not -- follows directly.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The proposed hybrid is genuinely real-time-feasible and does NOT hide an offline sim, with two bounded caveats. STEP 1 (Melosh despin field) is the load-bearing risk and it holds: the thin-shell despinning stress is closed-form trig-in-colatitude (Vening Meinesz 1947), ~a dozen FLOPs/texel, or a trivial 1D latitude LUT -- no PDE, no Legendre evaluation, no iteration. STEP 2 (regime gate) is a single algebraic ratio -- cheap, though physically it should be a fuzzy 3-way (mobile/episodic/stagnant) not a clean binary; that is a correctness nuance, not a cost problem. STEP 3 (steered anisotropic ridged/billow noise locked to the director field) and STEP 4 (low-freq Worley/FBM plateau masks + 1/g-capped isostatic uplift) are standard GPU procedural-terrain operations with bounded per-texel cost. STEP 6 (second generation = re-evaluate Step 1 with a rotated pole and blend) is just another closed-form pass -- no integration. The icy-shell branch (diurnal + NSR tidal stress) is also computed analytically via the standard thin-shell approximation per point, so it stays closed-form. The one place that flirts with hidden cost is STEP 5's Jacobi relaxation: true isostatic/biharmonic relaxation is NOT guaranteed to converge in a fixed small iteration count (multigrid is the real tool), so 8-16 passes only cosmetically smooth short wavelengths. But the dossier explicitly scopes this as bounded, non-convergent, cosmetic -- it does NOT claim equilibrium and does NOT smuggle in an unbounded solve. CRUCIALLY, nothing here does plate-motion time-integration, a global per-pixel coupled solve, or offline thermal-history stepping; every step is per-texel-analytic or fixed-iteration. The honest residual gaps are about INPUT FIDELITY (zeroed D12 kills the icy-shell feature class; missing despin-amplitude + shell-thickness + radial-strain-sign means correct PATTERN but wrong MAGNITUDE and possibly wrong scarp-vs-graben sign), not about concealed compute. So: real-time feasible = yes; the threats to output QUALITY are under-supplied drivers and the binary-gate/relaxation simplifications, all of which the dossier discloses.

verify.notes: Verification grounded in primary/secondary planetary-geophysics literature. Strongest confirmations: (1) despin stress is closed-form trig-in-colatitude -- Vening Meinesz 1947 (proportional to cos^2 theta etc.), Melosh 1977 (fixed province boundary at 48 deg, pattern set by shell thickness); this validates the single most load-bearing 'analytic per-texel' claim. (2) Icy-shell grooves/cycloids are tidally driven and unreachable with D12 zeroed (Greenberg/Hoppa/Hurford). (3) Despin amplitude scales with spin-squared delta -> single rotation scalar is insufficient. Genuine weaknesses the dossier ALREADY discloses (so not refutations, but the caller should weight them): regime is contested and non-monotonic (Valencia vs O'Neill/Lenardic; episodic-lid is a real third state -> binary gate will mis-call boundary bodies); Jacobi relaxation is non-convergent for long-wavelength compensation (8-16 passes are cosmetic only -> large features won't read as truly compensated); constant-thickness closed form breaks to coupled 4th-order PDEs for variable thickness (Beuthe 2008) -- fine for an approximation but means the 'analytic' result is the idealized case. I could not extract equations directly from the Melosh PDF (scanned/image-only, no text layer; semantic PDF search unavailable -- fastembed not installed), so the trig-in-colatitude confirmation rests on the search-result summary plus the independent Vening Meinesz / Beuthe corroboration, which is consistent and high-confidence. Net: cheap approximation is real-time-honest; output realism is bottlenecked by under-supplied L0 drivers, exactly as the dossier's underSupplied flags assert."}

engine.name: Endogenic-heat / magmatism
engine.brief: D12 + tidal-heat-flux + D14/D5 + composition(fluid) -> thermal-emission+age field + volcanic landforms (hotspot-placed) + magma-ocean / cryovolcanic systems.

dossier.mechanism: Endogenic-heat / magmatism: a body's interior is heated by three real sources -- (1) radiogenic decay (U/Th/K, declining with D16 age), (2) tidal dissipation from forced eccentric/resonant orbits (the dominant heat source for Io, Europa, Enceladus, Triton), and (3) residual accretional/primordial heat. That interior heat budget, set against the body's ability to lose heat (governed by D14 mass/gravity and radius), determines a single master quantity: surface heat flux q (W/m^2). q drives partial melting in the silicate mantle or volatile ice shell, feeds buoyant diapirs/plumes that rise via Rayleigh-Taylor instability, and erupts as lava or cryomagma. Eruptive STYLE and landform morphology are then shaped by gravity (taller edifices at low g), atmospheric pressure (D5 gates explosive vs effusive -- high pressure suppresses magma fragmentation), and fluid composition (silicate vs carbonate vs water/ammonia/nitrogen cryomagma, set by D1/D2/D10). The same heat budget controls the AGE of the visible surface: high q resurfaces frequently and erases craters (young surface); low q lets craters accumulate (old surface). Tidal flux scales as dE/dt ~ (21/2) k2 Mp^2 Rs^5 n e^2 / (Q a^6), so it is set by the SYSTEM GRAPH (host mass, semi-major axis, eccentricity, resonance), not by any single per-body scalar.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Intended primary driver, but per the system note it is HARD-ZEROED in the current game pipeline. With D12=0 the entire tidal branch (Io/Europa/Enceladus/Triton-class worlds) is dead and the engine collapses to radiogenic+primordial only. This is the single biggest under-supply.

inputs.name: tidal-heat-flux q_tidal
inputs.note: True tidal flux needs host mass Mp, semi-major axis a, eccentricity e, mean motion n, Love number k2, and dissipation Q -- i.e. the per-system graph (star/sibling/moon/resonance). L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline, and a single scalar D12 cannot carry the a^-6 / e^2 / resonance structure that makes tidal heating spatially patterned (e.g. polar concentration on Enceladus, sub/anti-jovian asymmetry on Io).

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets edifice height ceiling (lava piles higher before gravitational failure at low g -> Olympus Mons), shield aspect ratio, and the heat-loss denominator (larger bodies retain heat longer).

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Pressure-gates explosive vs effusive eruption. High surface pressure (Venus ~92 bar) suppresses magma fragmentation, requiring high volatile content to go explosive; thin/no atmosphere favors fire-fountains and wide pyroclastic dispersal.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory
inputs.note: Impact-flux + resurfacing budget; the volcanic resurfacing term competes with crater accumulation to set apparent surface age.

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Radiogenic heat declines roughly exponentially with age (half-lives of U/Th/K); old small bodies are volcanically dead unless tidally driven.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq + D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Select fluid phase: hot/dry -> silicate lava; cold/volatile-rich -> cryomagma (water/ammonia/N2/CH4). Also gate substellar magma-ocean formation when D1 exceeds silicate solidus.

inputs.name: D10 carbonToOxygen
inputs.note: High C/O -> carbide/graphite mantle mineralogy -> exotic carbonate or carbon-rich melt chemistry and surface color.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: On a tide-locked body with D1 above solidus, places a persistent dayside/substellar magma ocean (hemispherical), independent of tidal dissipation.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: Core size and mantle differentiation; influences melt composition and how much radiogenic budget sits in the silicate fraction.

inputs.name: thermal/age field from upstream (E-impacts/cratering)
inputs.note: Existing crater/basin patches that E7 floods or embays as an editor.

inputs.name: system-graph: host body + orbital resonance chain
inputs.note: Resonance (Laplace 1:2:4 for Io/Europa/Ganymede; Enceladus:Dione 2:1) is what FORCES the non-zero eccentricity that sustains tidal heat. A scalar cannot encode 'which siblings am I locked to and how stiff is the chain.'

outputs.name: surfaceHeatFlux q
outputs.note: Scalar/low-res field (W/m^2). Master output: thresholds set resurfacing rate, melt fraction, thermal emission.

outputs.name: thermalEmissionField
outputs.note: Night-side glow / hotspot temperature map for emissive shading (Io paterae ~1000K+, lava lakes, fissure incandescence, substellar magma-ocean glow).

outputs.name: surfaceAgeField (resurfacing override)
outputs.note: Where volcanism is active, age is reset young; modulates crater density and weathering downstream. Couples to D11/D16.

outputs.name: hotspotCenters (point set)
outputs.note: Plume/hotspot locations from Rayleigh-Taylor-like spacing; seed volcanic edifices, paterae, fissures.

outputs.name: shieldVolcanoes / paterae
outputs.note: Edifice height & aspect ratio scaled by D14 (low g -> tall like Olympus Mons).

outputs.name: lavaPlains / flood basalts / mare-fill
outputs.note: Effusive flows that embay and flood existing craters/basins (editor-on-host).

outputs.name: cryovolcanic terrain
