cheapApprox.description: Three-stage closed-form + steered-noise + editor pipeline, all real-time. STAGE 1 (closed-form, per body, once): compute a scalar heat-flux budget q = q_radiogenic(D16) + q_tidal + q_primordial(D14,D16), where q_radiogenic ~ A*exp(-D16/tau) and q_tidal is evaluated DIRECTLY from the system-graph tidal law dE/dt ~ (21/2)k2 Mp^2 Rs^5 n e^2/(Q a^6) divided by 4*pi*Rs^2 (this is algebra, not simulation -- it just needs the graph inputs). Map q to (resurfacingRate, meltFraction, edificeStyle) via published thresholds: Io ~2-4 W/m^2 silicate volcanism; Enceladus ~0.1-1 W/m^2 cryo; <~0.05 W/m^2 -> dead/cratered. STAGE 2 (steered noise, hotspot placement): scatter N hotspot seeds on the sphere where N grows with q (Rayleigh-number proxy: low q -> few wide-spaced plumes, high q -> many) using blue-noise / Poisson-disk with spacing from the convection-wavelength scaling (~plume spacing). Bias seeds by D7 (substellar/antistellar concentration), tidal polar-concentration pattern, and a low-freq mantle-fertility noise. STAGE 3 (baked field + editor shader): at each hotspot, stamp an analytic edifice profile (height = k * q^p / D14, capped by gravitational-failure ceiling ~ strength/(rho*g); cryo vs silicate vs carbonate by D1/D2/D10) and an emissive temperature. For flood/mare fill, run the engine EDITOR-style over an existing crater/age field: where (hotspotProximity AND local elevation < flood level) set surface = young smooth lava, raise emissive, override age. Explosive-vs-effusive is a single closed-form switch on D5 + volatile content (fragmentation threshold). NO offline timestepping anywhere -- plume spacing and edifice height come from STEADY-STATE scaling laws, which is exactly the 'borrow settled scaling, place once' principle. The one honest caveat: realistic SPATIAL tidal-heating patterns (Enceladus south-polar focusing, Io sub/anti-jovian double bulge) come from finite-element viscoelastic models offline; in budget we approximate them with a fixed analytic obliquity/eccentricity-tide template (a baked spherical-harmonic-style mask) keyed by the graph, not a live solve.

epochBehavior.note: Runs per-epoch as the T3 endogenic editor. In a 'volcanic/resurfacing' epoch it FLOODS and embays an earlier engine's output: lava plains drown craters laid down by the impact/cratering engine (lunar-mare analog -- basalt ponding in pre-existing basins ~100 Myr after basin formation), and resurfacing resets the age field young where q is high. On dead/old bodies (low q) it is a near no-op and the cratered host shows through. Cryo worlds get a late-stage refreshing pass (Triton/Europa-style young surface).

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current code almost certainly hard-codes outcomes by discrete body 'type' (e.g. an enum like ROCKY/ICE_MOON/LAVA_WORLD/VOLCANIC selecting a fixed texture or feature set), and with D12 hard-zeroed there is no live tidal pathway, so any 'volcanic moon' look is necessarily faked by type rather than derived. It should instead derive continuously from the scalar heat-flux budget q: a body is volcanic because q crosses the silicate-volcanism threshold, cryovolcanic because q crosses a lower threshold with D2 volatiles present, and dead because q is below threshold -- with Io/Enceladus/Triton emerging as REGIONS of (q, D14, D2) space rather than named types. Likewise edifice height should come from k*q^p/D14 (continuous), not a per-type fixed mountain mesh; and explosive-vs-effusive from the D5 fragmentation threshold, not a per-type flag.
loadBearingClaims: The tidal-heating power law dE/dt ~ (21/2)k2 Mp^2 Rs^5 n e^2/(Q a^6) is closed-form and can be evaluated in real time from the system graph with NO simulation -- the only thing missing is interface plumbing to expose Mp/a/e/resonance to the per-body pipeline (THEO/OBS-anchored; the spatial PATTERN of that heat, however, genuinely needs offline viscoelastic FEM and must be approximated by a baked template).

D12 being hard-zeroed kills the dominant heat source for an entire class of bodies (Io ~2-4 W/m^2, Enceladus ~0.1-1 W/m^2 are tidal, not radiogenic), so the engine currently cannot produce its signature features without restoring a tidal-flux input.

Volcanic edifice height scales inversely with surface gravity (Olympus Mons ~22 km at 0.38 g) and can be captured by a closed-form height = min(k*q^p/g, strength/(rho*g)) -- the gravitational-failure ceiling is a real structural limit, but my exponents k,p are fitted/assumed, not measured.

Surface AGE is governed by the same q budget (Europa ~40-90 Myr, Triton <100 Myr possibly <10 Myr, lunar maria 3.8-2.5 Gyr) so resurfacing-vs-cratering can be a single threshold on q rather than a separate system -- the competition with impact flux (D11) is real but the exact crossover is a tuning assumption.

Explosive vs effusive is pressure-gated by D5: high atmospheric pressure (Venus ~92 bar) suppresses fragmentation so eruptions are effusive unless volatile content is high (~2-5% H2O depending on vent elevation) -- correct in sign, but the precise volatile/pressure thresholds are altitude- and composition-dependent and only loosely constrained.

verdicts.claim: Tidal-heating power law dE/dt ~ (21/2) k2 Mp^2 Rs^5 n e^2/(Q a^6) is closed-form and evaluable in real time from the system graph with no simulation; only interface plumbing is missing.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed verbatim against multiple sources (Grokipedia, A&A 2026, arXiv 0710.5651): the canonical spin-synchronous eccentricity-tide global dissipation rate is exactly (21/2) G k2 Mp^2 Rs^5 n e^2 / (Q a^6). The dossier dropped the explicit G but that is harmless notational shorthand (G folded into a constant). This is plain algebra given the graph inputs (Mp, a, e, n, k2, Q) -- no timestepping. The honest caveat that the SPATIAL pattern needs offline viscoelastic FEM is borne out by the literature (Souček/Běhounková/Tobie-class FE models for Enceladus south-polar focusing). Claim stands.

verdicts.claim: D12 being hard-zeroed kills the dominant heat source for tidally-driven bodies (Io ~2-4 W/m^2, Enceladus ~0.1-1 W/m^2 are tidal not radiogenic).
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Io global mean surface heat flux measured at ~2.24-2.5 W/m^2 (Veeder 1994; recent 2.24+/-0.45), range 1.5-4.0 -- consistent with '2-4'. Enceladus total flux ~0.2 W/m^2-class with radiogenic only ~4e-4 W/m^2 (0.4 mW/m^2), i.e. tidal dominates by ~2-3 orders of magnitude; radiogenic alone (~0.3 GW) cannot sustain the ocean. With the tidal branch zeroed the engine genuinely cannot reproduce Io/Enceladus/Europa/Triton-class worlds. Correct.

verdicts.claim: Volcanic edifice height scales inversely with surface gravity (Olympus Mons ~22 km at 0.38 g) and is captured by height = min(k*q^p/g, strength/(rho*g)); exponents k,p are fitted/assumed.
verdicts.reasoning: Directionally confirmed: Olympus Mons ~22 km, lower Martian gravity is a primary reason cited (weaker gravity, lower buoyant load, lithospheric support). The gravitational-failure ceiling ~ strength/(rho*g) is a real structural limit (edifices fail by lithospheric flexure / gravity spreading under load). The dossier honestly flags k,p as fitted/assumed, not measured -- so the load-bearing physical SIGN is right and the speculative part is self-disclosed. Real edifice height also depends on lithosphere thickness, magma supply duration, hotspot stationarity (not just g), but the dossier does not overclaim those. Not refuted; the modeling choice is a defensible cheap proxy with disclosed assumptions.

verdicts.claim: Surface AGE is governed by the same q budget (Europa ~40-90 Myr, Triton <100 Myr possibly <10 Myr, lunar maria 3.8-2.5 Gyr) so resurfacing-vs-cratering can be a single q threshold; crossover with impact flux is a tuning assumption.
verdicts.reasoning: Numbers confirmed: Europa average exposed surface age 40-90 Myr (crater SFD; range 20-200), Triton ~10 Myr (Schenk & Zahnle 2007, uncertainty factor ~10, up to 200-300 Myr), lunar maria 3.8-2.5 Gyr. The qualitative coupling (high q -> frequent resurfacing -> young, few craters; low q -> craters accumulate) is standard planetary geology. The dossier correctly marks the exact q-vs-impact-flux crossover as a tuning assumption rather than a measured constant. Honest framing; not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Explosive vs effusive is pressure-gated by D5: high atmospheric pressure (Venus ~92 bar) suppresses fragmentation; explosive needs ~2-5% volatile content.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed and the specific numbers check out: literature states Venus ~90 bar retards bubble coalescence/disruption making explosive volcanism unlikely; pyroclastic landforms would require abnormally high volatile content of 2.5-4 wt% H2O (matching the dossier's ~2-5%), and CO2 would need >6.5 wt%. The sign and the cited threshold band are accurate. Dossier correctly notes thresholds are altitude/composition-dependent and only loosely constrained. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: The spatial tidal-heating pattern (Enceladus south-polar focusing, Io sub/anti-jovian double bulge) requires offline viscoelastic FEM and is approximated in-budget by a fixed analytic baked spherical-harmonic mask keyed by the graph.
verdicts.reasoning: This is the dossier's own honest caveat and it is fully supported: producing the real spatial pattern requires solving anelastic deformation + heat transfer in a (possibly variable-thickness, faulted) shell -- finite-element viscoelastic models (Souček, Běhounková, Tobie). Crucially the dossier does NOT claim to do this live; it replaces the solve with a precomputed baked mask, which is the correct real-time move. No hidden live solve. The self-flag is accurate, not an oversell.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The three-stage pipeline is genuinely real-time-feasible and does NOT hide an offline sim or unbounded relaxation. STAGE 1 is pure algebra: a handful of scalar evaluations (q_radiogenic = A*exp(-age/tau), q_tidal from the closed-form tidal law, q_primordial) computed once per body. No iteration, no timestepping, no PDE. STAGE 2 is blue-noise / Poisson-disk hotspot scattering with N and spacing set by steady-state convection-wavelength scaling -- this is a bounded, well-known O(N) sampling operation (N is small, ~tens of hotspots), not a convection simulation. The 'Rayleigh-number proxy' borrows a SETTLED scaling law rather than integrating fluid dynamics, which is legitimate. STAGE 3 is analytic edifice stamping (one closed-form profile per hotspot) plus a single editor SHADER PASS over an existing crater/age field (a per-texel local test: hotspotProximity AND elevation < floodLevel). That is a standard fragment-shader splat/flood operation -- per-pixel but LOCAL, not a per-pixel GLOBAL solve and not iterative-to-convergence. Explosive-vs-effusive is a single closed-form branch on D5 + volatiles. The ONE genuine offline dependency -- the spatial tidal-heating pattern from viscoelastic FEM -- is explicitly acknowledged and replaced by a PRECOMPUTED baked spherical-harmonic mask keyed by the graph, i.e. an asset lookup at runtime, not a live solve. That is the honest, correct way to ship an FEM-derived field in budget. I found no concealed iteration, no unbounded relaxation, and no global linear/nonlinear system being solved per frame or per pixel. The main practical risk is not feasibility but FIDELITY: the fitted edifice exponents (k,p) and the q-vs-impact-flux crossover are tuning assumptions, and the baked tidal mask is a fixed template that will not respond to arbitrary resonance/obliquity combinations the way a real FEM would -- but the dossier self-discloses all of these. Real-time feasibility: yes.

verify.notes: This dossier is unusually well-grounded and, notably, self-honest: every place where the physics genuinely needs offline computation (viscoelastic FEM spatial pattern) or speculative fitting (edifice exponents k,p; q/impact crossover) is pre-flagged by the author rather than concealed. All five enumerated load-bearing claims independently confirmed against current literature (tidal law verbatim incl. the 21/2 and a^-6/e^2 structure; Io ~2.24-2.5 W/m^2; Enceladus tidal >> radiogenic by ~2-3 orders; Europa 40-90 Myr / Triton ~10 Myr; Olympus Mons ~22 km gravity-limited; Venus ~92 bar suppresses fragmentation, ~2.5-4 wt% volatile threshold). The single numeric loosening I would note: the dossier writes the tidal law without the explicit factor G -- harmless shorthand. The D12-hard-zeroed under-supply diagnosis is the most consequential finding and is correct: with the tidal branch dead, the engine structurally cannot make its signature (Io/Enceladus/Europa/Triton) worlds, and any 'volcanic moon' output is necessarily faked by a type enum -- exactly the typeDemotionNote's argument. The cheap approximation is real-time honest; the residual concern is fidelity/tuning, not feasibility. Could not refute any load-bearing claim. Sources include Grokipedia/Tidal_heating, A&A 2026 synchronous-rotation tidal model, arXiv 0710.5651, IOPscience PSJ Io thermal map + Triton tidal-heating, Wikipedia Olympus Mons, ScienceDirect 0032063315000100 (Venus explosive volcanism), Souček/Běhounková-class Enceladus FE tidal-dissipation papers.

engine.name: Bombardment
engine.brief: D11/D14/D5/D2 + composition(target) -> crater population + ejecta + crater morphology. (Space-weathering of the FINISHED surface is split out to E8b, T5.)

dossier.mechanism: Hypervelocity impactors from the system's small-body reservoir (asteroids, comets, secondary debris) strike the finished crust and excavate craters. The engine writes three coupled records onto the surface. (1) CRATER POPULATION: a size-frequency distribution (SFD) of craters accumulated over the body's exposure age. Production follows a power law in diameter (Neukum/Hartmann production functions; cumulative slopes near -2 to -3.8 across size decades); the population grows with exposure time until small craters reach EQUILIBRIUM/saturation, where new craters erase old ones and the observed SFD pins to a cumulative slope of roughly -2 regardless of further bombardment. (2) CRATER MORPHOLOGY: each crater's form is set by its diameter relative to the body's simple-to-complex transition diameter Dc, which scales inversely with surface gravity (Dc proportional to g^-1.25): bowl-shaped simple craters (depth/diameter ~0.2) below Dc; central-peak complex craters, then peak-ring basins, then multi-ring basins above it. The transition is ~16 km on the Moon, ~8 km on Mars, intermediate on Mercury. Target rheology rewrites this sequence: on icy crusts complex craters are shallower, lack peak rings, and develop central pits, central domes, palimpsests, and viscously relaxed (flattened) profiles absent on rock. (3) EJECTA: each crater throws a continuous ejecta blanket (thickness decaying as a power law in radial distance, geometrically self-similar when scaled to crater radius per McGetchin), a raised rim (rim-height/radius roughly gravity-independent), distal secondary-crater fields, and bright rays whose length scales as ~R^1.22 of the primary radius. An atmosphere acts as a high-pass impactor filter: drag, ablation, and airburst fragmentation remove small/weak impactors, truncating the small-crater branch of the SFD at a cutoff diameter that grows with atmospheric column mass (Mars ~few m to ~8 m, Titan ~6-8 km, Venus ~20-30 km). Volatile-rich/icy targets and carbon-rich targets shift strength, density, and post-impact relaxation. Across epochs the impact flux declines steeply (early accretion-tail / heavy-bombardment phase orders of magnitude higher than the present rate), so ancient terrains carry far denser, more degraded, more saturated crater fields than young resurfaced terrains.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory
inputs.note: Impact flux x exposure-age budget: sets total crater areal density and how far the small-crater branch has climbed toward equilibrium/saturation. The single most load-bearing input. As a lone scalar it conflates two separable things (flux level vs. time exposed) and cannot carry the per-epoch flux DECAY curve.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets simple-to-complex transition diameter Dc ~ g^-1.25 (morphology selector), depth/diameter, ejecta launch velocities, and ejecta-blanket radial extent in crater radii.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: High-pass impactor filter -> small-crater cutoff diameter. Monotonic proxy works, but the real cutoff also depends on impactor velocity/material and is non-linear (Mars vs Venus vs Titan differ by ~3 orders of magnitude); a single scalar can carry the trend, not the species-resolved physics.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Icy vs rocky target rheology: governs whether craters are bowl/peak-ring (rock) or central-pit/dome/palimpsest/relaxed (ice). Selects the morphology FAMILY, not just a parameter.

inputs.name: target composition / crust strength + density
inputs.note: From the differentiation/crust engine (rock vs ice vs carbon-rich C-from D10, regolith depth). Needed for pi-group strength term and relaxation. Currently approximated from D2/D10 scalars rather than a real material field.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Warm interior accelerates viscous relaxation of crater topography (Ganymede-style domes, palimpsests, near-total erasure on Io/Enceladus-grade bodies). HARD-ZEROED in the current pipeline, so tidally-heated worlds wrongly retain pristine deep craters.

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Time axis that, combined with the flux history, yields accumulated crater density and degradation state. Partially redundant with D11 as currently fused.

inputs.name: system small-body reservoir (impactor SFD, comet vs asteroid mix, planetocentric secondaries from moons/rings, resonance-pumped flux)
inputs.note: Real impactor population is set by the system: a body near a massive planet, inside a debris belt, or with many moons gets a different impactor SFD slope, velocity distribution, and secondary-cratering load. L0 computes a system graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline, so every body is bombarded by an identical implicit impactor population.

inputs.name: epoch flux-decay schedule
inputs.note: Bombardment intensity per named epoch (early heavy -> declining tail -> present). No driver carries the time-resolved decay curve; must be supplied as an epoch parameter, not a per-body scalar.

outputs.name: craterDensityField
outputs.note: Per-texel accumulated crater areal density / saturation fraction (drives how 'old and beaten' terrain reads). Modulated by host-terrain age so resurfaced patches read younger.

outputs.name: craterCatalog
outputs.note: Procedural list/heightfield of placed craters: position, diameter (sampled from the truncated production SFD), morphology class, age/degradation rank.

outputs.name: craterHeightfield
outputs.note: Composited crater topography: rim uplift, bowl/floor, central peak/pit/dome, terraces, peak/multi-ring structure -> displacement + normal map.

outputs.name: ejectaBlanketField
outputs.note: Continuous ejecta apron (radial thickness power-law), albedo/roughness contrast, rays, and secondary-crater speckle around large fresh craters.

outputs.name: degradationField
outputs.note: Per-crater freshness used by E8b space-weathering and by relaxation: sharp bright rayed (young) -> softened rimless ghost/palimpsest (old or relaxed).

outputs.name: saturationFlag
outputs.note: Boolean/scalar marking terrain that has reached crater equilibrium (slope ~-2), telling the renderer to stop reading distinct fresh craters and read a uniformly cratered texture instead.
