cheapApprox.description: All closed-form placement + baked compositing; NO offline simulation required. STEP 1 (population, closed-form): from D11 surfaceHistory x D16 age x epoch-flux, compute total crater number N for the patch. Sample crater diameters by inverse-transform of a piecewise power-law SFD (Neukum/Hartmann slopes: steeper at small D, ~-2 in the saturated regime). Cap the small-D branch at an atmospheric cutoff diameter d_min = f(D5) (lookup curve fit to Mars/Venus/Titan), discarding craters below it. STEP 2 (saturation, closed-form): when areal density exceeds the empirical equilibrium threshold, switch from placing distinct craters to blending a pre-authored 'saturated highland' tile, and stop adding small craters (they cancel). STEP 3 (placement): blue-noise / Poisson-disk scatter on the sphere, weighted by host-terrain age so younger resurfaced regions get fewer/sharper craters (this is the editor coupling). STEP 4 (morphology selector, closed-form branch): for each crater compare D to Dc = k * g^-1.25 (from D14); pick a parametric profile from a small atlas keyed by D/Dc AND by target family (rock vs ice vs carbon from D2/D10): simple bowl (d/D~0.2), central-peak, peak-ring, multi-ring; for icy targets swap in central-pit/dome/palimpsest profiles and reduce depth. Each profile is an analytic radial height function (rim cosine bump + paraboloid bowl + optional central peak gaussian + ring annuli), evaluated in the displacement shader -> no relaxation solve. STEP 5 (ejecta, baked field): stamp a radial ejecta texture (thickness ~ r^-3 beyond rim, self-similar in crater radii per McGetchin) plus, for the freshest large craters, ray sprites with length ~R^1.22 and secondary speckle. STEP 6 (degradation): assign each crater an age rank from its draw order vs flux history; older craters get softened normals/erased rims (a single smoothing parameter), approximating both impact gardening and viscous relaxation. OPTIONAL relaxation upgrade for tidally-heated/icy bodies: one bounded screen-space Gaussian-blur pass on the crater heightfield scaled by D12 (cheap stand-in for ice creep) rather than a true elastoviscoplastic solve.
cheapApprox.method_note: closed-form for population + morphology, baked fields for ejecta, optional 1-pass bounded relaxation only for icy/heated bodies

epochBehavior.note: Bombardment runs once per named epoch with an epoch-specific flux multiplier (early heavy-bombardment epoch deposits the dense saturated ancient population; later epochs add sparse fresh craters). It is ALSO an editor on host terrain: it reads the current surface age/resurfacing field and craters younger patches less, and later resurfacing engines (lava flooding, cryo, tectonics) in turn edit ITS craters (flooded floors, ghost craters, tectonically sliced rims). So E8a both accumulates across epochs and is mutually editor-coupled with resurfacing tiers.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Likely hard-codings to derive instead from drivers/fields: (1) crater MORPHOLOGY almost certainly chosen by a discrete planet 'type' (rocky/icy/lava) rather than by D/Dc with Dc=k*g^-1.25 from D14 plus the D2/D10/D12 rheology family -- the simple->complex->peak-ring->multi-ring->central-pit->palimpsest sequence should be one continuous selector, not a per-type texture set. (2) Small-crater cutoff likely a fixed minimum size or a per-type 'has atmosphere' boolean instead of a continuous d_min(D5) curve. (3) Crater DENSITY likely keyed to an 'old/young' type flag rather than computed from D11 x D16 x epoch-flux with a real equilibrium-saturation switch. (4) Ejecta ray/secondary presence likely an on/off per type instead of derived from crater freshness and D5 (rays are suppressed by space weathering and absent where the atmosphere filters secondaries). (5) Tidally-heated worlds: D12 hard-zeroed means relaxed/palimpsest morphologies can't be selected at all, so Io/Europa/Enceladus-class bodies wrongly render Moon-like pristine deep craters -- an outcome currently fixed by omission rather than derived.
loadBearingClaims: Simple-to-complex transition diameter scales as Dc proportional to g^-1.25, letting a single gravity driver (D14) select crater morphology class via D/Dc (THEO/OBS; ~16 km Moon, ~8 km Mars) -- if the exponent or the clean single-variable dependence is wrong, the morphology selector mis-sizes the transition on off-Solar-System gravities.

Small craters reach an equilibrium/saturation state with cumulative SFD slope ~-2 independent of further bombardment, justifying the 'stop placing distinct small craters, blend a saturated tile' shortcut (OBS/THEO) -- if the real equilibrium slope or onset density differs, ancient-terrain density will read wrong.

Atmospheric filtering can be captured by a single monotonic cutoff diameter d_min(D5); real cutoff also depends strongly on impactor velocity and material and spans ~3 orders of magnitude (Mars m-scale vs Titan/Venus km-scale) (SIM/OBS) -- a scalar D5 may not place the cutoff correctly across exotic atmospheres.

Ejecta blankets are geometrically self-similar (thickness a fixed function of distance in crater radii) and rays scale as R^1.22, so one baked radial template rescales for all craters (THEO/OBS) -- self-similarity breaks for very large basins and oblique impacts, which the template won't capture.

Viscous relaxation of crater topography on icy/tidally-heated bodies can be approximated by a single bounded blur pass rather than an elastoviscoplastic solve (SIM/SF) -- if relaxation timescale/strength is mis-mapped from D2/D12, icy worlds will look either implausibly fresh or implausibly erased.

verdicts.claim: Simple-to-complex transition diameter scales as Dc ~ g^-1.25, letting D14 (gravity) select crater morphology class via D/Dc (~16 km Moon, ~8 km Mars).
verdicts.reasoning: The inverse-gravity dependence is well established (Pike; depths and transition diameters 'vary inversely with gravitational acceleration g'). The specific exponent 1.25 appears in the literature (Krüger 2018 / cited sources note Dc ∝ g^-1.25 alongside the simpler ~1/g form). Caveat that lightly weakens but does not refute: the clean single-variable dependence is an idealization — transition diameter ALSO depends on target rheology/strength (ice vs rock shifts it down) and on impact velocity/acoustic fluidization (arXiv 1704.04247), and the published anchor numbers are Moon ~15-20 km and Mars ~6-11 km rather than the dossier's tidy '~16 / ~8'. The dossier itself flags the rheology family separately (D2/D10/D12), so the g^-1.25 selector is used correctly as the gravity term, not as the whole story. Load-bearing claim stands.

verdicts.claim: Small craters reach equilibrium/saturation with cumulative SFD slope ~-2 independent of further bombardment, justifying the 'blend a saturated tile, stop placing small craters' shortcut.
verdicts.reasoning: Directly confirmed: lunar crater counts over decades show the equilibrium cumulative SFD ∝ r^-2 (Xiao 2015; arXiv 1902.07746). One important grounding correction the dossier gets RIGHT in spirit: equilibrium density is only a FEW PERCENT of geometric saturation (empirical R≈0.1-0.3), not literal rim-to-rim packing — so the 'saturated tile' must encode empirical, not geometric, saturation, else density reads too high. The -2 slope and onset-threshold mechanism are sound. The shortcut is legitimate.

verdicts.claim: Atmospheric filtering can be captured by a single monotonic cutoff diameter d_min(D5); the dossier gives Mars ~few m-8 m, Titan ~6-8 km, Venus ~20-30 km.
verdicts.reasoning: The MECHANISM (atmosphere as high-pass filter, cutoff grows with column mass) is correct and the cross-body 3-order-of-magnitude span is real. But specific numbers are overstated/mis-stated, which is why I mark refuted per the 'default refuted if not independently confirmable as stated' rule. Venus: the crater-ABSENCE threshold is ~2-3 km (smallest possible ~150-300 m), and the ~10-30 km figure is the regime where craters are DISTORTED/MULTIPLE from fragmentation — not a clean 'cutoff' as the dossier implies. Mars: published atmospheric downturn for primaries is ~10-60 m / even down to ~10-20 cm in some models, broadly consistent with 'few m', so that one is roughly OK. Also, as the dossier's own note concedes, the true cutoff depends strongly on impactor velocity AND material, so a single scalar D5 carries the trend but cannot place the cutoff correctly across exotic atmospheres. Mechanism sound; the load-bearing 'single scalar suffices for placement' claim is the overstatement.

verdicts.claim: Ejecta blankets are geometrically self-similar (thickness a fixed function of distance in crater radii, McGetchin r^-3) and rays scale as R^1.22, so one baked radial template rescales for all craters.
verdicts.reasoning: McGetchin/Settle/Head t = 0.14 R^0.74 (r/R)^-3.0 confirmed exactly, and self-similarity in the gravity regime (thickness identical in all directions when normalized to crater radius) is the standard result. Ray scaling: literature gives Rr ∝ r^1.25 (Baldwin) to r^1.27 (Elliot 2018); the dossier's 1.22 is just outside the most-cited values but within the documented spread and rounding — not enough to refute. The dossier correctly self-flags the real failure mode: self-similarity breaks for very large basins (proximal vs distal ejecta differ, secondary-dominated) and for oblique impacts (butterfly/forbidden-zone patterns) — a single isotropic template won't capture those. As stated for the common case it holds.

verdicts.claim: Viscous relaxation of crater topography on icy/tidally-heated bodies can be approximated by a single bounded blur pass rather than an elastoviscoplastic solve.
verdicts.reasoning: As a VISUAL approximation this is defensible and I cannot refute it on real-time-rendering grounds. The real physics is genuinely a temperature-dependent (Arrhenius) elastoviscoplastic creep solve (Dombard & McKinnon; Bland; Caussi 2024) — and the dossier honestly labels its blur as 'SIM/SF' and a 'cheap stand-in,' not as the real mechanism. Two physical caveats that the blur gets WRONG and a reviewer should note: (1) relaxation is strongly SIZE-SELECTIVE — large craters relax much faster than small ones, so a uniform-radius Gaussian blur inverts/flattens the correct size dependence unless the blur kernel is scaled per-crater by diameter; (2) relaxation produces SPECIFIC morphologies (domed floors, central domes, palimpsests with raised centers) — a pure low-pass blur erases relief toward flat and will NOT produce an upward-domed floor. So the blur captures 'softening/erasure' but not the diagnostic dome/palimpsest signature the featureMap claims. Not refuted (it's offered as an approximation, honestly tagged), but it under-delivers two of the named icy features.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The proposed pipeline is genuinely real-time-feasible and does NOT smuggle in an offline simulation, unbounded relaxation, or a per-pixel global solve. Walking the steps adversarially: STEP 1 population = inverse-transform sampling of a piecewise power-law SFD — O(N) closed-form, no iteration. STEP 2 saturation = a density-threshold branch to a pre-authored tile — explicitly AVOIDS the expensive regime by NOT simulating crater-on-crater erasure (the physically correct but unbounded part); this is the key move that keeps it bounded, and it's legitimate because equilibrium genuinely pins to slope -2 regardless of further bombardment. STEP 3 blue-noise/Poisson-disk scatter — standard, bounded. STEP 4 morphology = analytic radial height functions (cosine rim + paraboloid + gaussian peak + ring annuli) evaluated in the displacement shader — closed-form, no relaxation solve. STEP 5 ejecta = baked radial texture stamp + sprites — O(craters), bounded. STEP 6 degradation = single smoothing parameter from draw-order rank — O(1) per crater. The ONLY iterative element is the OPTIONAL relaxation upgrade, and it is explicitly a SINGLE BOUNDED screen-space Gaussian-blur pass — fixed cost, not iterate-to-convergence. No global coupling, no N-body, no convergence loop anywhere. Honest grounding tags (THEO/OBS for the solid parts, SIM/SF for the relaxation stand-in) match reality. Caveats that affect FIDELITY but not FEASIBILITY: (a) the saturated-tile threshold must use empirical saturation ~few % of geometric, not geometric packing; (b) the relaxation blur kernel must be scaled per-crater by diameter (size-selective) and cannot reproduce domed-floor/palimpsest morphology, so two icy featureMap entries are over-claimed; (c) the atmospheric d_min(D5) lookup carries the trend but not species-resolved physics, and the Venus number in the prose is overstated. None of these reintroduce unbounded cost — they are accuracy notes. Verdict: a real, bounded, GPU-friendly approximation, not a disguised offline sim.

verify.notes: 5 load-bearing claims checked against primary literature. 2 of 5 marked refuted-as-stated (atmospheric cutoff numbers; and note I held the others to the same bar but they survived independent confirmation). Net assessment: the dossier's PHYSICS is well-grounded and its grounding tags are honest; the failures are (1) overstated specific numbers (Venus cutoff ~20-30 km should be ~2-3 km absence / 10-30 km distortion regime), and (2) the relaxation blur under-delivers the icy dome/palimpsest morphologies it claims and must be size-selective to be even directionally correct. The cheap approximation is the strongest part: it is genuinely real-time-feasible with no hidden offline sim, no unbounded relaxation (the one iterative step is a single bounded blur pass), and no per-pixel global solve. The saturation→pre-baked-tile switch is the load-bearing trick that legitimately sidesteps the only physically-unbounded part of the problem. Key fidelity fixes for implementers: use empirical (not geometric) saturation density; scale the relaxation kernel per-crater diameter; treat d_min(D5) as trend-only; and either drop or specially-author the domed-floor/palimpsest cases the blur can't produce. Sources: Pike & ScienceDirect on g^-1 transition scaling; Krüger 2018 (JGR Planets, g^-1.25); Xiao 2015 & arXiv 1902.07746 (equilibrium slope -2, density few % of geometric saturation); McGetchin Settle Head EPSL 1973 (t=0.14R^0.74(r/R)^-3.0); Elliot 2018 (ray length r^1.27); Dombard/Bland/Caussi 2024 (elastoviscoplastic & size-selective relaxation, domed floors); ScienceDirect S0019103504000582 & Britannica/Wikipedia (Venus ~2-3 km crater absence, fragmentation 10-30 km).

engine.name: Hydrology / working-fluid
engine.brief: relief + D1/D2(fluid)/D14/D8 -> drainage networks + base-level field + shorelines + deltas + outflow channels + karst + standing-liquid field. Working fluid may be water, methane, etc. NORTH-STAR coupling case: does mountains+rivers collapse into ONE engine with E6?

dossier.mechanism: Surface working-fluid (water, or low-T cryogenic liquids like methane/ethane on a Titan-class body) precipitates from the atmosphere, runs off down the relief gradient, and self-organizes into dendritic drainage networks. The governing physics is the stream-power incision law: vertical incision rate E = K·A^m·S^n, where A is upstream drainage area (a discharge proxy), S is local channel slope, K is an erodibility coefficient that folds in lithology + climate + working-fluid properties, and m/n is the concavity index (~0.5). Networks obey Hack's law (channel length L ~ A^h, h~0.57). Water/fluid pools wherever the relief contains closed depressions: a base-level field is set by depression-filling — every cell either drains to a lower neighbor or fills to its spill point, producing standing-liquid bodies (lakes/seas) and a global sea-level surface. Where fluid exits a channel into a standing body it drops its load and builds a delta; where a filled basin overtops its spill point catastrophically it carves outflow channels (Mars Kasei/Valles Marineris class). On soluble bedrock (carbonate on Earth; water-ice acting as soluble 'bedrock' on Titan) chemical dissolution by the working fluid carves karst — sinkholes, poljes, labyrinthic terrain — instead of, or alongside, mechanical incision. Working-fluid identity is gated by D1 (equilibrium temperature) against the fluid's liquid-stable range: water for temperate bodies, methane/ethane near ~90-95 K, none if too hot/cold or volatile-starved.

inputs.name: relief / elevation field
inputs.note: From E6 (tectonics/orogeny) + cratering + volcanism stack: the DEM that flow routes over. THE dominant input — no relief, no drainage. This is a full 2D height FIELD, not a scalar.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Selects which working fluid is liquid-stable (water vs methane/ethane vs none) and sets evaporation/precipitation vigor. Scalar — fine.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Total fluid budget: how much liquid exists to fill basins (sea level / lake fraction). Scalar — fine.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Determines the actual working-fluid species (CH4/C2H6/H2O/CO2-ice clathrate) and whether bedrock is soluble in it (karst gate). Scalar enum-ish — adequate but lossy for mixed-fluid bodies.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Gates precipitation transport + whether a hydrologic cycle runs at all (need atmosphere to rain). Scalar — fine.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Coriolis -> orographic precipitation asymmetry (wet windward / dry leeward), banded rainfall by latitude. Scalar carries rate but NOT the spatial precipitation pattern it should induce.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets channel/delta scale, sediment transport competence, and incision depth scaling. Scalar — fine.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory / D16 age
inputs.note: Erosional maturity: how dissected the network is (Titan = juvenile, little incision; Earth = mature). Maps to integrated K·time. Scalar — fine.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Eyeball-climate hydrology: substellar precipitation maximum, terminator drainage, nightside cold-trap ice/lake. Scalar flag forces a spatial climate pattern the field interface can't express.

inputs.name: precipitation field
inputs.note: Ideally an atmosphere/climate engine emits a 2D rainfall map (orographic + latitudinal + eyeball). Currently no such engine exists; E9 must synthesize it from scalars D5/D8/D7/D3 + relief.

inputs.name: axial tilt D3
inputs.note: Seasonal migration of precipitation belts + polar lake/cap placement (Titan's lakes are polar). Scalar — adequate as a placement bias.

outputs.name: flowAccumulation / drainage-area field
outputs.note: Per-cell upstream contributing area; threshold defines where channels appear.

outputs.name: baseLevel / standing-liquid field
outputs.note: Depression-filled water surface: lakes, seas, global sea-level mask. Drives shoreline placement.

outputs.name: channel network mask + Strahler order
outputs.note: Dendritic river/valley network, width scaled by accumulation^0.5 and D14.

outputs.name: shorelines
outputs.note: Intersection of base-level field with relief; benches/terraces at paleo-levels.

outputs.name: deltas / alluvial fans
outputs.note: Deposited where channels meet standing bodies (sediment lobes).

outputs.name: outflow channels
outputs.note: Catastrophic spill-carved megachannels where filled basins overtopped (editor pass on relief).

outputs.name: karst field
outputs.note: Sinkhole/polje/labyrinthic-terrain density where bedrock soluble in the working fluid.

outputs.name: incision delta-height (editor output)
outputs.note: Subtractive height modification of the E6 relief: valleys carved into mountains.

cheapApprox.description: Run as a baked-field GPU pass over the relief texture at terrain-bake time (per epoch), NOT a live offline sim. Pipeline: (1) FLOW ROUTING — D8 steepest-descent flow direction per texel in one fragment pass; resolve flat/pit blockers with a GPU priority-flood / FastFlow-style depression-fill so every cell drains (priority-flood is ~20 lines, O(n log n)). (2) FLOW ACCUMULATION — parallel-prefix/jump-flooding accumulation in O(log n) passes (Jain 2024 FastFlow demonstrates this on GPU) to get drainage area A per texel. (3) CHANNELS — threshold A to extract the network; channel width = c·A^0.5; this reproduces Hack's law for free since A->L scaling is emergent. (4) INCISION EDITOR — apply one closed-form stream-power step Δz = -K·A^m·S^n·(maturity from D11/D16), m~0.45 n~1, as a single subtractive height pass (NOT iterated to steady state — one bounded relaxation step keyed to age is enough to read as 'young vs old' terrain). (5) BASE LEVEL / LAKES — the depression-fill water surface from step 1, clipped by a global fill volume from D2·tempEq, gives lakes + sea level + shorelines analytically. (6) DELTAS — additive Gaussian sediment lobes stamped where high-A channels enter the standing-liquid mask. (7) KARST — if D4 says bedrock soluble in fluid, modulate with a closed-form sinkhole noise field (Worley/cellular) gated by accumulation, no sim. (8) PRECIPITATION — synthesize a cheap rainfall weight from latitude band (D8) + upslope/windward dot-product (orographic) + substellar bump (D7) and multiply into K; this stands in for the missing climate engine. Working fluid (color, viscosity-driven channel sinuosity, density-driven delta angle) is a closed-form lookup keyed by D1/D4. Everything is one bake producing textures the runtime shader samples — real-time cost at runtime is zero beyond texture reads.

epochBehavior.note: Runs per-epoch as an EDITOR on the relief produced by E6/cratering/volcanism: it carves valleys (subtractive), fills basins with standing liquid, stamps deltas (additive), and on a catastrophic-spill epoch can carve outflow channels into a pre-existing crater/canyon (e.g. methane/water flooding an impact basin then bursting its rim). Each named epoch re-runs on the then-current host surface, so later volcanism can dam a river or lava can flood a former lakebed, and a later wet epoch re-incises. Drainage maturity accumulates across epochs via D16/D11.

featureMap: river/valley drainage networks (dendritic channels)
lakes and seas (standing-liquid bodies, e.g. Titan polar lakes / Mars paleolakes)
shorelines and shoreline terraces
deltas and alluvial fans
catastrophic outflow channels (Kasei/Valles-Marineris class megachannels)
karst terrain (sinkholes, poljes, Titan labyrinthic terrain)
global sea-level / coastline mask
dossier.typeDemotionNote: Likely hard-codes 'water planet' vs 'ice planet' vs 'dry planet' as discrete surface TYPES that select a fixed river/ocean texture set, rather than deriving the working fluid and its presence from D1×D2×D4. The correct co-genesis form: fluid identity (H2O/CH4/C2H6/none), liquid-stable range, channel sinuosity/color, karst-on/off, and lake fill fraction should all fall out continuously from drivers — a body at ~92 K with methane gets juvenile low-incision drainage + polar lakes automatically, not because it was tagged 'Titan-type'. Similarly 'has rivers' is probably a boolean flag where it should be the emergent result of (atmosphere present AND fluid liquid-stable AND relief present). Outflow channels and deltas are probably decorative presets rather than consequences of the actual base-level/spill computation.
loadBearingClaims: The North-Star collapse question: E9 (hydrology) and E6 (mountains/relief) should NOT collapse into one engine, but E9 is hard-dependent on E6's output and must run as an EDITOR after it. They are one COUPLED pass over a shared height field, not one engine — drainage is a function OF relief but co-evolves with it (incision lowers peaks, so a single forward pass loses the orogeny<->erosion feedback). A single bounded relaxation step keyed to age captures enough of the feedback for visual reading without an iterated landscape-evolution sim.

A single non-iterated stream-power incision step (one Δz pass) reads convincingly as 'eroded terrain' — this is the riskiest claim; real landscape evolution models iterate to steady state over many timesteps, and one pass may produce unconvincing or unstable incision (n=1 helps stability, but slope feedback is lost).

The current L0 SCALAR interface cannot carry the precipitation FIELD that hydrology fundamentally needs (orographic + eyeball + latitudinal pattern). E9 is forced to synthesize rainfall from scalars + relief, which will be physically crude — and tidal-lock (D7) eyeball hydrology and Coriolis (D8) orographic asymmetry are genuinely under-supplied by scalars.

GPU priority-flood + FastFlow-style accumulation can produce a correct full-planet drainage + lake base-level field at bake time within a real-time/streaming budget (per-tile), so hydrology does NOT secretly require an offline simulation. If the depression-fill cannot be made robust on a cubemap/spherical tiling with seams, this fails and lakes/sea-level break at tile boundaries.

Working-fluid selection is a clean continuous function of D1/D2/D4 (Titan methane at ~90-95 K, water for temperate bodies); the ~1 cm/yr methane rainfall and ~10^-6 m/yr Titan erosion rates confirm a real but sluggish cryo-hydrologic cycle, justifying 'juvenile, low-incision' drainage as a driver-derived state rather than a preset.

verdicts.claim: E9 and E6 should not collapse into one engine but E9 must run as an EDITOR on E6's relief; a single bounded relaxation step keyed to age captures enough orogeny<->erosion feedback for visual reading without a full LEM.
verdicts.reasoning: The architectural framing is sound and matches the literature: drainage is a function OF relief, so E9 is hard-dependent on E6. The honest admission that a single forward pass loses the orogeny-erosion feedback (incision lowers peaks, changing slopes, changing incision) is correct. The mitigating clause ('one bounded step reads enough') is a design assertion, not a verifiable fact, but it is presented as a risk-acknowledged tradeoff rather than a guarantee, so it is not overstated. The coupling claim itself is well-grounded in geomorphology (stream-power LEMs explicitly couple uplift and incision). Not refuted, but confidence capped at medium because the 'enough for visual reading' assertion is untested.

verdicts.claim: A single non-iterated stream-power incision step (one Delta-z pass) reads convincingly as 'eroded terrain'.
verdicts.reasoning: The dossier itself flags this as 'the riskiest claim,' which is appropriate. Independent evidence undercuts it: (1) Real LEMs iterate to steady state over many timesteps; FastFlow's own erosion results use ~200 iterations / 'under 10 seconds' to generate aged landscapes, not one pass. (2) With the chosen m/n~0.5, the stream-power model is documented to show 'unrealistic behavior' — horizontal scale-invariance and ultra-sensitivity to initial conditions (esurf 2017) — so a single pass at this exponent inherits known pathologies. (3) A one-shot Delta-z = -K*A^m*S^n applied to the ORIGINAL slope (not a relaxed one) tends to over-deepen high-A trunk channels relative to headwaters and produces V-incision without the longitudinal concavity that comes only from feedback. n=1 helps numerical stability but does not restore the lost slope feedback. Marked refuted because the strong form ('reads convincingly') is not supportable; a weaker 'reads as young-vs-old at low fidelity' might survive. The dossier's own hedging is why confidence is medium rather than high.

verdicts.claim: The L0 scalar interface cannot carry the precipitation FIELD hydrology needs (orographic + eyeball + latitudinal); tidal-lock (D7) and Coriolis (D8) are genuinely under-supplied by scalars.
verdicts.reasoning: This is correct and, if anything, understated. Orographic precipitation is intrinsically a 2D field computed from wind direction dotted against the relief gradient; a scalar D8 'rotation rate' cannot encode the windward/leeward spatial asymmetry, and a scalar D7 flag cannot encode the substellar-max / terminator-drainage / nightside-cold-trap spatial pattern of eyeball climate. Titan's observed polar lake concentration (97% near the north pole) is a spatial climate signature no scalar reproduces — it must be hand-injected as a placement bias. The dossier's own input notes mark relief, D8, D7, and precipitation as underSupplied:true, which matches reality. The cheap-approx's 'synthesize rainfall from latitude band + upslope dot-product + substellar bump' is the correct mitigation but is explicitly 'physically crude,' which is honest. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: GPU priority-flood + FastFlow-style accumulation can produce a correct full-planet drainage + lake base-level field at bake time within a real-time/streaming (per-tile) budget; hydrology does NOT secretly require an offline sim.
verdicts.reasoning: Partially true but overstated in two ways. (1) TERMINOLOGY/CITATION ERROR: classic Priority-Flood (Barnes 2014, arxiv 1511.04463) uses a PRIORITY QUEUE that is explicitly 'not suited to parallelization on the GPU' because it imposes sequential order. The GPU-parallel result is FastFlow (Jain 2024, cgf.15243), and there flow routing is O(log n) but DEPRESSION routing is O(log^2 n) and 34-52x harder than flow accumulation — the dossier conflates the two and calls priority-flood 'GPU, ~20 lines, O(n log n),' which describes the single-threaded CPU variant, not a GPU one. (2) HARDWARE/SCALE: FastFlow's 'under 55ms at 4096^2' is on an Nvidia RTX A6000 with 48GB — a datacenter card, far above a WebGL/consumer target; full erosion (200 iters) is 'under 10 seconds.' (3) The decisive unaddressed risk is the dossier's own caveat: depression-fill must produce a GLOBALLY consistent base-level across a cubemap/spherical tiling. Priority-flood/lake-filling is inherently a GLOBAL coupling problem (a spill point can propagate across the whole planet), which does NOT decompose cleanly into independent tiles without cross-tile iteration — the very thing that breaks lakes/sea-level at seams. So the 'per-tile streaming budget' claim hides a global solve. The 'one bake, runtime cost zero' part is true (cost is moved to bake), but the claim that the bake is cheap AND tile-local AND seam-robust is not established. Refuted on the strong form.

verdicts.claim: Working-fluid selection is a clean continuous function of D1/D2/D4 (Titan methane ~90-95 K, water for temperate bodies); ~1 cm/yr methane rainfall and ~10^-6 m/yr Titan erosion confirm a real but sluggish cryo-hydrologic cycle justifying 'juvenile, low-incision' drainage as driver-derived.
verdicts.reasoning: The conceptual claim (fluid identity as a continuous function of equilibrium temperature, volatile budget, and atmospheric composition) is sound and well-supported — methane/ethane liquid-stable near ~90-95 K on Titan is correct, and continuous co-genesis is the right design. The ~1 cm/yr methane rainfall figure is corroborated (literature gives ~1 cm/yr time-averaged, with 0.6-60 mm/h storm rates). HOWEVER the supporting erosion-rate claim is mis-grounded: the primary Titan fluvial literature (Collins 2005; Perron 2006) concludes erosion rates on Titan are 'likely SURPRISINGLY SIMILAR to terrestrial rates given similar stream conditions' — Titan's net juvenile appearance comes from INFREQUENT, possibly episodic precipitation and integrated time, not from an intrinsically tiny ~10^-6 m/yr incision rate. The dossier uses a cited-looking '10^-6 m/yr' number to justify 'low-incision' physics when the actual mechanism for low net dissection is climatic intermittency. Because the justification mis-attributes the cause (and the specific rate figure is not the consensus story), the load-bearing claim is refuted on grounding even though the design conclusion ('juvenile low-incision drainage, polar lakes, derived not tagged') is defensible.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning:
The cheap approximation is MOSTLY honest and mostly feasible, but it hides one genuine offline/global-solve dependency and contains a load-bearing citation error, so it is not real-time-feasible as written for a FULL PLANET.

What IS feasible (real): Steps that are genuinely closed-form / O(log n) and bake-time-only — D8 steepest-descent flow direction (1 fragment pass), jump-flood/parallel-prefix flow ACCUMULATION (O(log n), this is FastFlow's cheap half), threshold-based channel extraction, the single bounded stream-power Delta-z subtractive pass (one step, not iterated), additive Gaussian delta lobes, Worley/cellular karst noise gated by accumulation, and the closed-form fluid lookup from D1/D4. These are real fragment-shader passes; moving them to a per-epoch bake and sampling textures at runtime is legitimate, and 'runtime cost is zero beyond texture reads' is true for these.

What is NOT feasible / hides a solve:
1) DEPRESSION-FILL / BASE-LEVEL (step 1 and step 5) is the hidden cost. The dossier calls it 'priority-flood, ~20 lines, O(n log n)' and implies GPU/per-tile cheapness, but (a) classic Priority-Flood uses a priority queue that is explicitly NOT GPU-parallelizable (sequential dependency), and (b) the actual GPU method, FastFlow, makes depression routing O(log^2 n) and 34-52x costlier than accumulation — the dossier conflates the two and understates the cost. More fundamentally, computing a globally-consistent lake/sea-level surface is an inherently GLOBAL coupling problem: a basin's spill point can propagate fill state across the entire planet, which does not decompose into independent tiles without cross-tile iteration. So the 'per-tile streaming budget' framing conceals exactly the global/iterative solve the prompt warns about, and the dossier's own caveat admits lakes/sea-level 'break at tile boundaries' on a cubemap if fill isn't robust — that failure mode is unresolved, not mitigated.
2) PERFORMANCE GROUNDING is optimistic: the cited 'fast' numbers (under 55ms at 4096^2; full erosion under 10s for 200 iters) are on a 48GB RTX A6000 datacenter GPU, not a WebGL/consumer target, and the single-pass incision is a deliberate fidelity sacrifice that the dossier honestly flags as its riskiest claim.

Net: as an EDITOR/bake that runs the cheap forward passes is real-time-plausible; but the claim that the FULL pipeline — including a seam-robust global depression-filled base-level — fits a real-time per-tile budget without a global or iterative solve is not established and is contradicted by the very papers cited. Hence realistic=false.

verify.notes: Sources used: FastFlow (Jain et al., CGF 2024, doi 10.1111/cgf.15243; author PDF read locally) — flow routing O(log n), depression routing O(log^2 n), 34-52x costlier; tested to 8192^2 on RTX A6000 48GB; 'under 55ms at 4096^2'; full erosion ~200 iters 'under 10s'; framed as INTERACTIVE AUTHORING (editor), no spherical/cubemap tiling addressed. Priority-Flood (Barnes et al. 2014, arxiv 1511.04463) — priority-queue variant explicitly NOT GPU-parallelizable; parallel variant needs tiled cross-talk. Stream-power m/n=0.5 pathology (esurf-5-807-2017): scale-invariance + ultra-sensitivity to initial conditions. Hack's law h=0.57+/-0.06 confirmed (Wikipedia/GeomorphOnline) — but dossier wrongly ties Hack's LENGTH law to a channel-WIDTH ~A^0.5 formula. Titan: ~1 cm/yr methane rain confirmed (Lunine&Lorenz; Perron 2006); erosion rates 'surprisingly similar to terrestrial' per Collins 2005 / Perron 2006 — contradicts the dossier's '10^-6 m/yr' low-rate justification (true cause of juvenility is intermittency, not tiny instantaneous rate). Titan polar lakes (97% near N pole) + karst/labyrinth dissolution on soluble ice CONFIRMED. SCIENCE ERROR not in the loadBearingClaims but in the mechanism text and featureMap: 'Kasei/Valles-Marineris class' lumps a fluvial outflow channel (Kasei Valles, water-carved) with a TECTONIC RIFT (Valles Marineris, Tharsis extension) — Valles Marineris is not a catastrophic-spill fluvial megachannel; treating it as an E9 output is mis-grounded. Overall: the dossier is unusually self-aware (it pre-flags its three biggest risks), but the depression-fill global-solve / cubemap-seam problem is the real load-bearing weakness, and the priority-flood-vs-FastFlow conflation + the Titan erosion-rate mis-attribution + the Valles Marineris lumping are the concrete factual hits.

engine.name: Aeolian
engine.brief: relief + D5/D14/D2(grain)/D8(wind-rose) + frost-gate -> sediment-flux field -> dunes / yardangs / wind streaks + dust-budget field.

dossier.mechanism: Wind shear over a granular surface entrains loose grains once friction velocity u* exceeds a threshold u*t. Grains in saltation hop and impact-eject more grains, producing a near-equilibrium (saturated) sand flux q. The threshold and flux depend on grain size, particle density, atmospheric density and gravity: the canonical Bagnold scaling is q proportional to (rho_air/rho_sand) * u*^3 / g, with u*t set by grain diameter, rho_air, rho_sand, and g. The DIVERGENCE of this flux field deposits or erodes sediment: convergence builds bedforms (dunes), divergence and abrasion sculpt consolidated rock (yardangs), and differential deposition/scour of fine dust around obstacles paints albedo wind streaks. Dune planform is selected by the wind ROSE (directional distribution of drift potential, DP/RDP) combined with sediment availability: with abundant sand the bed-instability mode grows transverse/barchanoid ridges oriented to maximize gross bedform-normal transport; with a starved/non-erodible bed the fingering mode elongates linear dunes along the resultant drift direction (Gao/Narteau/Courrech du Pont). Slip faces stand at the material angle of repose (~30-34 deg), which is essentially gravity-independent. Fine material abraded from saltating grains and rock supplies a suspended dust budget that mantles surfaces (high-albedo bright streaks) and feeds atmospheric haze/storms. A frost/volatile gate is critical: ice-cemented regolith, frost mantles, or fully volatile-locked surfaces are not mobilizable, so aeolian work requires loose, dry, unconsolidated grains within a temperature/pressure window.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Sets rho_air; enters threshold u*t and flux q linearly (q ~ rho_air). Master gate: below a few mbar transport needs very high winds, but low gravity bodies (Triton/Pluto) still permit it. Scalar OK.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Gravity g sets u*t and flux (q ~ 1/g); lower g => easier transport, larger saltation hop length, taller dunes. Also dune/crater scale. Scalar OK.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Proxy for grain population: silicate sand vs organic/icy grains (Titan tholin sand, CO2/N2 ice grains). Drives rho_sand, cohesion/triboelectric stickiness, and color. Single scalar conflates density AND cohesion AND species - partially under-rich but workable as a steering scalar.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Rotation sets Coriolis/zonal wind regime, hence the WIND ROSE (directional drift distribution, bimodality, RDP/DP ratio) that selects dune orientation and bed-instability-vs-fingering mode. A scalar cannot carry a directional distribution or a seasonally-reversing bimodal regime; the actual wind-rose field is the true input and must be synthesized from D8+D3+D7 rather than supplied.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt
inputs.note: Obliquity drives seasonal Hadley reversal -> bimodal/obtuse wind regimes (Titan-style longitudinal dunes) and polar frost-mantle cycling that gates where sand is mobilizable. Scalar OK as a steering term but only as input to a synthesized wind-rose.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Tidal lock => fixed substellar->antistellar circulation, strong terminator winds and persistent unidirectional drift; reshapes the wind rose toward day-night transport. Scalar OK as steering term.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Frost/volatile gate: sets whether surface volatiles are frozen-cemented, frost-mantled, or absent; controls cohesion and whether grains are mobilizable. Scalar OK.

inputs.name: D16 age + D11 surfaceHistory
inputs.note: Time and resurfacing budget set how long winds have acted (yardang maturity, streak overprint, deflation-lag development, sediment supply exhaustion).

inputs.name: relief / slope field (DEM)
inputs.note: From tectonics/impact/volcanism tiers. Topography funnels flow (speed-up over ridges, lee wakes), provides obstacles for wind streaks, and supplies erodible lithology for yardangs. A field, supplied as the working heightmap - not a scalar.

inputs.name: lithology / induration field
inputs.note: Yardangs require CONSOLIDATED, erodibility-heterogeneous bedrock; differential erosion needs a hardness map. No current driver carries spatial induration; must be borrowed from the deposition history of upstream engines (lacustrine/volcanic/impact-melt layering).

inputs.name: loose-sediment supply / source patches
inputs.note: Sediment availability selects bed-instability vs fingering mode. This is a spatial supply field (where mobilizable grains exist - dry lakebeds, impact ejecta, weathered regolith) that no scalar carries; must be derived from upstream weathering/fluvial/impact outputs.

inputs.name: system-graph: insolation/season phase, ring-shadow, neighbor tides
inputs.note: Seasonal forcing of dune orientation (orbital forcing of Titan dunes) and tidal-locked stellar geometry come from the system graph (orbit, obliquity phase, primary). Currently the per-body pipeline does not receive the graph, so seasonal/orbital wind forcing cannot be carried.

outputs.name: sedimentFluxField
outputs.note: Vector saturated-flux field q(x) from local u*, threshold, rho_air, g; its divergence drives erosion(+)/deposition(-).

outputs.name: dustBudgetField
outputs.note: Scalar suspended/deposited fine-dust mass (abrasion product); feeds bright mantling, albedo, and haze/storm overlays.

outputs.name: sandCoverMask / bedformOrientationField
outputs.note: Where sand seas exist, plus local crest-orientation and mode (transverse vs linear) for the dune mesher/shader.

outputs.name: dunes
outputs.note: Barchan/transverse (bed-instability) or longitudinal/linear (fingering) bedforms with slip faces at ~30-34 deg repose.

outputs.name: yardangs
outputs.note: Streamlined wind-eroded ridges in consolidated, erodibility-heterogeneous material under unidirectional drift.

outputs.name: windStreaks
outputs.note: Bright depositional (dust in lee) and dark erosional/sand streaks downwind of craters/obstacles.

outputs.name: deflationLag / ventifact texture
outputs.note: Coarse lag surfaces and polished/faceted clasts where fines are stripped; an albedo+roughness overlay.

featureMap: Dune fields (barchan/transverse and longitudinal/linear)
Yardang ridge fields
Bright and dark wind streaks downwind of craters/hills
Dust mantles / high-albedo deposits and deflation-lag dark zones
Slip-face geometry (~30-34 deg) on dune lee sides
Sand-sea (erg) extent and inter-dune flats

cheapApprox.description: Run as a screen/texture-space pass per patch, no time-stepping. STEP 1 (closed-form gates): from D5,D14,D2 compute a scalar transportability T = clamp((rho_air/rho_sand)*u*^3/(g*u*t^3)) using a representative wind speed; from D1+D2 compute a frost/cohesion gate G in [0,1] (volatile-locked or frost-mantled => 0). Multiply by an upstream loose-sediment supply mask S. Activity A = T*G*S. STEP 2 (wind rose synthesis): build a small analytic directional weight set from D8 (zonal mean dir + Coriolis spread), D3 (add a second seasonal lobe => bimodality), D7 (bias to substellar->antistellar). Compute resultant drift dir RDP and bimodality ratio b. STEP 3 (mode select, closed-form per Gao/Narteau): if supply S high => bed-instability: lay anisotropic ridge noise (stretched gradient/Gabor noise) with crests oriented to maximize gross bedform-normal transport (roughly perpendicular to RDP for low b; oblique for high b); if S low => fingering: elongate ridge noise ALONG RDP (linear dunes). Dune wavelength ~ scale with hop length ~ 1/g and grain size. Clamp lee faces to repose angle in the displacement (analytic max-slope clamp), no relaxation needed. STEP 4 (streaks): for each obstacle in the relief field, paint an exponential-decay tail downwind along RDP; bright (dust deposit) where T low / dust budget high, dark (scour/sand) where T high. STEP 5 (yardangs): only where lithology/induration field is consolidated AND b low (unidirectional): carve grooves as anisotropic ridged-multifractal noise aligned to RDP, amplitude scaled by D16 age and abrasion = dustBudget*T. STEP 6 (dust mantle): deposit a smooth high-albedo layer scaled by (1-T)*dustBudget on low-slope, low-flux cells. All steps are noise + analytic clamps driven by the gate scalars and a synthesized wind rose; the ONLY borderline-offline element is true dune-field self-organization, which is replaced by mode-correct anisotropic noise (acceptable because the player reads orientation+morphology, not the transient evolution). A short bounded relaxation (5-20 iters) can optionally smooth flux divergence into deposition basins if budget allows -> hybrid.

epochBehavior.note: Aeolian is a late tier (T4) EDITOR: it overprints the surface left by tectonics, impacts, volcanism, and fluvial/weathering tiers. It fills existing craters and basins with sand (dune ponding), carves yardangs into previously deposited consolidated units (e.g. old lacustrine or ignimbrite layers), and paints streaks downwind of pre-existing crater rims/hills. Re-runs per epoch when the wind regime or sediment supply changes (e.g. obliquity excursion, atmosphere loss), each pass overprinting the prior surface; the final epoch's pass dominates what is visible.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current code likely hard-codes 'dune type' (barchan vs linear vs star) and 'has yardangs/streaks yes-no' by a discrete planet/biome TYPE, and applies a fixed slip-face look. Both should derive from continuous drivers/fields: dune morphology must emerge from (wind-rose bimodality b from D8/D3/D7) x (sediment-supply field S) via the bed-instability/fingering selection rule, not a type switch; yardang presence must require a consolidated, heterogeneous lithology field plus low-bimodality unidirectional drift, not a tag; streak brightness/direction must come from local transportability T and RDP, not a preset. Slip-face angle should read the material angle-of-repose (near-constant ~33 deg, gravity-independent) rather than a per-type constant, while dune WAVELENGTH/HEIGHT scale with gravity and grain size. 'Dust planet' look should be the (1-T)*dustBudget mantle output, not a discrete skin.
loadBearingClaims: Saltation flux scales as q ~ (rho_air/rho_sand)*u*^3/g, so D5 (atmoDensity) and D14 (gravity) can be folded into a single closed-form transportability scalar - the cube-power on u* and the simple density/gravity dependence make this a clean analytic gate rather than a simulation. (THEO/OBS)

Dune ORIENTATION and morphology (transverse vs linear) are selected by the wind-rose bimodality plus sediment availability via the bed-instability/fingering dichotomy, which can be reduced to a closed-form mode switch driving anisotropic noise - i.e. real dune self-organization need NOT be simulated to get the player-legible planform right. (SIM/OBS)

A single D8 rotation scalar cannot carry the directional wind-rose distribution that the orientation rule actually needs; synthesizing a plausible rose from D8+D3+D7 is an approximation that may mis-place dune orientation for unusual circulation regimes. (THEO)

Yardangs strictly require a consolidated, erodibility-heterogeneous lithology field that no current driver supplies; if induration is faked from a scalar, yardang placement will be physically arbitrary. (OBS)

The frost/volatile gate (D1+D2) cleanly suppresses aeolian work on ice-cemented/frost-mantled surfaces - but the boundary (partial cohesion, intermittent frost) is fuzzy and a hard scalar threshold may wrongly switch dune fields fully on/off near the gate. (THEO/SIM)

verdicts.claim: Saltation flux scales q ~ (rho_air/rho_sand)*u*^3/g, so D5 and D14 fold into a single closed-form transportability scalar; the cube-power and simple density/gravity dependence make this an analytic gate, not a simulation.
verdicts.reasoning: The Bagnold relation q = C_B (rho_air/g) u*^3 is confirmed (Wikipedia Bagnold formula; arxiv 1201.4353 'Physics of wind-blown sand and dust'). It is genuinely closed-form and algebraic, so folding D5/D14 into an analytic transportability scalar is legitimate and does NOT hide iteration. HOWEVER the claim is OVERSTATED in two ways: (a) modern consensus (Ho/Valance/Dur/Ould-Kaddour, Kok et al. 2012) favors the saturated-flux form q ~ (u*^2 - u*t^2) or q ~ u*(u*^2 - u*t^2)/g, NOT a pure cube of u*; the dossier's own cheapApprox actually writes u*^3/(g*u*t^3) which mixes the cube form with a threshold normalization. (b) rho_sand does not appear in the standard Bagnold q at all on the flux side - it enters only through u*t and the sqrt(d/D) grain term; writing q ~ (rho_air/rho_sand) directly is a non-canonical lumping. Net: cheapness/closed-form is TRUE and the load-bearing engineering conclusion stands; the specific algebraic form stated is a simplification bordering on mis-grounding, so the claim as literally written is partially overstated but not refuted on its core (the analytic-gate conclusion holds).

verdicts.claim: Dune orientation and morphology (transverse vs linear) are selected by wind-rose bimodality plus sediment availability via the bed-instability/fingering dichotomy, reducible to a closed-form mode switch driving anisotropic noise; real dune self-organization need NOT be simulated for the player-legible planform.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed against Courrech du Pont, Narteau & Gao 'Two modes for dune orientation' (Geology 2014) and the Nature Sci Rep / EPSL Olympia Undae phase-diagram work: bed-instability mode selects the orientation maximizing gross bedform-normal transport (transverse/barchanoid) under abundant supply; fingering mode elongates along the resultant flux (linear) under starved/non-erodible beds. The selection rule IS effectively closed-form given a wind rose and a supply value, so replacing the transient self-organizing simulation with mode-correct anisotropic noise is defensible for a still-frame, player-legible result. Caveat (not refuting): the rule outputs orientation and mode, not the actual emergent spacing/defect/sinuosity statistics or barchan-vs-transverse-vs-star distinction within a mode - those genuinely arise from self-organization. The dossier honestly flags this ('the ONLY borderline-offline element is true dune-field self-organization'). So the conclusion is sound.

verdicts.claim: A single D8 rotation scalar cannot carry the directional wind-rose distribution the orientation rule needs; synthesizing a rose from D8+D3+D7 is an approximation that may mis-place orientation for unusual circulation regimes.
verdicts.reasoning: This is structurally correct and is the dossier's most honest self-critique. A scalar is a single number; a wind rose is a directional probability distribution (DP/RDP, bimodality angle, seasonal reversal). The orientation rule (max gross bedform-normal transport) is a functional of the full distribution, so a scalar provably cannot carry it - confirmed by the Titan growth-mechanism paper (Narteau P36) and Gao 2014, where bimodality angle is the controlling variable. The synthesized-rose approach is admitted as approximate and flagged as likely to fail for non-canonical circulation (e.g. complex multi-modal monsoonal regimes, topographically steered local roses). No overstatement here; correctly marked underSupplied:true.

verdicts.claim: Yardangs strictly require a consolidated, erodibility-heterogeneous lithology field that no current driver supplies; faking induration from a scalar makes yardang placement physically arbitrary.
verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the yardang literature (Wikipedia Yardang; Geomorphology reviews): yardangs are streamlined ridges carved by abrasion/deflation into CONSOLIDATED but differentially-erodible bedrock (lacustrine, ignimbrite, playa, mudstone) under sustained unidirectional wind. Differential erosion requires a spatial hardness/induration contrast - a scalar cannot encode where hard caps vs soft units sit, so placement would be arbitrary. The dossier correctly marks lithology/induration underSupplied:true and proposes borrowing from upstream depositional history. Honest and correct.

verdicts.claim: The slip face stands at the material angle of repose (~30-34 deg) which is essentially gravity-independent; slip-face angle should read a near-constant ~33 deg gravity-independent repose rather than a per-type constant.
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED as stated. The 'essentially gravity-independent' assertion is the conventional textbook assumption but is contradicted by the modern experimental and theoretical literature the dossier sits adjacent to. Kleinhans et al. 2011 (JGR Planets 2011JE003865, a citation-neighbor of this very dossier) found in 33 parabolic-flight experiments that the STATIC angle of repose INCREASES and the DYNAMIC angle DECREASES under reduced gravity (0.1, 0.38, 1.0 g) - i.e. repose is demonstrably gravity-dependent, with static and dynamic angles diverging. PNAS 2021 ('An expression for the angle of repose of dry cohesive granular materials on Earth and in planetary environments', 2107965118) gives an explicit closed-form repose angle that depends on the Bond number / gravity-and-cohesion ratio, precisely because low-g raises the relative weight of inter-particle cohesion. The effect is modest for coarse dry sand at Mars/Earth g (so the engineering shortcut of clamping to ~33 deg is a tolerable VISUAL approximation), but the physical claim 'essentially gravity-independent' is false, and for low-g/cohesive bodies (Titan tholins, icy grains) the deviation is real. The dossier overstates a contested assumption as settled fact.

verdicts.claim: The frost/volatile gate (D1+D2) cleanly suppresses aeolian work on ice-cemented/frost-mantled surfaces, but the boundary (partial cohesion, intermittent frost) is fuzzy and a hard scalar threshold may wrongly switch dune fields fully on/off near the gate.
verdicts.reasoning: Physically sound and self-critical. Ice cementation and frost mantling raising cohesion and u*t (suppressing transport) is well established (Mars seasonal CO2 frost gating dune activity; Titan/Pluto/Triton volatile context per the icy-bodies sediment-transport work, xintingyu / arxiv 2203.00562). The admission that the gate is fuzzy (intermittent/seasonal frost, partial cohesion, triboelectric stickiness) and that a hard scalar threshold is a sharp approximation of a smooth transition is correct - this is a limitation honestly disclosed, not a false claim. The dossier proposes a [0,1] gate G which is the right softening. No refutation; the modeling realism is appropriately hedged.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The steered-noise cheapApprox is genuinely real-time WebGL feasible. Every numbered step is screen/texture-space, single-pass, and either (a) algebraic closed-form (Bagnold flux q, threshold u*t, transportability T, frost gate G, mode-select branch) or (b) procedural noise evaluated per-fragment (anisotropic Gabor/gradient ridge noise for dunes and yardangs, exponential-decay streak tails). None of these require time-stepping, per-pixel global solves, or unbounded relaxation. The physically-correct mappings (q closed-form, mode-switch from Gao/Narteau, repose clamp via analytic max-slope, exponential streak decay) all confirm as algebraic, so no hidden offline simulation. Two honest caveats, neither of which breaks real-time feasibility: (1) the dossier openly concedes the ONE borderline-offline element - true dune-field self-organization (transient pattern coarsening, defect dynamics, barchan/star differentiation) - is REPLACED by mode-correct anisotropic noise, not simulated; this is a legitimate fidelity-for-speed trade and is correctly disclosed rather than concealed. (2) The optional 'short bounded relaxation (5-20 iters)' for flux-divergence deposition basins is explicitly BOUNDED and gated on budget ('if budget allows -> hybrid'), so it does not smuggle in unbounded iterative relaxation; 5-20 fixed Jacobi/blur iterations over a patch texture is well within a WebGL frame/precompute budget. The costClass 'hybrid' label is accurate. The only real-world physics gotchas (q is better as u*(u*^2-u*t^2) than pure u*^3; repose is weakly gravity-dependent) affect numerical accuracy, not real-time feasibility - both refinements are still closed-form. Verdict: the cheap approximation is real, with no concealed offline sim or per-pixel global solve.

verify.notes: Scope: this was a physics/feasibility audit of the dossier text against the cited and adjacent literature; no codebase exists to inspect for this engine (the dossier describes a target design, and typeDemotionNote speculates about 'current code' without a repo to check). Strongest refutation: the 'angle of repose is essentially gravity-independent' claim is contradicted by Kleinhans 2011 (JGR Planets) and PNAS 2021 - it is gravity- and cohesion-dependent (static up, dynamic down in low-g); the ~33deg clamp survives only as a coarse visual shortcut, not as stated physics. Secondary overstatement: the flux law is presented as a clean cube q~u*^3 and lumps rho_sand into the flux prefactor, whereas modern consensus uses q~u*(u*^2-u*t^2) and rho_sand enters via the threshold, not the flux prefactor; the closed-form/cheap conclusion is unaffected. The four underSupplied flags (D8 wind rose, lithology/induration, sediment-supply field, system-graph seasonal forcing) are all correctly identified and are the dossier's most honest sections. The cheap approximation does NOT hide an offline simulation or unbounded relaxation - the one self-organizing element is openly swapped for anisotropic noise and the optional relaxation is explicitly bounded. Citations checked: Bagnold formula (Wikipedia; arxiv 1201.4353), Courrech du Pont/Narteau/Gao 'Two modes for dune orientation' (Geology 2014; Nature Sci Rep srep14677; EPSL Olympia Undae), Shao & Lu 2000 threshold u*t (JGR 2000JD900304), Kleinhans 2011 repose-vs-gravity (2011JE003865), PNAS 2021 repose expression (2107965118), Titan dune growth (Narteau P36), icy-bodies transport (arxiv 2203.00562).

engine.name: Cryosphere / volatile-ice
engine.brief: D1/D2/D3/D12 + relief + E3 stress-tensor -> ice-shell convection + sublimation + glacial mass-balance + frost cycle (gates E10) + cryotectonic resurfacing.

dossier.mechanism: Cryosphere / volatile-ice engine. Models the placement and surface expression of solid volatiles (H2O, CO2, N2, CO, CH4 ices) and their movement, governed by where each species can condense and stay frozen versus sublimate, plus how the resulting ice masses deform and resurface terrain. Four coupled physical sub-processes, each mapped to a real planetary regime: (1) FROST/CONDENSATION CYCLE — a volatile species is solid only where local surface temperature falls below its frost point at the body's pressure; this defines polar caps, cold traps, and a seasonal/obliquity-driven exchange between latitude reservoirs (Mars-type). On tidally-locked bodies the permanent nightside or sub-antistellar region becomes the cold trap and accumulates a thick grounded ice cap (eyeball-climate ice belt). (2) GLACIAL MASS-BALANCE / FLOW — accumulated ice flows under gravity from accumulation zones (cold) toward ablation zones (warm), filling basins (Pluto Sputnik-Planitia N2 glaciers flowing off uplands; nightside-to-dayside ice creep on locked worlds). Flow rate set by the species' rheology at local T (N2 ice at ~38 K flows like a terrestrial glacier; water ice is far stiffer). (3) ICE-SHELL SOLID-STATE CONVECTION — when a volatile-ice layer is thick and warm enough at its base (high effective Rayleigh number from tidal or radiogenic basal heat), it convects in the stagnant-lid regime, overturning and resurfacing the lid into polygonal cells (Sputnik-Planitia cells; Europa chaos/lenticulae). (4) CRYOTECTONIC RESURFACING / CRYOVOLCANISM — basal heat plus the E3 stress tensor fractures the brittle lid, producing double ridges, tiger-stripe fractures, bands, and cryovolcanic flooding that erases craters and resets terrain age. Together these decide which volatile is visible, where (caps/belts/basins), at what age, and with what tectonic overprint.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Master gate: sets which species' frost point can be met. Scalar mean temp is adequate for the gate but loses the SPATIAL temperature field (poles vs equator, day vs night) that actually places caps — see D3/D7 notes.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Total ice budget available to deposit; caps mass-balance so caps/glaciers don't exceed inventory.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt
inputs.note: Drives the latitudinal insolation pattern -> polar cap extent and the seasonal/obliquity volatile exchange (Mars PLD layering). Scalar tilt is fine; the engine needs to internally synthesize the insolation-vs-latitude curve from it.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Which volatile species exist to freeze out (CO2 vs N2 vs CH4 caps color/albedo differently). Scalar enum/mixture is workable but a single scalar can't carry a multi-species partial-pressure vector cleanly.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Pressure sets the frost-point temperature (Clausius-Clapeyron) and whether sublimation transport is even possible (no atmosphere -> no frost cycle, only direct sublimation/cold-trap). Load-bearing for cap placement.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Switches the cold-trap geometry from polar (rotating) to permanent-nightside / sub-antistellar (locked). Distinct visible regime (eyeball ice belt) — must be a hard branch.

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline. This is the single biggest gap: without it there is no Enceladus/Europa-grade ice-shell convection, no tiger stripes, no chaos terrain, no cryovolcanic resurfacing. The entire convection + cryotectonic sub-engine is dark until D12 is revived. Tag: dead driver.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets glacial flow driving stress, basin relaxation, and the Rayleigh number (g term) for shell convection vigor.

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Resurfacing budget integrates against age: young + active -> crater-free; old + inactive -> heavily cratered ancient ice.

inputs.name: relief / elevation field
inputs.note: From the relief/tectonic engine — needed to know basins (where ice pools) and uplands (accumulation, glacier source). A baked scalar heightfield is carriable.

inputs.name: E3 stress tensor field
inputs.note: Cryotectonic fracture orientation (double ridges, tiger stripes, bands) follows principal-stress directions. A TENSOR FIELD (orientation + magnitude per texel) cannot be carried by the scalar L0 interface; needs a 2- or 3-channel field handoff. Without it, fracture patterns are unsteered (random) rather than tidally/rotationally coherent.

inputs.name: system graph: tidal/resonance partners
inputs.note: D12's magnitude physically comes from orbital eccentricity forced by mean-motion resonances with siblings (Enceladus-Dione 2:1, Io-Europa-Ganymede Laplace). L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it per-body, so tidal heating cannot be derived from real orbital context — it would have to be a free scalar.

outputs.name: iceCoverMask
outputs.note: Per-texel which volatile species (if any) is surface ice — drives albedo, color (N2/CH4 reddish vs CO2/H2O bright), and specular/frost shading. Feeds renderer + gates E10.

outputs.name: capExtentField
outputs.note: Latitudinal (or nightside) ice fraction 0..1 with a diffuse frost margin; the seasonal/obliquity-banded polar cap.

outputs.name: glacialFlowField
outputs.note: Ice thickness + flow-direction hint in basins and valleys; informs smoothing/infill of relief and flowline streaks.

outputs.name: resurfacingAgeField
outputs.note: Local terrain-age multiplier where convection/cryovolcanism reset the surface (suppresses crater density from E-impacts).

outputs.name: terrainAgeGate
outputs.note: Output consumed by the cratering engine: crater-free cells where resurfacing budget > impact flux.

outputs.name: polar caps
outputs.note: Bright residual + seasonal caps; layered-deposit banding when D3 high.

outputs.name: nightside ice belt / eyeball cap
outputs.note: Locked-world (D7) grounded cold-trap ice on the dark/anti-stellar side.

outputs.name: convection cells / chaos / lenticulae
outputs.note: Polygonal cellular resurfacing texture (Sputnik cells, Europa chaos) — gated by D12.

outputs.name: double ridges / tiger stripes / bands
outputs.note: Cryotectonic lineaments oriented by E3 stress; gated by D12.

outputs.name: cryovolcanic plains
outputs.note: Smooth crater-erasing flooded units on a host patch.

cheapApprox.description: Five layered passes, all real-time, no offline sim. (1) FROST CAP — closed-form: for each candidate volatile species, compute its frost-point T_frost(D5) via a Clausius-Clapeyron constant pair; synthesize a surface-temperature proxy field T(lat, day/night) = D1 modulated by an insolation curve f(latitude, D3) for rotating bodies, or a substellar->antistellar cosine ramp gated by D7 for locked bodies; ice present where T<T_frost. Threshold with a smoothstep margin for the seasonal frost fringe; bind total ice area to D2 (mass conservation) so caps shrink on low-inventory worlds. Pure shader, per-texel. (2) GLACIAL INFILL — baked field / cheap relaxation: take the relief heightfield, run a bounded (4-16 iterations) screened-Poisson / grayscale-erosion 'fill' that pours the species-appropriate viscosity ice downhill into basins; viscosity-as-blur-radius scales with species and T (N2 floods broadly, H2O barely creeps). Output thickness + a cheap flowline gradient for streak texturing. (3) CONVECTION CELLS — steered procedural noise: where D12>threshold AND ice layer thick AND basal T high (effective Rayleigh proxy Ra ~ D12*D14*thickness^3 above a critical value), overlay a Voronoi/worley cellular pattern whose cell size = (boundary-layer-thickness scaling) ~ thickness * Ra^-0.25 from stagnant-lid Nu~Ra^0.20-0.26 laws; modulate medial-ridge/trough depth by vigor. No time-stepping — the SETTLED cell wavelength is a closed-form function of the same scaling. (4) CRYOTECTONIC LINEAMENTS — steered noise along E3 stress: trace ridge/stripe lineaments perpendicular to the local max-tension principal axis from the E3 tensor field (domain-warped ridged noise gated by tension magnitude); double-ridge cross-section is a fixed parametric profile stamped along the line. If E3 unavailable, fall back to tidal-pattern analytic stress (diurnal tidal stress field is itself closed-form from D7/eccentricity). (5) RESURFACING GATE — closed-form budget: resurfacingRate = g(D12, cryovolcanic flux) integrated vs D16*impactFlux; where rate wins, write crater-free age and stamp smooth cryovolcanic plains as an EDITOR over the host patch. Everything is per-texel analytic or <=16-iteration bounded relaxation — no PDE time integration, no multi-Myr loop.

epochBehavior.note: Runs per-epoch but principally as an EDITOR over earlier engines' output on a host patch: glacial infill smooths and floods the relief engine's basins; cryovolcanic plains and convection cells overwrite earlier terrain and ERASE the cratering engine's craters (resetting terrainAge); frost caps overlay albedo on whatever surface exists. In a multi-epoch run it re-evaluates each epoch as D1/D12/D16 evolve — e.g. an early warm tidally-heated epoch lays convective/cryovolcanic resurfacing, a later cold epoch deposits a static frost cap over it. The frost-cap and glacial passes can also run 'once' for a settled present-day snapshot when epochs aren't needed.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline almost certainly hard-codes cryosphere by discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'ice moon' -> always shows generic white ice; 'Pluto-like' -> reddish N2; 'Mars-like' -> polar caps) rather than deriving from drivers. The correct derivation: ice SPECIES and color emerge from D4 atmoComposition + which frost point D1/D5 actually meet (a hot body never shows N2; a CO2-atmosphere body shows CO2 caps); cap GEOMETRY emerges from D3 (polar) vs D7 (nightside) not from a 'tidally locked moon' flag; whether you get convection/chaos/tiger-stripes emerges from the continuous D12*D14*thickness Rayleigh proxy crossing a critical value, NOT from an 'active icy moon' boolean. Most damaging demotion: with D12 hard-zeroed, the engine likely fakes 'Europa-look' or 'Enceladus-look' as a static texture preset keyed to type, instead of producing it as the genuine output of basal-heat-driven convection + stress-steered fracture. Restore D12 and the E3 tensor and these features become emergent, letting an ARBITRARY driver combination (e.g. a high-iron, low-tilt, mildly tidally-heated CH4 world) produce a novel, never-preset cryosphere.

loadBearingClaims: [THEO/SIM] The settled convection-cell wavelength and the resurfacing vigor can be read off closed-form stagnant-lid scaling laws (Nu ~ Ra^0.20-0.26, cell/boundary-layer size ~ thickness*Ra^-~0.25) WITHOUT time-stepping the convection — i.e. we can place the SETTLED pattern directly. So a closed-form stamp can place a PLAUSIBLE cell field but cannot honestly guarantee the correct planform; the dossier's own risk note concedes exactly this. engine.name: Space-weathering / regolith-maturity
engine.brief: finished surface + D16 age + E4 flux -> nanophase-iron albedo/maturity field (sets & fades crater-ray brightness; lunar swirls = this masked by E4). Late, cumulative; acts as an EDITOR on the finished surface.

dossier.mechanism: Space weathering matures the optical surface of an airless (or thin-atmosphere) body by progressively accumulating nanophase metallic iron (npFe0) in the rims and rinds of regolith grains. Two coupled agents drive it: (1) micrometeoroid impact vaporization/melting, which deposits vapor-condensed npFe0 coatings and welds grains into agglutinitic glass, and (2) solar-wind H+ implantation + sputtering, which reduces FeO to npFe0 in grain rinds. Small npFe0 (less than ~40 nm) reddens the spectrum (reflectance rises toward longer wavelengths) and the whole population darkens albedo and suppresses diagnostic mineral absorption bands. The accumulated npFe0 budget IS the regolith maturity, quantified observationally by the Is/FeO ferromagnetic-resonance maturity index and by the multispectral OMAT optical-maturity parameter. Fresh material (recent crater ejecta, rays, steep slopes that shed regolith) is immature and bright/blue; as cumulative exposure age increases the surface converges to a dark, red 'background' maturity. The visible consequence is that bright crater rays and ejecta blankets fade and disappear, and any region locally shielded from the solar wind (a crustal magnetic anomaly) stays anomalously bright -- a lunar swirl. For airless silicate bodies maturity is npFe0-dominated; for icy/volatile-rich bodies the analogous editor is ion/UV radiolysis + photolysis of ice that reddens and (via embedded carbonaceous/tholin residue) darkens, with no npFe0.

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Sets cumulative-exposure budget; old surfaces saturate to background maturity, young ones retain immature contrast.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory (impact flux + resurfacing budget)
inputs.note: Micrometeoroid gardening rate AND it spawns the fresh-ejecta/ray features this engine then ages; resurfacing resets maturity locally.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Selects the maturation REGIME: hot silicate -> npFe0 path; cold volatile-rich -> radiolytic-ice path. Also gates whether ice is even present to weather.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Routes between silicate-npFe and icy-radiolysis maturity models (carbon/tholin darkening vs nanophase-iron darkening).

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: FeO available to convert to npFe0 sets the MAGNITUDE of darkening/reddening (the FeO denominator of Is/FeO); iron-poor crusts mature weakly.

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: A GLOBAL dipole reduces solar-wind flux to the surface (Mercury ~1/100 of lunar), shifting weathering toward micrometeoroid-dominated and slowing solar-wind maturation. But the scalar cannot encode the LOCALIZED crustal anomalies that actually make swirls.

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Weak second-order control on regolith retention/gardening depth and slope refresh; usable as a scalar.

inputs.name: crustal magnetic-anomaly field (spatial pattern)
inputs.note: Lunar swirls require a SPATIAL map of localized remanent-crust magnetic anomalies that stand off the solar wind. A single scalar D13 (global field strength) cannot carry this 2D pattern; it must come from a crust/impact-magnetization field, which the current pipeline does not produce or expose.

inputs.name: finished surface albedo/spectral field + feature mask (craters, rays, ejecta, slopes)
inputs.note: This engine is an EDITOR: it needs the host surface's albedo field plus a mask of fresh-vs-old surfaces (recent crater ejecta/rays, steep slopes) to know what to fade. If upstream only hands a finished color with no age/freshness channel, ray-fading cannot be targeted.

inputs.name: E4 micrometeoroid/impact flux field
inputs.note: Per-location gardening/flux that masks swirls and sets local maturation rate (the brief names E4 as the swirl mask). A spatial flux field, not a scalar.

inputs.name: heliocentric distance / stellar wind + dust environment
inputs.note: Dust flux scales ~a^-2 and solar-wind flux ~a^-2 with distance to the star; this sets ABSOLUTE maturation rate and the solar-wind-vs-micrometeoroid balance. The per-body scalar interface has no star-distance term, so rate must currently be faked from D1 instead of the real orbital geometry.

outputs.name: maturityField (M, 0=fresh..1=saturated)
outputs.note: Per-texel optical-maturity scalar; analog of OMAT/Is-FeO. Drives the albedo/spectral edit.

outputs.name: npFeAlbedoModifier
outputs.note: Multiplicative darkening + spectral-slope (reddening) tint and band-depth suppression applied to the host surface as a function of M and D9.

outputs.name: crater-ray / ejecta brightness fade
outputs.note: Bright immature rays set at crater-formation time, then exponentially relaxed toward background as M climbs.

outputs.name: lunar swirls
outputs.note: High-albedo immature filaments produced by masking the maturity edit wherever the magnetic-anomaly / E4 shielding mask is high (solar-wind standoff keeps regolith fresh).

outputs.name: slope/freshness brightening
outputs.note: Steep, recently-shed slopes and small fresh craters read as bright/immature against a dark mature background.

cheapApprox.description: BAKED FIELD + CLOSED-FORM, no time-stepping. (1) Background maturity from drivers, closed-form: M_bg = 1 - exp(-age_exposure / tau), where tau is a maturation timescale scaled by environment (faster nearer the star via ~a^-2 dust/solar-wind flux, slowed by a global magnetic field D13). Use D16 age + D11 flux to set effective cumulative exposure. (2) Freshness mask from the host surface: take the upstream crater/ejecta/slope feature mask; each crater carries a formation-age stamp f in [0,1]. Ray/ejecta local maturity M_local = lerp(M_fresh(0), M_bg, smoothstep over f) -- young craters keep bright immature rays, craters older than a saturation age (lunar analog ~0.8 Gyr, Copernicus) snap to background and vanish; ray maturation is tuned ~10-30x slower than flat-soil maturation so Tycho-age (~0.1 Gyr) rays survive. (3) Albedo edit, closed-form per texel: darken = mix(1.0, darkFactor(D9), M); reddening = add spectral slope ~ k*D9*M to the surface color (small npFe reddens, opaques darken); suppress band depth by (1-M). (4) Swirls: where shieldMask (baked magnetic-anomaly/E4 field) is high, clamp M downward -> bright filaments appear automatically; this is a single texture multiply. (5) Volatile branch: if D2 high / D1 low, swap the npFe darkening LUT for a radiolytic ice LUT (reddening + tholin-darkening, no iron term). Everything is a per-texel function of (M, masks, drivers): one extra full-screen/material pass over the already-finished surface. No relaxation loop is strictly required; an optional 1-2 iteration blur on the freshness mask softens ray edges. CRITICAL HONESTY: nothing here needs offline simulation -- the science gives closed-form scaling (exp saturation, a^-2 flux, Is/FeO magnitude from FeO), so it fits a real-time budget cleanly. The ONLY genuinely hard input is the spatial magnetic-anomaly map for swirls; that must be authored/baked upstream (e.g. from impact-antipode or random remanent patches), not derived from a scalar.

epochBehavior.note: Runs LAST, after the finished surface and all crater/ejecta/ray features exist. It edits that host surface: applies the global maturity darkening/reddening, fades crater rays per their formation age, and lifts albedo back up inside the magnetic-shield/E4 swirl mask. Naturally re-runs per epoch only to re-stamp ages of craters added in later epochs; the edit itself is a single deterministic pass, not iterative.

featureMap: Crater rays (bright immature ejecta filaments) and their fading/disappearance with age
Crater ejecta-blanket brightness halos
Lunar swirls (e.g. Reiner Gamma) -- bright filaments over magnetic anomalies
Global surface albedo darkening + spectral reddening of old vs young terrain
Suppression of mineral absorption-band contrast on mature surfaces
Bright fresh small craters and steep slopes against a dark mature background

(b) Swirls likely either absent or hand-placed by 'has swirls' boolean rather than emerging from a baked magnetic-shield mask * the maturity edit. (c) Darkening/reddening amount likely a per-body constant (or per planet-type 'rocky/icy' enum) instead of M * f(D9 ironFraction) for the silicate branch vs an ice-radiolysis LUT selected by D1/D2. (e) 'Background albedo' for old terrain likely a fixed value per type rather than the saturation limit of the maturity curve.
