[OBS/THEO]

Lunar swirls require a SPATIAL crustal-magnetic-anomaly field (solar-wind standoff), which a single scalar D13 cannot encode; without a baked anomaly map, swirls cannot be co-generated and must be authored. [OBS/SIM]

Maturation rate scales with environment: micrometeoroid dust flux and solar-wind flux both ~a^-2 in heliocentric distance, and a global magnetic field cuts surface solar-wind flux drastically (Mercury ~1/100 lunar), shifting the dominant agent to micrometeoroids -- the per-body scalar interface lacks star-distance, so absolute rate is currently underdetermined. [OBS/THEO]

Darkening vs reddening split is grain-size/npFe-size dependent (small npFe <~40 nm reddens + darkens VIS-NIR; larger opaques mainly darken) and magnitude tracks FeO (Is/FeO), so the albedo edit should scale with D9 ironFraction, not be a flat constant. [OBS/SIM]

Icy/volatile-rich bodies do NOT form npFe0; their maturity editor is radiolysis/photolysis of ice producing reddening + carbonaceous-residue darkening -- selecting the wrong branch from a 'rocky/icy' enum instead of D1/D2 would mis-color outer-system surfaces. [OBS/THEO]

verdicts.claim: Crater rays/ejecta fade to background optical maturity on a ~0.8 Gyr (Copernicus-saturation) timescale while flat mare soil matures far faster (~7 Myr cumulative exposure), so the engine MUST treat ray maturation and soil maturation as different rates, not one tau. [OBS/THEO]
verdicts.reasoning: PARTIALLY GROUNDED BUT OVERSTATED/MIS-MECHANISMED. Confirmed: optical-maturity saturation of large-crater ejecta occurs around the age of Copernicus (~800 Myr) and rays become indistinguishable from background for craters >~1 Gyr old (LROC/PSRD, Grier 2001). Confirmed: bulk soil optically matures fast — Tai Udovicic 2021 and Lucey 2000 frame optical maturation on Myr-to-sub-Gyr scales. HOWEVER the dossier's specific framing that 'ray maturation must be modeled as a SEPARATE rate ~10-30x slower than soil maturation' is not what the literature attributes the longevity to. The literature (Hawke et al. 2004, Grier 2001) explains long-lived bright rays primarily by a DIFFERENT mechanism: COMPOSITIONAL contrast (highland-albedo material excavated onto dark mare stays bright even AFTER full optical maturity), not by rays weathering at an intrinsically slower rate. Rays are a mix of 'immaturity rays' (fade with maturation) and 'compositional rays' (persist by albedo contrast); combination rays evolve INTO compositional rays. So the engine's premise that one body-specific tau with a 10-30x ray slowdown reproduces ray longevity conflates two physically distinct causes. The ~7 Myr figure is also a cumulative-exposure number the dossier itself hedges ('realized over Gyr via burial/re-exposure'), which is not a clean second tau. Refuted as a load-bearing mechanistic claim: ray persistence is dominantly compositional, not a slower maturation rate.

verdicts.claim: Lunar swirls require a SPATIAL crustal-magnetic-anomaly field (solar-wind standoff); a single scalar D13 cannot encode it; without a baked anomaly map swirls cannot be co-generated and must be authored. [OBS/SIM]
verdicts.reasoning: WELL GROUNDED. Multiple independent sources confirm swirls are co-located with localized crustal magnetic anomalies and are reproduced by solar-wind-standoff models (NASA/IMPACT 3D kinetic sims; Deca et al. 2018 Nature Comm Physics on Reiner Gamma; Nature Comm 2015). The mechanism is inherently a 2D spatial remanent-field pattern (mini-magnetosphere standing off solar-wind ions), which a global scalar field strength cannot represent. The dossier's input table and this claim correctly mark the spatial anomaly map as underSupplied and the only genuinely hard input. Not refuted. Minor caveat the dossier already acknowledges: 'all swirls have anomalies but not all anomalies have swirls,' so a baked anomaly map is necessary but not sufficient — the dossier does not overclaim sufficiency.

verdicts.claim: Maturation rate scales ~a^-2 with heliocentric distance for both dust and solar-wind flux, and a global magnetic field cuts surface solar-wind flux drastically (Mercury ~1/100 lunar), shifting the dominant agent to micrometeoroids and SLOWING solar-wind maturation; per-body scalar interface lacks star-distance so rate is underdetermined. [OBS/THEO]
verdicts.reasoning: CONTAINS A FACTUALLY WRONG NUMBER AND A BACKWARDS NET-EFFECT. The a^-2 flux scaling for solar-wind and near-Sun dust flux is supported (Altobelli 2019; solar-wind density falls ~r^-2). BUT the 'Mercury ~1/100 of lunar' solar-wind-to-surface figure is wrong: the literature (Mercury Space Science Reviews 2014; precipitation maps) gives Mercury receiving only ~3-5x FEWER protons than the Moon, NOT 100x — magnetospheric screening roughly offsets the higher solar-wind flux at 0.39 AU, it does not cut it 100-fold. More damaging: the claim's causal conclusion ('magnetic field slows maturation') is contradicted by the canonical test case. Braden & Robinson 2013 find Mercury's regolith optically matures ~2-4x FASTER than the Moon's (which is why Mercury has fewer rayed/Kuiperian craters), because micrometeoroid flux is ~5.5x higher and impact velocities higher. So a global magnetic field on a close-in iron body does NOT net-slow maturation — it shifts the agent to micrometeoroids which mature it faster. The dossier's typeDemotionNote (d) even bakes the wrong direction in ('a magnetized iron-rich body matures slower'). The qualitative 'rate is environment-dependent and the scalar interface lacks star-distance' part is valid, but the quantitative anchor and the sign of the magnetic-field term are refuted.

verdicts.claim: Darkening vs reddening split is grain-size/npFe-size dependent (small npFe <~40 nm reddens+darkens VIS-NIR, larger opaques mainly darken) and magnitude tracks FeO (Is/FeO), so the albedo edit should scale with D9 ironFraction, not a flat constant. [OBS/SIM]
verdicts.reasoning: WELL GROUNDED, with a minor threshold imprecision. Confirmed by space-weathering reviews (PMC5975224; Sci.gov nanophase-iron topics): small npFe0 (literature commonly cites <~10 nm, some <5 nm for strongest reddening) dramatically reddens VIS spectra; larger npFe0 (>~40 nm to microphase ~2 um) lowers albedo with little slope change (darkening). Is/FeO is the standard ferromagnetic-resonance maturity index with FeO as denominator, so darkening magnitude does track available iron. The dossier's '<~40 nm reddens' is slightly loose — the strong-reddening regime is more like <10-15 nm and 40-50 nm is the transition to darkening-dominant — but the structural claim (size-dependent split + FeO-scaled magnitude, demote flat constant to M*f(D9)) is correct. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Icy/volatile-rich bodies do NOT form npFe0; their maturity editor is radiolysis/photolysis of ice producing reddening + carbonaceous-residue (tholin) darkening; selecting the wrong branch from a rocky/icy enum instead of D1/D2 mis-colors outer-system surfaces. [OBS/THEO]
verdicts.reasoning: WELL GROUNDED. Radiolysis/photolysis of icy surfaces (Springer Space Science Reviews; reviews of icy-satellite weathering) is the recognized weathering pathway for volatile-rich outer-system bodies, producing reddening and organic/tholin darkening, with no nanophase-iron mechanism. Routing the branch on physical drivers (tempEq D1 / volatileFraction D2) rather than a coarse rocky/icy enum is a sound demotion. Not refuted. Caveat: real bodies can be mixed (e.g. carbonaceous/hydrated silicate asteroids weather differently again — bluing/brightening in some C-types), so a strict two-branch LUT is a simplification, but the claim as stated (npFe0 absent on icy bodies, radiolysis is the editor) is correct.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The cheap approximation IS genuinely real-time feasible and does NOT hide an offline sim, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. Audit of each step: (1) Background maturity M_bg = 1 - exp(-age/tau) is a per-texel closed-form scalar — no iteration. (2) Ray/ejecta freshness from a per-crater formation-age stamp f with smoothstep/lerp toward M_bg is a local table lookup per crater + per-texel blend — no coupling between texels. (3) Albedo edit (darken via mix, add k*D9*M spectral slope, suppress band depth by (1-M)) is a pure per-texel function — one full-screen/material pass. (4) Swirls = single texture multiply against a baked shield mask — trivially cheap. (5) Volatile branch = LUT swap selected by D1/D2 — a branch, not a solve. The only 'iteration' mentioned is an OPTIONAL 1-2 tap blur on the freshness mask, which is bounded and tiny. The genuinely hard input — the spatial magnetic-anomaly map — is honestly flagged as something that must be authored/baked upstream, NOT solved at runtime (the real science uses Pleiades-supercomputer kinetic plasma sims; the dossier correctly does NOT attempt that and instead bakes a proxy). So the runtime budget is one extra editor pass over the finished surface plus baked textures: legitimately a 'baked-field' cost class. The honesty disclaimer is accurate. The realism of the APPROXIMATION is sound even though some SCIENTIFIC parameters feeding it (the dual-tau ray rate, the Mercury 1/100 figure, the sign of the magnetic-field rate term) are wrong — those are calibration/grounding errors in the tau-scaling and ray model, not violations of the real-time budget. They will mis-color/mis-time outputs (e.g. magnetized iron bodies wrongly mature slower, ray persistence attributed to slow weathering rather than compositional contrast) but they do not make the method non-real-time.

verify.notes: Three of five load-bearing claims survive scrutiny (swirls-need-spatial-map, grain-size/FeO albedo split, icy-radiolysis branch) and are well cited. Two are refuted: (claim 1) the ray-vs-soil 'dual tau, rays 10-30x slower' mechanism mis-attributes long-lived bright rays — the literature (Hawke 2004, Grier 2001) explains persistent rays primarily by COMPOSITIONAL albedo contrast (highland material on mare), with rays being a mix of immaturity rays (fade) and compositional rays (persist after full maturity); a slower ray maturation RATE is not the dominant cause. The engine would arguably model ray persistence better by carrying a per-crater compositional-contrast flag in addition to/instead of a ray-specific tau. (claim 3) two concrete errors: 'Mercury ~1/100 lunar solar wind' is wrong (actual ~3-5x fewer protons), and the net causal direction is backwards — Braden & Robinson 2013 show Mercury matures ~2-4x FASTER than the Moon despite its magnetosphere, driven by ~5.5x higher and faster micrometeoroid impacts; the dossier's typeDemotionNote (d) hard-codes the wrong sign ('magnetized iron-rich body matures slower'). a^-2 flux scaling itself is fine. The cheap approximation is legitimately real-time (baked field + closed-form per-texel editor pass; no hidden offline solve at runtime — the one truly hard input, the spatial magnetic-anomaly map, is honestly deferred to baking/authoring). Net: architecture and cost-class are sound; the SCIENCE CALIBRATION has two refuted load-bearing errors that would produce wrong-but-cheap outputs. Key sources: PSRD/LROC (Copernicus ~0.8 Gyr), Hawke et al. 2004 Icarus (compositional vs immaturity rays), Braden & Robinson 2013 JGR (Mercury matures 2-4x faster), Mercury Space Sci Rev 2014 (proton flux ~3-5x fewer, micrometeoroid ~5.5x higher), Deca et al. 2018 / NASA IMPACT (swirl standoff), PMC5975224 + Sci.gov (npFe0 grain-size optics), Springer SSR (icy radiolysis).

engine.name: Surface-chemistry palette
engine.brief: composition + irradiation(E4) + T + all surface fields -> body-wide hue/palette field. Terminal coherence overlay.

dossier.mechanism: Surface-chemistry palette: the body-wide hue / albedo / spectral-slope field the surface presents to the eye, set by which mineral/ice/organic endmembers are exposed and how irradiation and temperature have chemically processed them. The engine models four well-separated real coloration regimes and blends them per-surface-patch by areal fraction (the Hu/Ehlmann/Seager "areal mixing of endmember albedos" approach). (1) SILICATE/ROCK base color from mineralogy + oxidation state: feldspathic surfaces are bright and spectrally flat (geometric albedo ~0.6), basaltic / Fe-oxidized / metal-rich surfaces are dark (albedo <0.3); iron-oxidation chemistry produces Mars-type reddening through nanophase / poorly-crystalline ferric oxides (hematite alpha-Fe2O3, goethite alpha-FeOOH, ferrihydrite), where hydration state (oxyhydroxide vs anhydrous oxide) shifts hue from yellow-brown toward deep red. (2) SPACE-WEATHERING optical maturation on airless / thin-atmosphere bodies: micrometeorite vaporization + solar-wind sputtering deposit submicroscopic reduced metallic iron (npFe0) that darkens albedo, reddens the visible-NIR spectral slope, and suppresses absorption-band depth as a monotonic function of exposure age x flux. (3) ICY/ORGANIC bodies: high-albedo H2O/CO2/NH3 frost (snow ~0.95, basalt glass ~0.09) progressively reddened/darkened by radiolysis-photolysis of C+N ices into tholins, and by sulfur / salt ion implantation (Europa-type) -- UV reddening that correlates with orbital irradiation dose. (4) CARBON-planet surfaces (C/O > ~0.8): graphite / silicon-carbide darkening with near-zero water signature. The terminal output is one coherent HSV + spectral-slope field that ties every upstream geomorphic feature into a single chemically-plausible color story, including temperature-keyed coloration such as Io-type sulfur allotrope hue (yellow toward red as warmer S3/S4/S5 species and chalcophile impurities increase).

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Master gate: frost stability vs rock; sulfur-allotrope hue temperature keying; magma/lava-world dark glass at high T.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Ice/frost areal budget; sets how much of the palette is high-albedo volatile vs silicate.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Haze/tholin species + whether ferric-oxide oxidation pathway is even available (O-bearing); also sky-coupling for terminal coherence.

inputs.name: D6 atmoRetention
inputs.note: Airless vs blanketed: gates space-weathering optical maturation (npFe0) vs atmospheric chemical weathering.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: Available Fe for both ferric-oxide reddening and npFe0 maturation; mineralogy darkening.

inputs.name: D10 carbonToOxygen
inputs.note: C/O>~0.8 flips silicate palette to graphite/SiC carbon-planet darkening; also competes with ferric oxidation for oxygen.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory
inputs.note: Impact flux x resurfacing -> exposure age proxy for optical maturation; fresh vs mature contrast (rays, young craters).

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: Shields surface from solar-wind/charged-particle dose -> modulates space-weathering rate and radiolytic tholin/sulfur reddening.

inputs.name: D16 age

inputs.name: D12 tidalHeating
inputs.note: Drives Io-grade sulfur volcanism and cryo resurfacing -> the sulfur/cryo palette. Hard-zeroed in current pipeline, so the entire tidally-heated coloration regime is dead; underSupplied as a live signal.

inputs.name: E4 irradiation field
inputs.note: Per-patch UV + charged-particle dose map (substellar peak, terminator falloff, pole shielding, magnetic geometry). A scalar driver cannot carry a spatial dose field; needs a real 2D/3D field from E4.

inputs.note: Latitude/illumination-resolved T (not just D1 scalar) needed for frost line on the body, eyeball substellar melt, and sulfur hue gradients.

outputs.name: hueSaturationValue

outputs.name: ferricOxidationField

Mars-type red/ochre oxidized terrain

Icy-body reddish tholin staining and bright/dark hemispheric color dichotomy

Lava-world dark glassy low-albedo surfaces
Terminal tonal coherence across all D/P/F geomorphic features

cheapApprox.description: Two-stage real-time pipeline. STAGE A (per-body, once/per-epoch): build a small palette LUT by AREAL MIXING of a fixed library of measured endmember reflectances (feldspathic ~0.6 flat; basalt glass ~0.09; Fe-oxidized red ramp hematite->goethite->ferrihydrite; H2O/CO2 frost ~0.9; tholin red-brown; graphite/SiC dark; sulfur yellow->red ramp; SO2 frost white). Endmember weights are closed-form sigmoids/ramps of the scalar drivers: ice fraction = smoothstep on (D2, D1 vs frost temp); ferric reddening = D9 x oxygen-availability(D4, 1-D10) x weathering-time(D16); carbon flip = smoothstep(D10 around 0.8); maturity = 1-exp(-k*exposure) with exposure = D11 x dose, dose = airless(D6) x (1-D13 shielding) x D16. Maturation applies the empirical triple effect as a transfer function: lower V (darken), increase spectral-slope (redden), reduce band contrast (desaturate diagnostic features). STAGE B (per-fragment shader): sample the LUT/ramps, then steer with cheap procedural noise (FBM) masked by upstream feature fields to place provinces (sulfur flows around volcanic vents, tholin concentration toward irradiated hemisphere, frost toward poles/cold), and apply an irradiation-dose gradient from a baked E4 dose map (substellar-hot / terminator / pole). Sulfur hue is a closed-form temperature->hue ramp. Final compositing of HSV + slope is the terminal coherence overlay. No offline simulation required; the only thing that MUST be precomputed offline is the endmember reflectance library itself (a static asset, measured in the literature), and a small per-body dose/temperature texture if E4 supplies one.

epochBehavior.note: Re-runs as the terminal overlay after each epoch's geomorphic/volcanic edits so the palette reflects the latest exposed surface (e.g. fresh lava re-darkens, then matures; new impacts expose bright fresh material). Within an epoch it behaves as an editor-on-host over the existing surface fields: it recolors them rather than creating geometry.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: High demotion risk. Current code almost certainly assigns palette by a discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'Mars-like'->red LUT, 'moon'->grey, 'ice'->white, 'lava'->black, 'Io'->yellow). These should instead emerge: red is not a type but D9 x oxygen-availability(D4,1-D10) x time(D16); grey-and-dark is maturity = f(airless D6, exposure D11, shielding 1-D13, age D16); white is frost = f(D2, T<frost); black is either basalt mineralogy, magma at high D1, OR carbon-planet at D10>0.8 -- three different physical causes that a 'lava type' collapses into one. Sulfur yellow/red must be a temperature/allotrope ramp gated by tidal-heating-driven volcanism, not an 'Io' flag. Tholin reddening must be dose-driven (E4 + orbital context), not an 'outer icy moon' flag.
loadBearingClaims: Areal mixing of a small fixed library of measured endmember albedos (Hu/Ehlmann/Seager 2012) is a sufficient real-time palette model -- i.e. surface color is well-approximated by linear-area blends of bright-feldspathic / dark-basaltic / red-ferric / white-frost / dark-carbon / sulfur endmembers, with nonlinear intimate-mixing corrections (dust-on-ice darkening, opposition effects) folded into ramp shaping rather than full radiative transfer. Most likely wrong in the nonlinearity: tiny dust fractions darken ice by 10x, which a naive linear blend gets badly wrong.

Space-weathering optical maturation is reducible to a monotonic exposure parameter (1-exp(-k*exposure)) driving the empirically-observed triple effect (darken + redden + band-suppress). The rate constant k and the airless/atmosphere gating (D6) are the fragile part; maturation rate also depends on composition (FeO content) which the scalar D9 may not capture faithfully.

Per-patch irradiation dose (substellar peak, terminator falloff, pole/magnetic shielding) is required for correct tholin/sulfur/salt province placement and CANNOT be carried by any L0 scalar -- it needs E4 to emit a real spatial field. If E4 only hands a scalar, the irradiation-keyed coloration collapses to a uniform tint and the eyeball-planet color asymmetry is lost.

The entire tidally-heated coloration regime (Io sulfur volcanism, cryo resurfacing color) is currently DEAD because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed in the pipeline; reviving Io/Enceladus/Europa-class palettes requires un-zeroing D12 (or sourcing tidal heating from the system graph), not just a palette tweak.

Ferric-oxide hue is governed by oxidation state AND hydration (anhydrous hematite deep-red vs hydrated goethite/ferrihydrite yellow-brown), and the dominant Martian phase may be ferrihydrite (cold-wet origin) rather than hematite -- so a single 'rust red' constant is an oversimplification; hue should shift with available water/atmo history, which the scalar interface may not resolve.

verdicts.claim: Areal mixing of a small fixed library of measured endmember albedos (Hu/Ehlmann/Seager 2012) is a sufficient real-time palette model, with intimate-mixing nonlinearities folded into ramp shaping rather than radiative transfer.
verdicts.reasoning: Hu, Ehlmann & Seager 2012 (ApJ 752:7) is a real paper and does treat terrestrial-exoplanet surface spectra via mixtures of measured endmembers. Areal (macroscopic/geographic) mixing IS approximately linear in reflectance — confirmed by the spectral-unmixing literature ('several areal scenes can be accurately unmixed by the linear mixing model'). The claim is NOT refuted as a real-time MODEL choice. BUT the dossier's own hedge is correct and important: intimate (grain-scale) mixing is nonlinear — it is linear only in single-scattering albedo after a Hapke reflectance<->albedo transform, and naive linear unmixing of intimate mixtures yields >30% abundance errors. Dust-on-ice darkening (a tiny dark fraction disproportionately darkens bright ice) is a real, strongly nonlinear effect confirmed in snow-albedo radiative-transfer work. The '10x darkening from tiny dust' figure is on the dramatic end (literature shows large but grain-size/geometry-dependent reductions, not a universal 10x), so that specific multiplier is overstated. Net: the model is sound and the limitation is honestly disclosed; only the magnitude of the dust-on-ice multiplier is slightly inflated.

verdicts.claim: Space-weathering optical maturation reduces to a monotonic exposure parameter (1-exp(-k*exposure)) driving the empirical triple effect (darken + redden + band-suppress).
verdicts.reasoning: The triple effect (albedo reduction, VIS-NIR reddening/spectral-slope increase, absorption-band suppression) driven by submicroscopic npFe0 is firmly established for the Moon, Mercury, and asteroids. A saturating exposure law is a reasonable first-order capture. The dossier correctly flags the fragile parts. One important nuance the literature adds that strengthens the caveat: maturation is NOT cleanly monotonic in a single parameter — SMALL nanophase iron (<~40 nm) darkens AND reddens, while LARGER microphase iron (40 nm-2 um, dominant at high maturity) darkens WITHOUT reddening. So reddening can saturate and even roll over while darkening continues. A single 1-exp(-k*x) curve coupling all three effects is therefore an approximation, but a defensible real-time one. Rate constant k and FeO-content (D9) dependence are genuine weaknesses, as stated. Claim stands.

verdicts.claim: Per-patch irradiation dose (substellar peak, terminator falloff, pole/magnetic shielding) is required for correct tholin/sulfur/salt province placement and cannot be carried by an L0 scalar — it needs E4 to emit a real spatial field.
verdicts.reasoning: Strongly supported. Europa's trailing hemisphere is measurably darker/redder than the leading hemisphere in a 'bull's-eye' centered on the trailing apex where magnetospheric flux peaks; individual lineae shift red->yellow as they cross hemispheres. This is an intrinsically spatial, dose-driven pattern that a single scalar cannot represent. The architectural claim — collapse to uniform tint and loss of eyeball-planet asymmetry if only a scalar is supplied — is a correct and honest engineering consequence, not an overstatement.

verdicts.claim: The entire tidally-heated coloration regime (Io sulfur volcanism, cryo color) is dead because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed; reviving it requires un-zeroing D12, not a palette tweak.
verdicts.reasoning: The physics half is solid: Io's yellow->orange->red coloration is driven by temperature-keyed sulfur allotropes (S3/S4/S5 concentrations rising with melt temperature, quenched on the cold surface, slowly relaxing to yellow S8 under magnetospheric radiation) — confirmed. So sulfur/cryo palettes genuinely depend on tidal-heating-driven volcanism. The 'hard-zeroed in current pipeline' part is a claim about the engine's own code state that I cannot independently verify from the dossier alone; I take it as the author's accurate report of pipeline state. Conditional on that being true, the conclusion (revival needs the upstream signal, not a cosmetic palette change) follows. Marked not-refuted but medium confidence because the code-state premise is unverifiable here.

verdicts.claim: Ferric-oxide hue depends on oxidation state AND hydration; the dominant Martian phase may be ferrihydrite (cold-wet origin) not anhydrous hematite, so a single 'rust red' constant oversimplifies.
verdicts.reasoning: Directly confirmed by Valantinas et al. 2025 (Nature Communications 16:1712): poorly crystalline ferrihydrite, not anhydrous hematite, is the best-fit dominant ferric phase in Martian dust, recording ancient cold-wet conditions. Hydration state shifting hue (anhydrous hematite deep red vs hydrated goethite/ferrihydrite yellow-brown) is standard iron-oxide mineralogy. A single rust-red constant is therefore genuinely an oversimplification. Claim fully supported.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time feasible and does NOT hide an offline simulation, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. Inspecting the pipeline: STAGE A builds a small per-body palette LUT from CLOSED-FORM sigmoid/ramp/smoothstep functions of scalar drivers (ice = smoothstep on D2/D1; ferric = D9 x oxygen-avail x time; carbon flip = smoothstep(D10~0.8); maturity = 1-exp(-k*exposure)) combined with linear areal mixing of a STATIC, measured endmember reflectance library. Every operation is O(endmembers) per body — no iteration, no convergence loop, no coupling between patches. STAGE B is a standard fragment shader: LUT/ramp sample + FBM procedural noise masked by upstream feature fields + a sampled baked dose-map gradient + a closed-form temperature->hue sulfur ramp. This is textbook procedural surface shading — clearly within a WebGL frame budget. The only mandatory offline artifact is the endmember library itself, which is correctly identified as a static measured asset (not a simulation run per-frame or per-body). HONEST LIMITATIONS, not hidden solves: (1) Linear areal mixing sacrifices physical accuracy for intimate (grain-scale) mixtures — dust-on-ice darkening and opposition effects are nonlinear and would require a Hapke single-scattering-albedo transform for fidelity; the dossier folds these into 'ramp shaping,' which trades accuracy, not feasibility, and is openly flagged. (2) Five inputs are underSupplied (E4 spatial dose field, compositional endmember field, surface-temperature field, host-star SED, orbital/magnetospheric dose, plus hard-zeroed D12). WITHOUT real upstream spatial fields, the spatially-resolved coloration (eyeball-planet asymmetry, trailing-hemisphere reddening, sulfur provinces) collapses to uniform tints. This is a data-availability dependency, correctly disclosed, not a concealed real-time cost. The 'baked E4 dose map' is the right move — it pushes any expensive dose computation offline/per-epoch into a texture the shader merely samples. Conclusion: the cheap approximation is honestly real-time; its weaknesses are accuracy and upstream-data dependencies, both explicitly stated, not smuggled iteration.

verify.notes: Attempted to refute each load-bearing claim; none refuted. The dossier is unusually self-honest — its own loadBearingClaims pre-emptively flag the genuine weaknesses (intimate-mixing nonlinearity, non-monotonic maturation, scalar-vs-spatial dose interface, single-rust-red oversimplification, D12 hard-zero). Independent literature checks confirmed all five physical regimes and their drivers: Hu/Ehlmann/Seager 2012 (real paper, areal mixing ~linear in reflectance per unmixing literature); npFe0 triple effect (real, but small-vs-large iron particle distinction means reddening is not strictly monotonic — strengthens the dossier's own caveat); Europa trailing-hemisphere dose-driven reddening (real, spatial); Io sulfur allotrope temperature keying (real); Valantinas et al. 2025 Nature Comms ferrihydrite-over-hematite (real, directly on point). The only OVERSTATEMENT found is minor: the 'tiny dust fractions darken ice by 10x' multiplier is on the dramatic end — real-world snow/ice albedo reductions from dust are large and nonlinear but grain-size/geometry-dependent, not a universal 10x. The D12 'hard-zeroed in current pipeline' premise is a code-state claim unverifiable from the dossier alone; conditional on it being accurate, the conclusion holds (medium confidence on that one item only). Cheap approximation is genuinely real-time; no hidden offline sim or per-pixel global solve. Grounding tags (OBS/SIM/THEO/SF) and citation set are appropriate — citations resolve to real, on-topic sources.

engine.name: Temporal / transient
engine.brief: D3/D1 + frost+dust+ice+ring states -> seasonal / time-varying overlay (recurring slope lineae, frost flush, dust-clearing, ring spokes).

dossier.mechanism: E13 models recurring, time-varying surface/ring overlays produced by the seasonal cycling of volatiles and dust driven by insolation. The core physical chain: a planet's obliquity (D3) plus its orbital position modulates insolation by latitude and time-of-year; where surface temperature crosses a volatile's condensation/sublimation threshold, frost (CO2 or H2O) deposits in autumn/winter and flushes (sublimes) in spring, producing a waxing/waning seasonal cap and a moving "defrosting front." Four concrete real-world processes are reproduced: (1) Recurring slope lineae (RSL) -- dark streaks on warm, equator-facing slopes that lengthen during the warm season and fade in the cold season, driven either by deliquescent brine/perchlorate hydration or by rarefied-gas-triggered dry granular flow when slope temperatures rise above a threshold; the warm-season onset is the diagnostic. (2) Seasonal frost flush -- the latitude-dependent appearance and retreat of a bright CO2/H2O frost cap, including spring sublimation jets that drive Kieffer-model basal sublimation, depositing dark dust fans/spots and (over many years) carving araneiform "spider" channels. (3) Dust-clearing / global dust storms -- seasonal dust lifting (peaking in the dusty season) that raises atmospheric opacity, masks the surface, then decays as the boundary layer stabilizes; deposition/removal episodes leave discrete albedo darkenings and gradual brightenings (streaks, fans, redistributed dust mantles). (4) Ring spokes -- transient radial dust features on a ring system formed by electrostatic levitation of micron dust off ring particles, modulated by the magnetosphere/solar-wind interaction and peaking near the planet's equinox when sunlight strikes the rings edge-on. All four are periodic functions of orbital phase (a "season clock") gated by driver thresholds, which is exactly what makes them cheap to fake without time-stepping.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt (obliquity)
inputs.note: Master seasonal driver: sets the latitude/amplitude of the insolation swing that gates frost deposition, RSL warm-season onset, and cap waxing.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Baseline equilibrium temp; combined with the seasonal insolation modulation decides whether the surface crosses a volatile condensation/sublimation threshold at all.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction
inputs.note: Frost/ice budget available to deposit as a seasonal cap and to flush.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Selects frost species (CO2 vs H2O vs none) and condensation point; also brine salt chemistry plausibility for RSL deliquescence.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Gates dust lifting/storms and the rarefied-gas RSL granular-flow mechanism; thin-but-present atmosphere is required for both.

inputs.name: orbital phase / season clock (true anomaly + time)
inputs.note: E13 is fundamentally a function of WHERE the body is in its orbit and a running time parameter. The L0 16-scalar vector carries no orbital phase, eccentricity, or animation time; a scalar cannot hold the per-frame/per-epoch phase the engine modulates against. This is the central under-supply.

inputs.name: orbital eccentricity + argument of perihelion
inputs.note: Drives hemispheric asymmetry (e.g. longer/colder aphelion-winter -> thicker cap in one hemisphere) and perihelion dust-storm seasonality. No scalar in D1-D16 carries it.

inputs.name: slope/aspect field (local terrain incidence)
inputs.note: RSL form on specific warm equator-facing slopes; needs a per-texel slope+aspect field from the terrain/tectonics engine (E-erosion/E-tectonic host). A driver scalar cannot carry a spatial field; must be read from the host heightfield at shade time.

inputs.name: host crater/araneiform substrate (editor target)
inputs.note: Frost jets carve spiders into existing polar deposits; spokes need an existing ring field. These are spatial fields/features from upstream engines, not scalars.

inputs.name: ring system presence + radial structure
inputs.note: Spokes require a ring; the per-system graph (rings/resonances) exists at L0 but is NOT exposed to the per-body pipeline, so the body cannot currently know it has rings.

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: Ring-spoke electrostatic levitation is modulated by the magnetosphere/solar-wind interaction; D13 gates spoke contrast/abundance.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: If tidally locked there is no diurnal/seasonal insolation sweep in the normal sense -> seasonal overlay degenerates to a fixed terminator/substellar pattern, not a moving season. E13 must branch on this.

outputs.name: seasonalFrostMask
outputs.note: Per-texel 0-1 frost coverage as a function of latitude + season clock; bright cap that waxes/wanes. Drives albedo + color toward frost species.

outputs.name: defrostFrontFans
outputs.note: Dark dust fans/spots and streaks deposited at the sublimation front (Kieffer jets); seasonally appearing dark splotches over a bright cap.

outputs.name: rslStreakField
outputs.note: Dark downslope lineae on warm equator-facing slopes, length/opacity animated by warm-season phase; fade in cold season.

outputs.name: dustOpacity+ dustStreaks
outputs.note: Time-varying atmospheric opacity (global-dust-storm masking) plus surface albedo darkening/brightening streaks and fan deposits from dust clearing/redeposition.

outputs.name: araneiformChannels
outputs.note: Dendritic 'spider' channel network etched into polar substrate by repeated jet venting (editor output baked into the host over epochs).

outputs.name: ringSpokeField
outputs.note: Radial dust spokes on the ring, contrast modulated by equinox phase + D13; short-lived, rotate near-synchronously with the magnetosphere.

Seasonal polar frost cap (waxing/waning bright cap)

Dust-clearing albedo streaks and fan deposits
Saturn-style ring spokes

cheapApprox.description: Drive everything off a single scalar 'season clock' s in [0,1) (orbital phase) supplied per frame/per epoch, plus a few drivers. (1) Frost mask: closed-form latitude band. coverage(lat,s) = smoothstep over a frost-line latitude that breathes with season: capEdgeLat = baseLat - amp*cos(2*pi*(s - phaseHemi)), where amp scales with D3 (obliquity) and baseLat with D1/D2; multiply by a worley/fbm jitter so the cap edge is ragged, not a clean circle. Pole offset and amp asymmetry come from eccentricity (if available) else a small fixed bias. (2) Defrost fans: where d(coverage)/ds < 0 (subliming front) AND slope>threshold, stamp dark fan sprites oriented downslope using a hash-seeded blue-noise point set; opacity = front activity. (3) RSL: a precomputed slope+aspect field (from host heightfield, dFdx/dFdy of height) selects warm equator-facing facets; streak length L = warmSeasonGate(s, tempEq, slopeTemp) animated as a 1D growth curve along the downslope direction; render as thin darkening with fbm edge noise; gate entire feature off D5>0 and tempEq in a warm band. (4) Dust opacity: a single time curve opacity(s) peaking in 'dusty season' window, scaled by D5; modulates a global haze term + temporarily lifts surface contrast; leave a baked low-frequency albedo-change mask that persists after the storm (editor write). (5) Ring spokes: in the ring shader, radial wedge function spoke(theta,r,s) = thresholded fbm in (theta - omega*t) advected angle, amplitude = bell(s near equinox) * D13; spokes fade over ~2-3 ring rotations via a decaying phase term. All six are analytic-or-noise, zero iteration. The ONLY thing that resembles simulation -- araneiform channel carving by repeated jets -- is NOT simulated at runtime: bake it once as a relaxation/L-system dendrite pattern stamped where the defrost-fan density integrated over many seasons is highest, then treat it as static terrain. Honest caveat: a physically faithful global-dust-storm spatial evolution and true brine percolation ARE offline GCM/diffusion problems; we deliberately replace them with a phase-curve + baked mask, which reproduces the LOOK (seasonal opacity rise, albedo streaks) but not the dynamics.

epochBehavior.note: Two roles. (a) Per-FRAME/animated overlay: the frost mask, RSL streak length, dust opacity, and ring spokes are cheap shader terms recomputed live against the season clock s -- this is the 'transient' (T5) character. (b) Editor-on-host bakes: the araneiform spider channels are written into the existing polar terrain produced by the erosion/tectonic engines (carving dendritic channels where integrated jet activity is high), and global-dust-storm episodes write a persistent low-frequency albedo-change mask onto the surface produced by upstream engines. Spokes edit the existing ring field from the system graph. So E13 runs last in the tier stack, reads earlier engines' surfaces/heightfields as host patches, and both (a) animates an overlay and (b) leaves permanent edits.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current code very likely hard-codes 'this is a Mars-type body -> draw RSL + a CO2 cap + dust storms' and 'this is a Saturn-type -> draw ring spokes' by discrete archetype. These should instead derive from drivers: frost species and cap from D4 (composition) + D1/D2 thresholds, not a 'Mars' flag; RSL gated by (D5>0) AND (warm-season slope temp crossing) AND a real slope/aspect field, not by planet type; ring spokes gated by ring-presence (system graph) AND D13 magnetic field AND equinox phase, so a strongly-magnetized ringed body of ANY type gets spokes and a weakly-magnetized one does not. The cap-hemisphere asymmetry should come from eccentricity/argument-of-perihelion, not a baked 'south cap bigger' constant. Frost-flush jets/fans should fire wherever the sublimation front passes over loose substrate, not only at a hard-coded polar latitude.
loadBearingClaims: RSL formation mechanism is genuinely unresolved (dry rarefied-gas granular flow vs. brine/aquifer-melt water activity); the engine's choice of mechanism affects which drivers gate it (D5 atmo for dry flow vs. D2/D4 brine chemistry for wet) -- picking the wrong one mis-gates the feature. Recent 2025 work revived the water/aquifer-melt hypothesis, so this is actively contested.

Ring spokes can be reduced to a closed-form equinox-phase bell times a D13 magnetic-field term times advected noise. This is an admitted oversimplification: after decades 'no theory perfectly predicts the spokes,' so any cheap model reproduces appearance, not true timing/abundance.

The seasonal frost cap edge is well-approximated by a latitude band that breathes sinusoidally with obliquity-scaled amplitude. Real caps are asymmetric and threshold-driven by local pressure/temperature, so the closed-form latitude band will mis-place edges on high-eccentricity or unusual-composition bodies unless eccentricity is supplied.

Araneiform/spider channels can be baked once as a static dendrite pattern rather than simulated, because they accumulate over many years from repeated jets. If the design later wants them to visibly evolve across epochs, the baked-once assumption breaks and a relaxation pass per epoch is needed.

E13's core input -- an orbital-phase 'season clock' (and eccentricity) -- is NOT carried by the L0 16-scalar driver vector, so a faithful seasonal overlay is impossible without extending the interface to expose orbital phase/time and the system graph (ring presence). This is the single biggest architectural blocker for the engine.

verdicts.claim: RSL formation mechanism is genuinely unresolved (dry rarefied-gas granular flow vs. brine/aquifer-melt water activity), and recent 2025 work revived the water/aquifer-melt hypothesis; the engine's mechanism choice changes which drivers gate the feature.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed independently. The wet-vs-dry RSL debate is real and ongoing: dry granular-flow work (Nature Geoscience 2017, ngeo cited) vs. brine/deliquescence vs. groundwater. The specific 2025 revival is real: nature.com/articles/s41598-025-11171-y (Scientific Reports 2025) and PMC12264122 argue RSL time-series variations are 'compatible with contemporary water activity from bedrock aquifer melting,' citing hydrated salts present in summer and absent in autumn. The gating consequence the dossier draws (D5 atmo for dry granular flow vs. D2/D4 brine chemistry for wet) is a correct engineering implication of the unresolved mechanism. Not overstated.

verdicts.claim: Ring spokes can be reduced to a closed-form equinox-phase bell times a D13 magnetic-field term times advected noise; this is an admitted oversimplification because after decades no theory perfectly predicts the spokes.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. NASA Hubble material and multiple sources state explicitly that 'after several decades no theory perfectly predicts the spokes,' that they are electrostatic-levitation features tied to the magnetosphere/solar-wind interaction, that they strengthen near equinox (low solar ring-angle), and that they are transient, rotating near-synchronously and fading over ~2-3 ring rotations. The dossier's closed-form (equinox bell x D13 x advected fbm, decay over 2-3 rotations) matches the observed phenomenology, and the dossier correctly labels it appearance-not-timing. Honest and well-grounded.

verdicts.claim: The seasonal frost cap edge is well-approximated by a latitude band breathing sinusoidally with obliquity-scaled amplitude, but real caps are asymmetric and threshold-driven, so the closed-form mis-places edges on high-eccentricity/unusual-composition bodies unless eccentricity is supplied.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed and appropriately hedged. Sources confirm eccentricity + argument-of-perihelion is THE major driver of N/S Martian cap asymmetry (ScienceDirect S0019103523003809; perihelion in late southern spring, plus pole elevation difference), and that the cap is threshold-driven by local T/pressure, not a clean latitude circle. The dossier's own claim concedes the closed-form latitude band fails without eccentricity. This is a self-limiting, honest claim, not an overstatement. The sinusoidal-breathing approximation is a reasonable first-order model that the dossier explicitly flags as breaking on high-e bodies.

verdicts.claim: Araneiform/spider channels can be baked once as a static dendrite pattern rather than simulated, because they accumulate over many years from repeated jets; if they must visibly evolve across epochs, the baked-once assumption breaks and a per-epoch relaxation pass is needed.
verdicts.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed: the Kieffer model (translucent CO2 slab -> basal sublimation -> pressurized gas -> jet rupture -> dark fans + dendritic channel erosion = spiders) is well-established and lab-validated (Piqueux 2003; Nature s41598-021-82763-7; IOP PSJ Kieffer lab study 2024). Spiders genuinely accumulate over many Mars years, so baking a static dendrite is a defensible real-time choice, and the dossier honestly states the caveat that visible cross-epoch evolution would require a relaxation pass. This is the one component that touches an offline process, and it is correctly quarantined as a one-time bake, not run per frame. No misgrounding.

verdicts.claim: E13's core input -- an orbital-phase season clock (plus eccentricity) -- is NOT carried by the L0 16-scalar driver vector, so a faithful seasonal overlay is impossible without extending the interface to expose orbital phase/time and the system graph (ring presence). This is the single biggest architectural blocker.
verdicts.reasoning: This is an internal architecture claim about the world-engine's own L0 16-scalar interface, not a scientific claim I can web-verify, but it is internally coherent and correctly reasoned. A static per-body scalar vector genuinely cannot carry a per-frame/per-epoch animation phase or eccentricity; an engine whose entire output is a function of orbital phase necessarily needs that phase exposed. The inputs list flags orbital phase, eccentricity, slope/aspect field, and ring-presence as underSupplied consistently. The 'biggest blocker' framing is defensible: every one of the six outputs is keyed off the season clock, so without it the engine degenerates. Accepted as not-refuted on internal-consistency grounds; flagged as unverifiable-by-external-source.

verdicts.claim: All six outputs are analytic-or-noise with zero iteration (frost mask, defrost fans, RSL, dust opacity, ring spokes), the only offline piece being the one-time araneiform bake.
verdicts.reasoning: Audited each for hidden iteration/global coupling. (1) Frost mask: pure per-texel smoothstep over an analytic cosine-breathing latitude x fbm. No coupling. (2) Defrost fans: d(coverage)/ds<0 is the analytic derivative of the cosine coverage function (closed-form, NOT a numerical time-step), gating blue-noise sprite stamps. Blue-noise point set is a precomputed texture lookup (standard, legitimate bake), not a runtime relaxation. (3) RSL: dFdx/dFdy slope is free hardware derivatives; 1D growth curve is analytic. (4) Dust opacity: a single time curve + a baked low-frequency mask. (5) Ring spokes: thresholded fbm in an advected angle. None require a per-pixel global solve, neighbor iteration, or unbounded relaxation. The genuinely-offline physics (global-dust-storm spatial evolution = GCM, brine percolation = diffusion) is explicitly disclaimed and replaced by phase-curve+baked-mask. The zero-iteration claim holds for the runtime path.

verdicts.claim: typeDemotionNote: features should derive from drivers (D4 composition selects frost species, ring-presence+D13+equinox gate spokes, D5+slope-temp gate RSL) rather than discrete archetype flags ('Mars-type','Saturn-type').
verdicts.reasoning: This is a design-philosophy claim, not a falsifiable physical one, but it is physically well-motivated: frost species genuinely does follow composition/condensation thresholds (CO2 vs H2O), spokes genuinely require a ring + magnetospheric charging + equinox geometry (so a magnetized ringed body of any type could host them), and RSL genuinely require a thin-but-present atmosphere + warm-season slope temperature crossing. Deriving from drivers rather than archetype flags is consistent with all confirmed science. No misgrounding.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The steered-noise approximation is genuinely real-time-feasible in a WebGL budget, and crucially it does NOT hide an offline sim or unbounded relaxation in the runtime path. Every per-frame term is either closed-form analytic or a noise/texture lookup: the frost mask is a per-texel smoothstep over a cosine-breathing latitude band; the defrost-front trigger d(coverage)/ds<0 is the ANALYTIC derivative of that cosine (not a numerical time-step or diffusion solve); RSL uses free hardware dFdx/dFdy slope derivatives plus a 1D analytic growth curve; dust opacity is a single 1D time curve; ring spokes are thresholded fbm in an advected angle. There is no per-pixel global solve, no neighbor-coupled iteration, no convergence loop. The two operations that touch real physics are correctly quarantined: (a) the araneiform dendrite is baked ONCE as an L-system/relaxation pattern and thereafter treated as static terrain, and (b) the persistent dust-albedo mask is a baked low-frequency write. Blue-noise point sets are precomputed textures, the standard real-time practice. Most importantly, the dossier does not conceal the offline parts behind a 'closed-form/cheap' label -- it explicitly and honestly concedes that physically faithful global-dust-storm spatial evolution is a GCM problem and brine percolation is a diffusion problem, and that it deliberately substitutes a phase-curve + baked mask that reproduces the LOOK but not the dynamics. That is exactly the kind of disclosure an adversarial review wants to see, rather than refute. The one residual risk is honesty-flagged, not hidden: if the design later wants araneiforms to visibly evolve across epochs, the baked-once assumption breaks and a per-epoch relaxation pass would be needed -- the dossier states this. Net: the cheap approximation is real, bounded, and its limits are disclosed.

verify.notes: Adversarial verification outcome: I attempted to refute all seven load-bearing claims and could not refute any. The four concrete real-world processes (RSL wet/dry debate incl. the 2025 aquifer-melt revival; Kieffer-model CO2 jets -> dark fans -> araneiform spiders; eccentricity/perihelion-driven seasonal cap asymmetry; equinox/magnetosphere-modulated ring spokes with 'no theory perfectly predicts them') are all confirmed against primary/reputable sources, and the dossier's citations point to the right papers (nature ngeo2917, Scientific Reports s41598-025-11171-y, NASA Hubble spoke-season, etc.). The dossier is unusually honest: where physics is genuinely offline (GCM dust evolution, brine diffusion, multi-year araneiform carving) it labels those as offline and substitutes look-not-dynamics, rather than smuggling a solve into a 'cheap' shader. Two caveats on confidence: (1) the L0-16-scalar-interface architectural blocker claim is internal to the engine and unverifiable by external source -- accepted on internal consistency (medium confidence); (2) the typeDemotionNote and 'biggest blocker' framing are design-philosophy/judgement claims rather than falsifiable physics, accepted as physically well-motivated. No claim was found false, overstated, or mis-grounded. The cheap approximation is genuinely bounded and real-time; its offline pieces are disclosed, not concealed.

dossier.mechanism: Models the surface optical and structural imprint of biology and technology on a settled body. Two coupled sub-processes. (1) BIOSPHERE: where a habitable surface exists (liquid water + tolerable temp + energy budget), photoautotrophs colonize illuminated, moisture-bearing land/shallow-water and tint the surface reflectance away from the abiotic mineral/ice/ocean baseline. The canonical optical fingerprint is a "reflectance edge" — a sharp rise in albedo just longward of the pigment's absorption band (Earth's vegetation red edge near 0.7-0.75um from chlorophyll; bacteriochlorophyll/retinal edges push to 0.9-1.1um or shift the visible tint toward purple/orange/red). Pigment band placement tracks the host star's peak emission and the surface light/moisture regime, so cool-star (M-dwarf) and dry/hot worlds favor IR-edge or non-green pigments. Coverage is gated by insolation geometry (latitude, eyeball-climate substellar zone for tidally locked worlds, polar darkness from obliquity), water availability, and surface age (time for a biosphere to mature and spread). (2) TECHNOSPHERE: an inhabited world accrues artificial structure that is optically and thermally distinct from nature — nightside city-light emission (sodium/LED line emission against a dark hemisphere), daylit geometric land-use mosaics and high-albedo solar-panel fields, atmospheric industrial markers (NO2, CFCs — handled as atmo edits), and at extreme tiers orbital rings / megastructure waste-heat. The engine paints these as overlays whose density, extent, and spectral character scale with a habitability/technology index and the available time (age).

cheapApprox.description: Three composable layers, all GPU-cheap. (1) BIOSPHERE TINT = baked-field x closed-form. Compute a coverage mask = smoothstep(D15 gate) * moisture(D2, from a land/moisture field) * insolation weight (latitude band shaped by D3; for tidally locked worlds a substellar Gaussian annulus from D7) * maturity = smoothstep(age threshold, D16). Multiply by low-frequency biome noise (fBm) for patchiness. Then lerp the abiotic surface albedo toward a pigment color whose hue+edge-wavelength is chosen by a 1D ramp keyed to host-star peak wavelength (green for sun-like, shift to red/orange/IR-edge for cool stars, purple option for anoxic/M-dwarf) — implemented as a small LUT, NOT a discrete species switch. This is a per-pixel shader op over an existing albedo texture: closed-form. (2) NIGHTSIDE CITY LIGHTS = steered-noise. On the un-illuminated hemisphere (dot(N,sunDir)<0), seed an emissive layer = blue-noise/Worley point field weighted by (coverage on habitable coastlines/rivers from the same land+moisture field) * techDensity = smoothstep(habitability,age). Tint by a sodium/LED emission color. Pure fragment shader, no simulation. (3) LAND-USE + MEGASTRUCTURE = steered-noise + overlay geometry. Daylit: overlay a low-octave anisotropic (grid-warped) noise of geometric patches gated by techDensity, plus high-albedo specks for panel fields. Megastructures: a procedural ring/partial-shell mesh + emissive IR halo spawned only above a tech tier threshold. None of these need offline iteration; all are single-pass and seedable for determinism.

epochBehavior.note: Runs in the final (latest) epoch as an EDITOR over the settled surface produced by terrain/weathering/climate engines: it tints the existing abiotic albedo field, masks city lights against the existing insolation map, and hands NO2/haze edits to the atmosphere engine. It does not author its own terrain. Conceptually could re-run per-epoch to show a biosphere emerging then a technosphere overprinting it, but for a static render one pass at the present epoch suffices.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline almost certainly switches biosphere/technosphere on a discrete world 'type' (e.g. an enum like EARTHLIKE / GARDEN / INHABITED that hard-codes 'add green + city lights'). This should be demoted: (a) presence/lushness of biosphere should be a continuous function of D15 x D1 x D2 x D16, not a type flag; (b) pigment hue + reflectance-edge wavelength should derive from host-star peak emission and surface light/moisture regime via a LUT, not a fixed green; (c) technosignature density/extent/tier (none -> faint lights -> global mosaics -> megastructures) should be a continuous ramp on habitability x age, not a boolean 'civilized' bit; (d) 'green plants' is itself a type-demotion of pigment chemistry — purple/orange/IR-edge biospheres should be reachable for the right stellar+atmospheric drivers.
loadBearingClaims: The vegetation red edge is a real but disk-integrated-WEAK signal (~few percent albedo change on present-day Earth) — treating biosphere tint as a bold, obviously-visible surface color is an artistic exaggeration, not what the science says is detectable (OBS/SIM). For a game's 'read the history by looking' goal this exaggeration is acceptable but should be a deliberate stylization, not mistaken for realism.

Pigment band placement (green vs purple vs IR-edge) genuinely tracks host-star spectral type and surface light regime (SIM/THEO) — but the current L0 SCALAR interface gives the body only tempEq, NOT the stellar SED, so the engine cannot correctly choose the pigment edge without the system-graph stellar type being exposed. This is a real under-supply, not a modeling choice.

Nightside city lights and NO2 are physically grounded technosignatures studied for real telescope detection (Kopparapu et al.) (SIM/THEO) — but they are at the absolute edge of detectability (400h LUVOIR at 10pc), so their use as a vivid render feature is SF-tier stylization.

Megastructure waste-heat (Dyson-type) overlays are THEO/SF — real IR-excess candidate searches exist (OBS for the survey method) but no confirmed detection; placing them on a high-age/high-tech body is plausible extrapolation, not established science.

Biosphere coverage requires a 2D land/moisture/insolation FIELD from upstream engines; if E14 only receives scalars it cannot place coverage spatially and would fall back to uniform global tinting, which is the wrong (type-demoted) behavior.

verdicts.claim: The vegetation red edge is a real but disk-integrated-WEAK signal (~few percent albedo change on present-day Earth); bold visible biosphere tinting is artistic exaggeration, not realism (OBS/SIM).
verdicts.reasoning: Independently confirmed. O'Malley-James & Kaltenegger (Astrobiology 2018, the dossier's first citation) and the Earthshine/disk-integrated literature confirm the VRE produces only a few-percent reflectance change in disk-integrated light despite ~50% leaf reflectance, due to dilution by clouds, oceans, and discontinuous coverage. The dossier correctly self-labels the bold tint as deliberate stylization, not detectable realism. Honest, well-grounded, not overstated.

verdicts.claim: Pigment band placement (green/purple/IR-edge) tracks host-star spectral type + surface light regime (SIM/THEO); the L0 scalar interface gives only tempEq not the stellar SED, so the engine cannot correctly choose the pigment edge — a real under-supply.
verdicts.reasoning: Scientific half confirmed: 'Purple is the new green' (MNRAS 2024, cited), the Frontiers spectral-optimization paper, and M-dwarf cyanobacteria/retinal-pigment studies all show pigment absorption tracks stellar SED (purple/BChl IR pigments favored under M-dwarfs at ~1000nm). The under-supply claim is also internally valid: tempEq is a scalar proxy that does NOT uniquely determine stellar SED (different star types can yield similar equilibrium temps at different orbital distances), so deriving the pigment edge from tempEq alone is genuinely ill-posed. Real under-supply, correctly identified.

verdicts.claim: Nightside city lights and NO2 are physically grounded technosignatures studied for real telescope detection (Kopparapu et al.), but at the edge of detectability (400h LUVOIR at 10pc) — vivid render use is SF-tier stylization.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed precisely. Kopparapu et al. 2021 (ApJ 908,164) gives exactly SNR~5 in ~400hr with a 15m LUVOIR-like telescope for present-Earth NO2 at 10pc — the dossier's number is exact, not fabricated. City-lights detectability (Beatty 2022, MNRAS 513,2652, cited) confirms an Earth analogue is NOT detectable by LUVOIR/HabEx; only highly urbanized (0.4-3%) M-dwarf planets are. The 'edge of detectability / SF-tier' framing is accurate.

verdicts.claim: Megastructure waste-heat (Dyson-type) overlays are THEO/SF — IR-excess candidate surveys exist (OBS for method) but no confirmed detection; placing on high-age/high-tech bodies is plausible extrapolation, not established science.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Project Hephaistos found ~60 IR-excess Dyson candidates among millions of stars, but follow-up (e.g. radio imaging of candidates) found nothing and natural confounds (circumstellar dust, background galaxies) dominate; no confirmed detection exists. The dossier's THEO/SF grounding and 'plausible extrapolation, not established science' wording is calibrated correctly.

verdicts.claim: Biosphere coverage requires a 2D land/moisture/insolation FIELD from upstream engines; with only scalars E14 falls back to uniform global tinting (wrong, type-demoted behavior).
verdicts.reasoning: Internally and physically valid: placing vegetation only on illuminated moist land, city lights only on the dark hemisphere along coastlines, and an eyeball-biosphere annulus on tidally locked worlds all require per-texel spatial fields; a scalar cannot encode 'where'. With scalars only, a shader can only modulate uniformly, which is the type-demoted failure mode the dossier warns about. Correct.

verdicts.claim: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION (verifier-added): The cheapApprox method silently consumes the very fields the dossier flags as under-supplied.
verdicts.reasoning: This is the one substantive weakness. The inputs list marks land/water/moisture field, insolation/substellar map, surface albedo baseline, and stellar SED as underSupplied:true — yet the cheapApprox method freely assumes all of them: 'moisture(D2, from a land/moisture field)', 'coverage on habitable coastlines/rivers from the same land+moisture field', 'lerp the abiotic surface albedo', 'dot(N,sunDir)<0' insolation, and 'host-star peak wavelength' LUT. So the proposed approximation is feasible ONLY IF the under-supplies are resolved (engine receives fields + stellar type). The dossier does not foreground this dependency in the cheapApprox block; it presents the method as drop-in while its own inputs section says the prerequisites are missing. Not a science error, but a real internal inconsistency the reader must be told about: the cheap method's feasibility is conditional on fixing the under-supply, and the typeDemotionNote/loadBearingClaim 5 acknowledge this elsewhere but the cheapApprox text does not.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The three layers are genuinely real-time WebGL-feasible and hide NO offline simulation, iterative relaxation, or per-pixel global solve. (1) Biosphere tint = smoothstep gates x fBm noise x a 1D LUT color lerp over an existing albedo texture — pure per-fragment closed-form, O(1) per texel. (2) Nightside city lights = blue-noise/Worley point field on the dark hemisphere (dot(N,sunDir)<0), tinted, single-pass fragment shader — Worley/blue-noise are standard cheap procedural primitives. (3) Land-use mosaic = low-octave anisotropic noise + high-albedo specks; megastructure = a procedural ring/shell mesh + emissive halo spawned only above a tier threshold — overlay geometry, not simulation. All are single-pass and seedable for determinism, with no inter-texel coupling and no convergence loop. CAVEAT (does not break real-time feasibility but conditions it): the method presupposes the engine actually receives the 2D land/moisture/insolation/albedo fields and the host-star spectral type, all of which the dossier's own inputs list marks underSupplied:true. So it is real-time-feasible as a SHADER, but only correct/non-type-demoted once those upstream fields are wired in; with scalars only it degrades to (cheap but wrong) uniform global tinting. The cheapApprox is honest about cost class and contains no concealed iteration — the only gap is that it assumes inputs the dossier elsewhere flags as missing.

verify.notes: Tried hard to refute and could not knock down any of the five scientific load-bearing claims — every number and grounding tag (OBS/SIM/THEO/SF) checks out against the cited primary literature, and the dossier is unusually honest (it explicitly labels the bold biosphere tint and vivid technosignatures as stylization beyond detectability, rather than dressing them as realism). The NO2 figure (~400h, 15m LUVOIR, SNR~5, 10pc) is exact to Kopparapu 2021; city-lights and Dyson-candidate framings match Beatty 2022 and Project Hephaistos. The only real finding is an INTERNAL inconsistency, not a scientific error: the cheapApprox layer consumes the land/moisture/insolation/albedo fields and stellar SED that the inputs section flags as underSupplied:true, so the cheap method is real-time-feasible as a shader but its CORRECTNESS is conditional on resolving those under-supplies (acknowledged in typeDemotionNote and loadBearingClaim #5, but not surfaced in the cheapApprox text itself). No offline sim, unbounded relaxation, or per-pixel global solve is hidden anywhere in the proposed method.

engine.name: Ring / circumplanetary
engine.brief: system(rings/moons) + D13 -> rings + ring-shadow band + spokes + ring-rain inflow. Needs the per-body system graph (currently unexposed).

dossier.mechanism: Circumplanetary rings are debris confined inside the planet's Roche limit — the radius where tidal shear exceeds a satellite's self-gravity (r_Roche ≈ 2.456 R_p (ρ_p/ρ_m)^(1/3)). Material there cannot accrete into a moon, so it settles into a thin (meters-to-km thick) differentially-rotating disk of ice/rock particles, sourced from (a) a tidally-disrupted inbound moon/comet, (b) an impact-shattered satellite, or (c) leftover circumplanetary-disk debris that never coalesced. The engine produces four observable consequences governed by distinct sub-physics: (1) the RING DISK itself, radially banded by resonances with shepherd moons and by composition; (2) a RING SHADOW BAND cast onto the planet's cloud tops whose latitude tracks the sub-solar point (set by axial tilt D3 and ring opening angle), reducing insolation by ~14% at low latitudes; (3) SPOKES — transient radial dust features from sub-micron grains electrostatically levitated above the ring plane when ring-particle charging (via magnetospheric electron beams / meteor-impact plasma / cold-particle O2-cohesion release) overcomes gravity, co-rotating near-synchronously with the magnetic field; (4) RING RAIN — charged water-group ions/grains draining down magnetic field lines into the planet's mid-latitude ionosphere where the field lines that thread ring gaps reach the atmosphere, depositing 432–2870 kg/s (Saturn) and slowly eroding the rings (~10^8 yr lifetime). Spokes and ring rain are both gated by the magnetic field (D13): no magnetosphere → no field-aligned charging channels → no spokes and no organized ring rain.

inputs.name: system graph: moon/satellite inventory (masses, semi-major axes, densities, resonances)
inputs.note: REQUIRED to decide if rings exist at all (a disrupted inner moon, or a moon straddling the Roche limit) and to place resonance gaps (Cassini Division = 2:1 Mimas) and shepherd-confined ringlets. A 16-scalar L0 vector cannot carry a variable-length list of orbiting bodies with orbital elements. This is the single largest gap for E15.

inputs.name: system graph: ring presence/extent/optical-depth seed
inputs.note: Whether the body HAS a ring, and its inner/outer radius and surface density, is a per-system architectural fact (L0 computes the graph but does not expose it). Needs a structured ring descriptor, not a scalar.

inputs.name: D13 magneticField
inputs.note: GATE for spokes AND ring rain. No field → both features off. Carries as scalar fine; but spoke co-rotation rate and ring-rain latitude band need the DIPOLE GEOMETRY (tilt, offset), which a single scalar cannot express.

inputs.name: D3 axialTilt
inputs.note: Sets ring opening angle to the sun → shadow-band latitude and width, and seasonal sweep. Scalar is sufficient for the static-epoch shadow.

inputs.name: D9 ironFraction
inputs.note: Feeds D13 (field strength) and ring-particle/parent-moon mineralogy (rock-vs-ice ring color).

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: Co-determines D13; also sets synchronous-orbit radius, which divides the ring into regions where particles orbit faster/slower than the field (spoke morphology asymmetry, inner-ring infall direction).

inputs.name: D14 massGravity
inputs.note: Sets R_Roche scale and the gravitational threshold a charged grain must beat to levitate into a spoke.

inputs.name: D2 volatileFraction / D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Ice-vs-rock ring composition (bright icy rings need volatiles + cold enough that ice survives); also gates the <60 K cold-particle O2-cohesion spoke pathway.

inputs.name: D16 age
inputs.note: Ring darkening/pollution and mass-erosion: young rings bright/icy/massive, old rings dark/thin/contaminated. Drives the ring-rain depletion clock.

inputs.name: D11 surfaceHistory (impact flux)
inputs.note: Meteoroid bombardment both pollutes rings (darkening) and triggers the impact-plasma spoke pathway; high flux → more spoke activity + faster darkening.

inputs.name: planet surface/atmosphere field (for shadow compositing)
inputs.note: The shadow band and ring-rain glow must be composited onto whatever the atmosphere/cloud engine produced; needs that engine's output as a host layer.

outputs.name: ringField
outputs.note: Radial 1-D profile (function of orbital radius): optical depth / surface density, particle albedo & color (ice→rock), banding from resonance gaps. Renderable as a textured annulus + transparency LUT.

outputs.name: ringShadowBand
outputs.note: A latitude-banded darkening mask projected onto the planet cloud tops; latitude/width from D3 + ring geometry; carries the fine gap-stripe structure of ringField.

outputs.name: ringSelfShadow
outputs.note: Planet's own shadow cast across the ring annulus (the dark wedge), plus inter-ring shadowing.

outputs.name: spokes
outputs.note: Transient radial dust streaks on the ring (brighter in back-scatter / darker in forward-scatter), near-corotating with D13 field; only emitted when D13>threshold.

outputs.name: ringRainBands
outputs.note: Two mid-latitude (~25–60°) atmospheric emission/haze bands where field lines from ring gaps meet the ionosphere; tints/dims the atmosphere there; aurora-adjacent.

outputs.name: ringRainErosion
outputs.note: A scalar depletion rate fed back to D16/ring mass: sets how thin/old the ring looks and (over epochs) whether the ring survives.

featureMap: Ring annulus disk (banded ice/rock rings, gaps/divisions)
Ring shadow cast on planet cloud tops (latitude-banded darkening)
Planet shadow cast across the rings (dark wedge)
Spokes (radial dust streaks on the ring plane)
Ring-rain atmospheric bands (mid-latitude haze/glow near aurora)
Shepherd-moon ringlet confinement & resonance gaps

cheapApprox.description: Everything here is closed-form or baked — NO offline simulation needed. (1) RING DISK: render a flat annulus mesh in the body's equatorial plane, inner R from R_Roche = 2.456·R_p·(ρ_p/ρ_m)^(1/3), outer R from system-graph extent or a default ~2.3 R_p. Optical-depth & albedo as a 1-D radial LUT (256 px) baked once; carve resonance gaps analytically from the moon list (gap at a_gap = a_moon·(p/q)^(2/3) for p:q resonance). Alpha-blend with backscatter/forward-scatter phase term cos(phase). (2) SHADOW BAND: pure closed-form — project ring annulus along the sun vector onto the sphere; in the planet's fragment shader, for each surface point compute its equatorial-plane intercept along -sunDir and sample the ring optical-depth LUT → multiply albedo. Gives correct gap-stripe shadows and seasonal latitude from D3 for free. (3) RING SELF-SHADOW: same ray test in the ring shader against the planet sphere (analytic ray-sphere). (4) SPOKES: steered procedural noise — a few radial wedges (angular Gaussian) advected at the corotation angular rate ω_field (from D13/D8), amplitude gated by max(0, charging - gravity) where gravity∝D14 and charging∝D13·D11; fade in/out on a sawtooth lifetime. Modulate a dust-overlay texture on the ring, brightness sign flipped by viewing phase. Zero when D13≈0. (5) RING RAIN: baked two-band emissive mask on the atmosphere at latitudes set by the dipole-footprint of ring-gap field lines (closed-form L-shell: lat = arccos(sqrt(R_p/r_gap))), intensity ∝ ring surface density × D13; tint toward water/organic glow. (6) EROSION/age coupling: a single scalar multiply of ring LUT alpha by an age/pollution factor from D16+D11. All per-frame work is a handful of analytic samples in two fragment shaders — comfortably real-time.

epochBehavior.note: Ring existence/extent is set once at formation (an early epoch — disruption/impact event), but the ring is then EDITED across later epochs: ring-rain erosion thins it and shifts D16/age (so a late-epoch view shows a darker, lower-mass, possibly vanished ring), and pollution from D11 impact flux darkens it. Spokes and shadow bands are evaluated per-frame from the current epoch's ring state, not baked per-epoch. So: place once, then re-evaluate mass/darkness per epoch; the visible ring is the formation engine's output edited by the erosion/pollution sub-process.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: Current pipeline almost certainly hard-codes 'gas giant → has Saturn-style rings, terrestrial → no rings' by body TYPE. That should derive from drivers + graph: a ring is present iff there is debris inside R_Roche (a disrupted/Roche-straddling moon in the system graph) — a rocky planet that ate a moon SHOULD get rocky (dark) rings, and a gas giant with no disrupted satellite should get none. Likewise spokes are likely toggled by 'is this Saturn?' rather than gated by D13 magnetic field + D11 impact flux + D2/D1 cold-O2 cohesion; ring color is likely a fixed 'icy white' rather than derived from D2/D9/D1 (rock-vs-ice composition). Ring-rain bands, if present at all, are probably a Saturn-specific decal instead of being placed by the dipole L-shell footprint of ring-gap field lines (D13 geometry + ring radii). Shadow-band latitude should come from D3, not a fixed texture.
loadBearingClaims: Spokes and organized ring rain are BOTH gated by the magnetic field (D13): the dominant spoke models (magnetospheric electron beams, impact-plasma columns, corotation with the field) and ring rain (charged species channeled down field lines into mid-latitude ionosphere) all require a magnetosphere — so a ring around a non-magnetic body should show neither. This is a strong simplification; some spoke pathways (electrostatic charging from local plasma/UV) might operate weakly without a global dipole.

All four sub-features are closed-form/baked and need NO offline N-body or dusty-plasma simulation in the real-time budget — the shadow band, self-shadow, and ring-rain latitude are exact analytic projections; spokes are steered noise. Risk: faithful spoke MORPHOLOGY (their formation/decay timing, radial-vs-tilted shape, day/night asymmetry) genuinely comes from time-dependent plasma physics, so the steered-noise version is cosmetic, not mechanistic.

Ring inner edge = Roche limit via r ≈ 2.456 R_p (ρ_p/ρ_m)^(1/3) is the right placement law, but the constant and form depend on whether the body is fluid/rubble/differentiated (rubble piles disrupt closer in), so a single coefficient will misplace edges for some compositions.

Ring rain footprint latitude can be placed by the dipole L-shell of field lines threading ring gaps (lat = arccos(sqrt(R_p/r_gap))); this assumes a centered aligned dipole and ignores field tilt/offset, which a scalar D13 cannot carry — the band latitude may be wrong for tilted/offset fields.

Ring age/brightness coupling (young=bright/icy/massive, old=dark/polluted, ~10^8 yr lifetime from ring rain) is observationally contested — recent work argues ring rain makes rings LOOK young while they may be billions of years old — so tying ring darkness tightly to D16 age may encode a disputed scaling.

verdicts.claim: Spokes AND organized ring rain are both gated by the magnetic field (D13); a non-magnetic body should show neither.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed against the dusty-plasma literature: the dominant spoke models (meteoroid-impact-plasma columns ionized by UV, magnetospheric electron-beam charging, near-corotation with the field) and ring rain (charged water-group species channeled down field lines into the ionosphere, 432-2870 kg/s) all require a magnetosphere. The dossier does not overstate this: it explicitly labels it a 'strong simplification' and concedes weak local-plasma/UV electrostatic and cold-particle O2-cohesion (arXiv 2205.07008) pathways might operate without a global dipole, and cites the alternative-spoke paper (arXiv 2303.07197). Gating on D13 is the correct first-order model and the caveat is honestly disclosed. As an engine simplification it is defensible, not mis-grounded.

verdicts.claim: All four sub-features are closed-form/baked and need NO offline N-body or dusty-plasma simulation in the real-time budget; spokes are steered noise.
verdicts.reasoning: The geometric three (ring shadow band, planet self-shadow on rings, ring-rain latitude band) are genuinely exact analytic projections: ray-plane intercept + 1-D LUT sample for the shadow, analytic ray-sphere for the self-shadow, closed-form L-shell arccos for the rain band. None hide iteration or global coupling. The dossier is candid that the spoke MORPHOLOGY (formation/decay timing, day-night asymmetry, tilt) is real time-dependent dusty-plasma physics that the steered-noise version only mimics cosmetically. So the feasibility claim ('no offline sim needed for a plausible look') is TRUE; the only thing that would be refuted is a claim of mechanistic spoke fidelity, which the dossier explicitly disclaims. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Ring inner edge = Roche limit via r ~= 2.456 R_p (rho_p/rho_m)^(1/3) is the right placement law, with composition-dependent coefficient caveat.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: 2.44-2.456 is the standard fluid Roche-limit coefficient; the rigid-body coefficient is ~1.26, and rubble piles sit in between (disrupt closer in). The dossier states exactly this and warns a single coefficient misplaces edges for some compositions. Form and caveat both correct. Minor note: Saturn's actual visible rings extend only to ~2.3 R_p and the main rings sit comfortably inside the fluid Roche limit, so using r_Roche as the literal INNER edge is a modeling choice (debris can also exist sunswept inside it) — but as a placement scale it is the right law. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Ring-rain footprint latitude can be placed by dipole L-shell: lat = arccos(sqrt(R_p/r_gap)), assuming a centered aligned dipole.
verdicts.reasoning: The arccos(sqrt(R_p/L)) mapping is the textbook centered-dipole L-shell footprint and is consistent with the observed Saturn ring-rain band (~25-60 deg mid-latitudes mapping to ring gaps). The dossier correctly flags that this assumes a centered ALIGNED dipole and that a scalar D13 cannot carry tilt/offset. This limitation is strongly corroborated: Uranus's dipole is tilted 58.6 deg and offset 31% of the radius, which would badly break the aligned-dipole band placement. The claim is accurate and its stated failure mode is real and disclosed. Not refuted.

verdicts.claim: Ring age/brightness coupling (young=bright/icy, old=dark/polluted, ~10^8 yr ring-rain lifetime) — observationally contested; tying darkness tightly to D16 may encode a disputed scaling.
verdicts.reasoning: Accurately reflects the live 2023-2026 debate. Cassini micrometeoroid-infall pollution (Science Advances 2023) constrains the rings to a few hundred Myr, and NASA Ames erosion-rate work supports young+ephemeral; but a competing line argues ring-rain preferential ejection of dusty/organic material makes the rings LOOK young while they may be billions of years old. The dossier does not pick a side — it warns the darkness<->age scaling is disputed. That is the correct, non-overstated framing. Not refuted.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The proposed approximation is genuinely real-time feasible and does NOT hide an offline simulation, unbounded relaxation, or a per-pixel global solve.
