Concretely: (1) Ring disk = static annulus mesh + a 256px 1-D radial LUT baked once; resonance gaps carved analytically from the moon list via a_gap = a_moon*(p/q)^(2/3) — O(number of moons), not N-body. (2) Shadow band = one ray-plane intercept along -sunDir per fragment plus one LUT texture sample — a couple of ALU ops + 1 texfetch, fully local, no global coupling. (3) Self-shadow = analytic ray-sphere test, closed-form. (4) Ring-rain band = baked emissive mask at a closed-form arccos L-shell latitude. The only genuinely simulation-derived feature, SPOKE MORPHOLOGY, is explicitly DOWNGRADED to steered procedural noise (angular Gaussians advected at the corotation rate, sawtooth lifetime) — the dossier openly states this is cosmetic, not mechanistic, so it does NOT smuggle a dusty-plasma solve into the frame budget. No iteration count is unbounded; no per-pixel scene-wide gather is required. The honesty markers are strong: every place where the cheap path sacrifices physical fidelity (spoke timing/shape, single Roche coefficient, aligned-dipole band, disputed age scaling) is disclosed rather than concealed. The two real engineering gaps are NOT feasibility problems but INPUT problems — the dossier correctly flags that ring existence/extent and the variable-length moon list cannot ride a 16-scalar L0 vector and need a structured ring/satellite descriptor from the system graph. That is an architectural input gap, not a hidden offline cost. Verdict: the 'closed-form/cheap' billing is accurate; the only thing it is cheap about that it claims to be physical is spoke morphology, and it admits that.

verify.notes: All five load-bearing claims survived adversarial checking; none refuted. The dossier is unusually honest — every simplification that could have been an overstatement is explicitly flagged as a simplification, disputed scaling, or cosmetic-only approximation, which removed the usual grounds for refutation. Independent confirmations: spoke dusty-plasma/meteoroid-impact mechanism and magnetospheric corotation (Horanyi 2004 Rev. Geophys.; arXiv 2205.07008, 2303.07197); fluid Roche coefficient 2.44-2.456 vs rigid ~1.26 (Roche-limit literature); ring-rain 432-2870 kg/s at ~25-60 deg mid-latitudes mapping to ring gaps (O'Donoghue 2013, arXiv 1310.7293); contested ring age (Science Advances 2023 micrometeoroid-infall vs ring-rain-makes-rings-look-young counterargument). KEY CAVEATS that are real but disclosed: (a) tilted/offset dipoles (Uranus 58.6 deg tilt, 31% offset) break the centered-aligned-dipole band placement a scalar D13 cannot fix; (b) steered-noise spokes are visually plausible but physically cosmetic; (c) single Roche coefficient misplaces edges for rubble/rigid compositions; (d) age<->darkness coupling encodes a genuinely disputed scaling. The dominant REAL weakness is not feasibility but the under-supplied inputs the dossier itself names as 'the single largest gap': a 16-scalar L0 vector cannot carry the variable-length moon inventory or the ring presence/extent descriptor; without a structured system-graph ring/satellite descriptor, gap placement and ring-existence decisions degrade to the very type-hardcoding the typeDemotionNote warns against. Feasibility claim: accurate. Real-time budget: comfortably met (a few analytic samples in two fragment shaders). No hidden offline sim, no unbounded relaxation, no per-pixel global solve detected."}

engine.name: Illumination regime (sidecar)
engine.brief: D7 + star + host -> lighting regime: terminator / eyeball-tidally-locked / rogue-starless thermal-only / compact-object-pulsed. A render-frame SIDECAR that modifies how every tier READS; NOT a step in the history chain.

dossier.mechanism: A render-frame sidecar that computes the *geometry and spectrum of incident radiation* a body receives, then exposes it so every terrain/atmosphere/surface tier READS lighting consistently. Real planetary-science content it encodes: (1) Standard solar irradiation — a point/finite-disk source giving a cosine-law insolation field cos(theta) from the sub-solar point, a terminator at theta=90 deg, and limb/penumbra softening set by the star's angular radius (host distance + star radius). (2) Eyeball / tidally-locked regime (D7) — when rotation is synchronized with the orbit the sub-stellar point is FIXED in body coordinates, producing a permanent dayside, a permanent nightside, and a stationary terminator ring; the canonical "eyeball" climate (open ocean/melt at substellar, frozen limb) and "terminator habitability" band are downstream of this fixed-illumination geometry, not of any new terrain process. (3) Rogue / starless regime — no external stellar term; the surface is lit only by its own thermal/volcanic self-emission (radiogenic + tidal interior heat leaking through, lava glow), so the only "light" is blackbody self-luminance from hot vents/lava and a near-black sky. (4) Compact-object-pulsed regime — a neutron-star/pulsar host delivers irradiation as a hard (X-ray/UV) spectrum and, for fast rotators, a *time-periodic* sweep (lighthouse beaming) rather than steady visible insolation, plus blue-shifted, low-luminosity-in-visible lighting. The spectrum of the source (D4 of the STAR, i.e. its effective temperature / spectral class) sets the *color temperature* and chromaticity of incident light: M-dwarf hosts deliver red/near-IR-weighted illumination (most flux 700-1000 nm, little blue), shifting perceived surface color and sky color regardless of intrinsic albedo. The engine outputs a unified "incident-radiation descriptor" (direction(s), angular size, color temperature, intensity, hardness, temporal modulation) that all tiers sample.

inputs.name: D7 tidalLock
inputs.note: Selects fixed-substellar (eyeball) geometry vs. rotating insolation. Scalar is adequate as a 0..1 lock fraction; partial lock / spin-orbit resonance (e.g. 3:2) wants a small structured hint but a scalar covers the common case.

inputs.name: D8 rotation
inputs.note: For unlocked bodies sets the diurnal cycle / sub-solar track; for pulsar hosts the body's own spin interacts with the beamed sweep. Scalar OK.

inputs.name: D4 atmoComposition
inputs.note: Atmospheric scattering tints/softens incident light (Rayleigh sky color, haze forward-scatter at terminator). Needed for terminator glow and sky color. Scalar composition index is a lossy proxy for true cross-section spectra but workable.

inputs.name: D5 atmoDensity
inputs.note: Sets optical depth -> terminator softening width, twilight wedge, day/night heat smearing that widens the lit-appearance band beyond the geometric terminator.

inputs.name: star effective temperature / spectral class
inputs.note: Sets incident COLOR TEMPERATURE and chromaticity (M-dwarf red-weighted vs G white vs pulsar hard-blue). This is the single most load-bearing input and is NOT in the 16 body drivers — it is a property of the HOST, which lives only in the L0 system-graph that is currently not exposed to the per-body pipeline.

inputs.name: star luminosity + orbital distance (insolation magnitude)
inputs.note: Sets absolute brightness and the star's angular disk size (penumbra/limb-softening width). Derivable from system-graph (L,star + a,orbit) but the scalar interface does not currently carry it; D1 tempEq is a downstream PROXY (it bakes in insolation) but cannot be inverted back to direction+angular-size+spectrum.

inputs.name: host-object class (star vs neutron star vs none/rogue)
inputs.note: Picks the whole regime branch (stellar / pulsed / starless). A scalar cannot encode 'is the primary a compact object' or 'is this body unbound' — it is a categorical graph fact.

inputs.name: pulsar spin period + beaming geometry
inputs.note: Required for the time-periodic pulsed-illumination modulation and hard-spectrum flux. Fully absent from a scalar interface; needs a small structured host record.

inputs.name: interior/self-emission heat flux
inputs.note: For the rogue regime the only illumination is self-emission, so the engine must read the interior-heat / volcanic-emission field (D12 tidalHeating + radiogenic from D9/D16, plus any lava-field output from the volcanism engine). D12 is hard-zeroed in the current pipeline, so the rogue regime currently has NO light source to read.

inputs.name: D1 tempEq
inputs.note: Used as a fallback brightness/color proxy when the true star spectrum is unavailable; also gates whether substellar melt/lava self-glow is visible.

outputs.name: incidentRadiationDescriptor
outputs.note: Per-body uniform: primary light direction(s) in body frame, source angular radius (for penumbra), intensity, color temperature/chromaticity, spectral hardness flag, temporal-modulation params (period, duty cycle for pulsar). Sampled by all tiers' shaders.

outputs.name: insolationField cos(theta)
outputs.note: Closed-form sub-solar cosine field; for locked bodies it is static in body coords, for unlocked it is parameterized by the rotating sub-solar longitude.

outputs.name: terminatorBand
outputs.note: Soft transition zone width as a function of star angular size + atmospheric optical depth (D5/D4); drives twilight wedge and limb glow.

outputs.name: selfEmissionMask
outputs.note: For rogue/lava regimes: which surface texels emit their own light (lava vents, hot fractures) and at what blackbody color, so the surface is its own light source.

outputs.name: skyColor / ambientTint
outputs.note: Sky and ambient fill color derived from star chromaticity + atmospheric scattering; near-black for rogue, red-orange for M-dwarf day, hard-blue tint for pulsar.

featureMap: Terminator line and twilight/limb glow on every lit body
Eyeball-climate appearance: bright substellar disk grading to dark frozen limb on tidally-locked worlds (governs how D7 reads at render time, not the ice itself)
Permanent dayside / permanent nightside hemispheric split
Sub-solar hot-spot brightening and substellar magma/lava self-glow
Sky color and ambient fill (red M-dwarf skies, washed pulsar skies, black rogue skies)
Self-illuminated lava/vent glow on starless or magma-dayside bodies
Phase/illumination of moons and the body as seen from space (lit crescent vs full)
Polar twilight banding interaction with axial tilt (D3) where the sub-solar latitude is offset

cheapApprox.description: Pure analytic shading sidecar, no simulation. (1) Build a single small uniform struct per body each frame: lightDir (unit vec in body frame), lightColor (RGB from star color-temperature via a blackbody->sRGB lookup or a 1D LUT keyed by star Teff), lightIntensity (from L_star / a^2, or D1 as fallback), srcAngularRadius (= R_star / a, used to widen the terminator), spectralHardness (0=visible,1=X-ray/UV), and pulse{period,duty}. (2) In each tier's existing surface shader, lighting = a Lambert/Oren-Nayar term lit = smoothstep(-w, +w, dot(N,lightDir)) where w = srcAngularRadius + k*atmoOpticalDepth(D5,D4) gives a physically-motivated soft terminator/penumbra in ONE line. (3) Regime is a branch selected by host-class enum: STELLAR -> the above; LOCKED -> identical but lightDir is constant in body coords (free — just don't rotate it with spin); ROGUE -> set lightIntensity=0 and instead drive emission from selfEmissionMask (an emissive term = blackbody color of the interior-heat field sampled from upstream volcanism/heat texture), so the planet lights itself; PULSED -> multiply intensity by a periodic square/sine pulse(time, period, duty) and bias lightColor toward hard-blue + raise an 'erosion/glow' aesthetic flag. (4) Sky/ambient = lightColor * scatteringTint(D4) with a small constant floor; rogue floor ~0. Everything is per-pixel analytic from a handful of uniforms; cost is a few ALU ops added to shaders that already run. No relaxation, no baking, no offline pass. The ONLY thing it must READ (not compute) is the upstream interior-heat / lava field for the rogue self-emission case — that field is produced by other engines, so E2 stays closed-form.

epochBehavior.note: As a render-frame sidecar it is logically evaluated EVERY FRAME (light direction/pulse phase update with camera/time), but it does no history writing and runs no per-epoch pass — its parameters (regime, star color, lock state) are resolved once from drivers+graph and then just sampled. It modifies how tiers READ; it never edits a host patch the way an editor engine (e.g. lava-flood) does.

dossier.typeDemotionNote: High demotion risk. Current code almost certainly hard-codes a single 'sunlight' regime: a fixed white directional light with a hard terminator, regardless of host. Likely discrete-type hard-codings to remove: (a) light COLOR baked white instead of derived from the host star's effective temperature -> should be a continuous blackbody LUT keyed by star Teff so an M-dwarf world is red-lit and a hot-star world blue-lit by derivation, not by tag; (b) terminator SHARPNESS as a constant instead of derived from star angular size + atmospheric optical depth (D5/D4); (c) 'eyeball planet' treated as a discrete planet TYPE with pre-painted ice rings, when it should emerge from D7 making lightDir static while the existing climate/ice tiers read that static insolation; (d) rogue/starless and pulsar worlds likely have NO branch at all (default-sunlit), so they're implicitly type-demoted to 'normal star' — the regime must derive from host-class in the system-graph; (e) substellar lava glow keyed to a 'lava planet' type rather than emerging wherever insolation*albedo + interior heat exceeds the melt threshold.
loadBearingClaims: The single most important input — host-star spectrum/color-temperature, luminosity+distance, and host-CLASS (star vs neutron star vs none) — is NOT carried by the 16 scalar body drivers; it lives only in the L0 system-graph that is currently unexposed. Without piping a small host record through, E2 cannot color light correctly or even select the rogue/pulsar regimes, and would silently default everything to generic sunlight. (THEO/architecture; the under-supply is the core finding.)

Illumination can be done fully closed-form in a real-time budget with NO simulation: cosine insolation + analytic soft terminator (width = star angular size + atmospheric optical depth) + blackbody color LUT, all from a few uniforms. This is the crux claim that E2 is cheap; it holds because illumination geometry/spectrum is genuinely analytic, UNLIKE heat REDISTRIBUTION (the actual eyeball CLIMATE band requires GCM-class transport) which is correctly NOT E2's job. (THEO)

The 'eyeball' appearance is downstream of fixed illumination geometry (D7 freezing the sub-solar point), so it should emerge from E2 making lightDir static plus existing climate tiers, not be a hard-coded planet type with painted ice rings. (OBS/THEO — eyeball climate is a published model, but that it should be ENGINE-derived rather than typed is a design claim.)

The rogue/starless regime has no external light, so its ONLY illumination is interior self-emission (radiogenic + tidal heat, lava glow). Because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed in the current pipeline and there is no exposed interior-heat field, the rogue regime currently has nothing to read and would render as a uniformly black/unlit body — a real gap, not a stylistic choice. (THEO/SIM — radiogenic/tidal interior heating of isolated planets is published; the pipeline gap is an architecture claim.)

Pulsar/compact-object illumination is hard-spectrum (X-ray/UV), low in visible luminosity, and for fast rotators time-periodic (beaming) — so a 'steady visible directional light' model is physically wrong for these hosts; the realistic render is a dim, blue-hard, possibly pulsing light plus surface erosion cues. The visible-light brightness from a millisecond pulsar is far too low to light a planet the way a star does, so the aesthetic must come from self-emission + hard-radiation glow, not reflected starlight. (OBS for the X-ray luminosity scale of PSR B1257+12; SF for how to render it as 'lighting'.)

verdicts.claim: Host-star spectrum/color-temperature, luminosity+distance, and host-CLASS (star/neutron-star/none) are NOT carried by the 16 scalar body drivers — they live only in the L0 system-graph currently unexposed to the per-body pipeline; without piping a small host record through, E2 cannot color light correctly or select rogue/pulsar regimes and defaults to generic sunlight.
verdicts.reasoning: This is an internal-architecture claim I cannot independently verify against source code (no repo present in the working dir; this is a memory/dossier directory). However it is internally coherent and physically necessary: color temperature, angular disk size, and regime branch are all properties of the HOST, not of the body. A per-body scalar set genuinely cannot encode a categorical graph fact like 'primary is a compact object' or 'body is unbound.' The reasoning is sound and the under-supply flags are correctly marked. I withhold full confidence only because the 'currently hard-codes white sunlight' assertion about the existing codebase is unverified — but the THEORETICAL necessity of the host record is correct. Not refuted on the load-bearing (architectural) substance.

verdicts.claim: Illumination can be done fully closed-form in a real-time WebGL budget with NO simulation: cosine insolation + analytic soft terminator (width = star angular size + atmospheric optical depth) + blackbody color LUT, all from a few uniforms — UNLIKE heat REDISTRIBUTION (eyeball CLIMATE) which needs GCM-class transport and is correctly NOT E2's job.
verdicts.reasoning: This is the crux feasibility claim and it survives adversarial scrutiny. Every component is genuinely non-iterative: cos(theta) is a single dot product; the soft terminator is one smoothstep; intensity is L/a^2 arithmetic; the blackbody->sRGB mapping is a 1D LUT baked OFFLINE (Planck integrated against CIE matching functions precomputed — a legitimate static bake, not a per-frame solve); pulse modulation is a sin/square of time. No relaxation, no global coupling, no per-pixel iterative solve is hidden anywhere. Critically, the dossier draws the RIGHT boundary: it explicitly does NOT attempt heat redistribution / the actual eyeball climate band, which my literature check confirms requires GCM-class ocean-heat-transport and sea-ice-drift modeling (Nature Astronomy s41550-019-0883-z; PNAS 1315215111). By offloading that to climate tiers and keeping only the geometry+spectrum of INCIDENT radiation, E2 stays genuinely analytic. The one honest dependency (reading the upstream interior-heat texture for rogue self-emission) is a READ, not a compute, and is flagged. The only legitimate accuracy caveat: real M-dwarf SEDs are NOT pure blackbodies (molecular opacities; peak does not move redward as Planck predicts — confirmed via M-dwarf spectral-sequence literature), so a Teff-keyed blackbody LUT is an approximation of chromaticity — but that is an accuracy limitation, not a feasibility/iteration problem, and is acceptable for real-time rendering.

verdicts.claim: The 'eyeball' appearance is downstream of fixed illumination geometry (D7 freezing the sub-solar point) and should EMERGE from E2 making lightDir static plus existing climate tiers, not be a hard-coded planet type with painted ice rings.
verdicts.reasoning: The physics half is well-established published science: tidal locking fixes the substellar point, producing a permanent dayside / stationary terminator, and the eyeball climate (clear central ocean, frozen limb) is the canonical model (Wikipedia Eyeball planet; arXiv 1705.08904 'No Snowball on Habitable Tidally Locked Planets'). The design half — that it should be engine-derived rather than typed — is a reasonable architecture claim, correctly tagged OBS/THEO. One important nuance the dossier handles correctly: the literature shows the OPEN-WATER appearance with ocean dynamics becomes lobster-shaped or even snowball (sea-ice drift can erase the open ocean entirely). That detailed climate pattern is NOT E2's job (it needs transport modeling), and E2 only claims to make lightDir static — the actual ice/ocean pattern is left to climate tiers. The claim is scoped honestly and not refuted.

verdicts.claim: The rogue/starless regime has no external light, so its ONLY illumination is interior self-emission (radiogenic + tidal heat, lava glow); because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed and no interior-heat field is exposed, the rogue regime currently has nothing to read and would render uniformly black — a real architecture gap, not a stylistic choice.
verdicts.reasoning: The physics is published and correct: rogue planets rely on radiogenic decay + gravitational contraction + (where applicable) tidal heating; small bodies can sustain massive volcanism and lava lakes that self-glow (Wikipedia Rogue planet; arXiv 2511.03392 on rogue-moon habitability; the tandfonline interiors-and-habitability review). The conclusion 'only light is self-emission, sky near-black' follows directly from there being no external source. The architecture gap claim (D12 hard-zeroed -> nothing to read -> black body) is internal and unverifiable from here, but is internally consistent and the dependency is correctly flagged as a READ of an upstream field. Medium confidence solely because the code-state assertion (D12 hard-zeroed) cannot be independently confirmed in this environment.

verdicts.claim: Pulsar/compact-object illumination is hard-spectrum (X-ray/UV), low in VISIBLE luminosity, and time-periodic for fast rotators (beaming) — so a steady visible directional light is physically wrong; the realistic render is dim/blue-hard/possibly-pulsing light plus surface erosion cues, with self-emission + hard-radiation glow rather than reflected starlight.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed against primary literature. PSR B1257+12 X-ray luminosity Lx ~ 2.5e29 erg/s (0.3-8 keV) (IOPscience 10.1086/518926; arXiv 0704.2079) — many orders of magnitude below a main-sequence star's optical output, so it genuinely cannot 'light a planet like a star' in visible. The A&A neutron-star-planets irradiation paper (aa31102-17) confirms the spectrum is hard (X-ray/UV) and erosive to atmospheres/volatiles. Pulsar lighthouse beaming producing time-periodic flux for fast rotators is textbook. The 'render it as dim/blue-hard/pulsing + self-emission' is correctly tagged SF (it's a rendering choice grounded in real physics). Not refuted.

cheapApproxRealistic.reasoning: The 'closed-form' label is honest, not a cover for hidden cost. Every output is computable per-pixel from a handful of per-body uniforms with a few ALU ops added to shaders that already run: cos(theta) is one dot product; the soft terminator is one smoothstep whose width is a closed-form sum of star angular radius and atmospheric optical depth; intensity is L/a^2; the blackbody->sRGB chromaticity comes from a 1D LUT baked OFFLINE (Planck x CIE precomputed once — a legitimate static asset, NOT a per-frame integration); pulse modulation is a sin/square of time. There is NO relaxation, NO per-pixel global solve, NO unbounded iteration, and NO global coupling between texels anywhere in the pipeline. The single external dependency — reading the upstream interior-heat/lava texture for the rogue self-emission case — is explicitly a READ of a field produced by other engines, not a compute E2 performs, and the dossier flags it as such. The design also draws the correct, crucial boundary that distinguishes a real cheap approximation from a disguised expensive one: it computes the GEOMETRY and SPECTRUM of INCIDENT radiation (genuinely analytic) and deliberately does NOT compute heat REDISTRIBUTION / the actual eyeball climate band, which the literature confirms needs GCM-class ocean-heat-transport + sea-ice-drift modeling. Pushing that to climate tiers is what keeps E2 closed-form. The only caveat is accuracy, not feasibility: a Teff-keyed blackbody LUT mis-predicts true M-dwarf chromaticity because real M-dwarf SEDs are dominated by molecular opacities rather than a Planck curve — but that is a fidelity trade-off appropriate to a real-time renderer, not a hidden offline cost.

verify.notes: All five external physics claims independently confirmed against primary literature: eyeball-planet climate (Nature Astronomy s41550-019-0883-z; arXiv 1705.08904), PSR B1257+12 X-ray luminosity ~2.5e29 erg/s (IOPscience 10.1086/518926; A&A aa31102-17), M-dwarf NIR-weighted SED, and rogue-planet radiogenic/tidal self-heating. None refuted. The three architecture/code-state claims (host record not in 16 scalar drivers; D12 hard-zeroed leaving rogue with no light source; existing code hard-codes white sunlight) could NOT be independently verified because no source repository is present in this environment (cwd is the memory directory, not the world-engine codebase) — they are marked medium confidence on that basis, but each is internally coherent and physically necessary, and I found no grounds to refute them. The cheap approximation is genuinely real-time feasible with no hidden offline sim or unbounded iteration. The most important accuracy caveat (not a feasibility issue): a Planck/blackbody LUT keyed by Teff is a known-lossy model of M-dwarf chromaticity since real M-dwarf spectra are shaped by molecular opacities, not a blackbody curve. The dossier itself acknowledges the scalar atmoComposition index is a lossy proxy for true cross-section spectra. Boundary discipline (illumination geometry/spectrum = E2; heat redistribution/climate = NOT E2) is the single strongest reason the 'cheap' claim holds.

plumbing.name: bulk mass AND radius (→ density, CMF, radius-valley position)
plumbing.note: The regime split (rocky/ocean/sub-Neptune/giant) is a mass-RADIUS / bulk-density classification (radius valley ~1.6 R⊕). A single D14 gravity scalar collapses mass and radius into one number and cannot recover density or CMF; code computes a `density` field internally but never feeds it back to choose the regime. Needs mass + radius as a pair, or density itself, as a carried field.

plumbing.name: stellar metallicity [Fe/H] + frost-line AU + orbit AU
plumbing.note: deriveComposition's ACTUAL inputs (PhysicsEngine.js:341) are metallicity, orbitAU, frostLineAU — system/star-graph quantities. The L0 scalar vector exposes only the OUTPUTS (D2/D9/D10). Fine for per-body rendering, but the engine cannot be re-run or perturbed from the scalar vector alone; the generative provenance lives in the dropped system graph.

plumbing.name: giant-impact / mantle-stripping flag (super-Mercury, stripped-core)
plumbing.note: High-CMF iron worlds and stripped-cores are a COLLISION-history / escape-history outcome (sibling impacts, XUV stripping). Currently faked by an RNG scatter term inside deriveComposition; the real driver is system-graph collision history + D6 retention, which a per-body scalar cannot carry.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Hard-zeroed in current pipeline. Strong tidal heating lowers effective rigidity → raises fluid Love number h2 → larger tidal/rotational figure (Io is plausibly relaxing toward a more fluid triaxial shape). With D12=0 the engine cannot soften a body's figure under heating; all bodies are treated as cold/rigid. This is a dropped driver the figure regime genuinely needs.

plumbing.name: orbit: semi-major axis a, primary mass M_p, primary radius R_p
plumbing.note: REQUIRED for the tidal term (M_p/M_body)(R_body/a)^3 and the Roche limit d=2.44 R_p(ρ_p/ρ_s)^(1/3). The L0 graph computes star/sibling/moon/ring relationships but does NOT expose them to the per-body pipeline. A per-body scalar 'tidalLock' fraction cannot reconstruct distance-to-primary or primary density, so the magnitude of the tidal bulge and the Roche proximity are currently un-derivable — they must be faked or hard-set. This is the single biggest under-supply.

plumbing.name: tidal bulge sub-primary direction vector
plumbing.note: The prolate long axis must point at the primary; that is a direction in the body frame, not a scalar. Needed so the bulge faces the right way (and, with D7, so the substellar/sub-primary point lines up with E2-illumination's eyeball-climate and any substellar-magma editor). A scalar interface cannot carry this orientation.

plumbing.name: E? collisional/accretion history field (giant-impact record)
plumbing.note: True irregular shapes (contact binaries, giant-impact basins that flatten one hemisphere) come from discrete collision events, not a scalar. No upstream engine currently emits an impact-event list; the irregularity must be approximated by seeded noise rather than derived from real history.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Io-grade equatorial volcanic province existence depends on tidal heat; hard-zeroed in current pipeline so the canonical Io case cannot be generated as-is

plumbing.name: orbit sense + synchronous-vs-not flag
plumbing.note: leading/trailing province requires knowing prograde direction and whether the body orbits inside/outside corotation; a per-body scalar set cannot carry this

plumbing.name: ring / dust / sibling-moon sources
plumbing.note: exogenic leading-hemisphere darkening (Phoebe-ring/E-ring analogue) needs the system graph of dust donors; not exposed to the per-body pipeline

plumbing.name: magnetosphere corotation flux
plumbing.note: trailing-hemisphere plasma bombardment needs parent magnetic-field + orbital-distance-vs-corotation; D13 is the body's OWN field, not the parent's, so a scalar cannot stand in

plumbing.name: crustal-block / impact-basin seed
plumbing.note: an ancient compositional megablock like Xanadu or a giant-impact hemispheric province is an upstream tectonic/impact field; no current upstream engine emits a placed province seed

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: HARD-ZEROED in current game pipeline. This is the engine's primary heat magnitude input — with it dead, all tidal-heat flux, cryovolcanism, Io-grade resurfacing, and tidal-stress cracking are forced off. The single most load-bearing under-supply for E3.

plumbing.name: orbital eccentricity e
plumbing.note: Heat ∝ e^2 and diurnal stress amplitude ∝ e. A per-body scalar interface that carries no orbit element cannot supply e; it is currently folded (if at all) into D12 rather than exposed. Without e the engine cannot distinguish a circular-orbit dead moon from an Io.

plumbing.name: physical libration amplitude
plumbing.note: Adds an oscillating stress component that measurably reshapes cycloid fits; a scalar driver vector cannot carry it.

plumbing.name: semi-major axis a / mean motion n
plumbing.note: Heat ∝ a^(-15/2); needed to convert resonance/orbit into magnitude. Not in the 16 scalars.

plumbing.name: resonance / neighbor graph (e.g. Laplace 1:2:4)
plumbing.note: Resonances PUMP and MAINTAIN the eccentricity that drives everything (Io–Europa–Ganymede). L0 computes a system graph but does NOT expose it per-body, so the engine cannot know an orbit's e is forced rather than damped — it cannot tell a resonance-locked active moon from a relaxed one.

plumbing.name: interior layering / Love numbers (h2, l2, Im(k2))
plumbing.note: Stress amplitudes and heat depend on the complex Love numbers, which come from an interior-structure model (E? differentiation engine). A scalar cannot carry a depth-dependent rheology; currently must be approximated from D9/D14/D2.

plumbing.name: D13 magneticField
plumbing.note: Master gate: field strength/presence. Scalar OK as a magnitude proxy, but it is a derived composite (ironFraction x rotation) and a scalar cannot carry field TOPOLOGY (dipole vs multipole, tilt, offset) which controls oval shape and asymmetry.

plumbing.name: field topology / dipole tilt & offset
plumbing.note: Needed for non-dipolar/ tilted ovals (cf. Uranus/Neptune offset-tilted fields, and Earth excursions producing globally-distributed low-latitude aurorae). No scalar or current field carries an axis/multipole descriptor.

plumbing.name: D4 atmoComposition
plumbing.note: Sets aurora EMISSION SPECIES/COLOR (O green/red vs N blue vs CO2/other). Scalar composition index is lossy -- color needs a species mix, but a categorical/low-dim proxy is workable.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Drives Io-type volcanic moon outgassing that feeds a plasma torus. HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline, so the entire torus/satellite-weathering pathway is dead.

plumbing.name: stellar wind dynamic pressure (rho, v) & orbital distance
plumbing.note: Other half of the standoff pressure balance and of erosion rate; depends on star type/age and orbit. Not exposed per-body today.

plumbing.name: system graph: host giant, sibling moons, resonances, rings
plumbing.note: Needed to know if THIS body is a torus source, a torus victim (sputter-weathered moon), or hosts a satellite-footprint aurora. L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline.

plumbing.name: D4 atmoComposition
plumbing.note: A scalar cannot carry a species mixture (N2/CO2/CH4/H2/NH3 fractions). Cloud species, haze chemistry (tholins need CH4+UV), and Rayleigh cross-section all need a small composition vector, not one number.

plumbing.name: stellar spectrum / luminosity / orbital distance
plumbing.note: Insolation pattern, day-night substellar geometry, UV flux (drives haze photochemistry AND escape) all need the star node + orbit; not exposed to the per-body pipeline today. D1 partially proxies bolometric insolation but not spectral shape or sub-stellar direction.

plumbing.name: surface land/ocean + topography field
plumbing.note: Cloud forcing, monsoon/orographic banding, and eyeball open-water mask need a 2D surface field from the hypsography/hydrology engines; a scalar driver cannot carry it. Currently the climate sky is computed body-globally with no surface feedback.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Hard-zeroed in current pipeline. An Io/Europa-grade interior heat source would add a bottom heating term (plumes, sublimation atmospheres) the engine cannot currently see.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Master driver for icy-shell lineament networks, grooves, expansion-driven grabens, and despin-coupled stress. HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline -> Europa/Ganymede/Io-grade tectonic grain cannot be produced at all. This is the single biggest gap for E6.

plumbing.name: interior thermal-history / radius-change sign+magnitude
plumbing.note: Whether the body is net-contracting (cooling) or net-expanding (heating/differentiation), and by how much, is not a current L0 scalar. It must be DERIVED from D12+D14+D16+D9, or added. Sign of radial strain flips the entire feature set (scarps vs grabens).

plumbing.name: primordial-spin / despin amplitude (Δbulge)
plumbing.note: Melosh despin stress depends on (initial spin^2 - final spin^2) and elastic shell thickness, not the present rotation alone. A single rotation scalar cannot carry the historical despin amplitude or the shell thickness needed to pick the fault-province pattern.

plumbing.name: orbital/tidal context (eccentricity, parent, resonance)
plumbing.note: Diurnal tidal stress amplitude (Europa-type lineaments) and non-synchronous-rotation crack-set rotation need eccentricity + parent-body + resonance state from the per-system graph, which L0 computes but does NOT expose to the per-body pipeline.

plumbing.name: crustal-thickness / lithosphere field from interior engine
plumbing.note: Tessera/plateau relief and isostatic compensation need a crustal-thickness field; if no interior/differentiation engine emits one, E6 must synthesize it proceduralLY from drivers.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Intended primary driver, but per the system note it is HARD-ZEROED in the current game pipeline. With D12=0 the entire tidal branch (Io/Europa/Enceladus/Triton-class worlds) is dead and the engine collapses to radiogenic+primordial only. This is the single biggest under-supply.

plumbing.name: tidal-heat-flux q_tidal
plumbing.note: True tidal flux needs host mass Mp, semi-major axis a, eccentricity e, mean motion n, Love number k2, and dissipation Q -- i.e. the per-system graph (star/sibling/moon/resonance). L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline, and a single scalar D12 cannot carry the a^-6 / e^2 / resonance structure that makes tidal heating spatially patterned (e.g. polar concentration on Enceladus, sub/anti-jovian asymmetry on Io).

plumbing.name: system-graph: host body + orbital resonance chain
plumbing.note: Resonance (Laplace 1:2:4 for Io/Europa/Ganymede; Enceladus:Dione 2:1) is what FORCES the non-zero eccentricity that sustains tidal heat. A scalar cannot encode 'which siblings am I locked to and how stiff is the chain.'

plumbing.name: target composition / crust strength + density
plumbing.note: From the differentiation/crust engine (rock vs ice vs carbon-rich C-from D10, regolith depth). Needed for pi-group strength term and relaxation. Currently approximated from D2/D10 scalars rather than a real material field.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Warm interior accelerates viscous relaxation of crater topography (Ganymede-style domes, palimpsests, near-total erasure on Io/Enceladus-grade bodies). HARD-ZEROED in the current pipeline, so tidally-heated worlds wrongly retain pristine deep craters.

plumbing.name: system small-body reservoir (impactor SFD, comet vs asteroid mix, planetocentric secondaries from moons/rings, resonance-pumped flux)
plumbing.note: Real impactor population is set by the system: a body near a massive planet, inside a debris belt, or with many moons gets a different impactor SFD slope, velocity distribution, and secondary-cratering load. L0 computes a system graph but does NOT expose it to the per-body pipeline, so every body is bombarded by an identical implicit impactor population.

plumbing.name: epoch flux-decay schedule
plumbing.note: Bombardment intensity per named epoch (early heavy -> declining tail -> present). No driver carries the time-resolved decay curve; must be supplied as an epoch parameter, not a per-body scalar.

plumbing.name: relief / elevation field
plumbing.note: From E6 (tectonics/orogeny) + cratering + volcanism stack: the DEM that flow routes over. THE dominant input — no relief, no drainage. This is a full 2D height FIELD, not a scalar.

plumbing.name: D8 rotation
plumbing.note: Coriolis -> orographic precipitation asymmetry (wet windward / dry leeward), banded rainfall by latitude. Scalar carries rate but NOT the spatial precipitation pattern it should induce.

plumbing.name: D7 tidalLock
plumbing.note: Eyeball-climate hydrology: substellar precipitation maximum, terminator drainage, nightside cold-trap ice/lake. Scalar flag forces a spatial climate pattern the field interface can't express.

plumbing.name: precipitation field
plumbing.note: Ideally an atmosphere/climate engine emits a 2D rainfall map (orographic + latitudinal + eyeball). Currently no such engine exists; E9 must synthesize it from scalars D5/D8/D7/D3 + relief.

plumbing.name: D8 rotation
plumbing.note: Rotation sets Coriolis/zonal wind regime, hence the WIND ROSE (directional drift distribution, bimodality, RDP/DP ratio) that selects dune orientation and bed-instability-vs-fingering mode. A scalar cannot carry a directional distribution or a seasonally-reversing bimodal regime; the actual wind-rose field is the true input and must be synthesized from D8+D3+D7 rather than supplied.

plumbing.name: lithology / induration field
plumbing.note: Yardangs require CONSOLIDATED, erodibility-heterogeneous bedrock; differential erosion needs a hardness map. No current driver carries spatial induration; must be borrowed from the deposition history of upstream engines (lacustrine/volcanic/impact-melt layering).

plumbing.name: loose-sediment supply / source patches
plumbing.note: Sediment availability selects bed-instability vs fingering mode. This is a spatial supply field (where mobilizable grains exist - dry lakebeds, impact ejecta, weathered regolith) that no scalar carries; must be derived from upstream weathering/fluvial/impact outputs.

plumbing.name: system-graph: insolation/season phase, ring-shadow, neighbor tides
plumbing.note: Seasonal forcing of dune orientation (orbital forcing of Titan dunes) and tidal-locked stellar geometry come from the system graph (orbit, obliquity phase, primary). Currently the per-body pipeline does not receive the graph, so seasonal/orbital wind forcing cannot be carried.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: HARD-ZEROED in current pipeline. This is the single biggest gap: without it there is no Enceladus/Europa-grade ice-shell convection, no tiger stripes, no chaos terrain, no cryovolcanic resurfacing. The entire convection + cryotectonic sub-engine is dark until D12 is revived. Tag: dead driver.

plumbing.name: E3 stress tensor field
plumbing.note: Cryotectonic fracture orientation (double ridges, tiger stripes, bands) follows principal-stress directions. A TENSOR FIELD (orientation + magnitude per texel) cannot be carried by the scalar L0 interface; needs a 2- or 3-channel field handoff. Without it, fracture patterns are unsteered (random) rather than tidally/rotationally coherent.

plumbing.name: system graph: tidal/resonance partners
plumbing.note: D12's magnitude physically comes from orbital eccentricity forced by mean-motion resonances with siblings (Enceladus-Dione 2:1, Io-Europa-Ganymede Laplace). L0 computes the graph but does NOT expose it per-body, so tidal heating cannot be derived from real orbital context — it would have to be a free scalar.

plumbing.name: crustal magnetic-anomaly field (spatial pattern)
plumbing.note: Lunar swirls require a SPATIAL map of localized remanent-crust magnetic anomalies that stand off the solar wind. A single scalar D13 (global field strength) cannot carry this 2D pattern; it must come from a crust/impact-magnetization field, which the current pipeline does not produce or expose.

plumbing.name: finished surface albedo/spectral field + feature mask (craters, rays, ejecta, slopes)
plumbing.note: This engine is an EDITOR: it needs the host surface's albedo field plus a mask of fresh-vs-old surfaces (recent crater ejecta/rays, steep slopes) to know what to fade. If upstream only hands a finished color with no age/freshness channel, ray-fading cannot be targeted.

plumbing.name: E4 micrometeoroid/impact flux field
plumbing.note: Per-location gardening/flux that masks swirls and sets local maturation rate (the brief names E4 as the swirl mask). A spatial flux field, not a scalar.

plumbing.name: heliocentric distance / stellar wind + dust environment
plumbing.note: Dust flux scales ~a^-2 and solar-wind flux ~a^-2 with distance to the star; this sets ABSOLUTE maturation rate and the solar-wind-vs-micrometeoroid balance. The per-body scalar interface has no star-distance term, so rate must currently be faked from D1 instead of the real orbital geometry.

plumbing.name: D12 tidalHeating
plumbing.note: Drives Io-grade sulfur volcanism and cryo resurfacing -> the sulfur/cryo palette. Hard-zeroed in current pipeline, so the entire tidally-heated coloration regime is dead; underSupplied as a live signal.

plumbing.name: E4 irradiation field
plumbing.note: Per-patch UV + charged-particle dose map (substellar peak, terminator falloff, pole shielding, magnetic geometry). A scalar driver cannot carry a spatial dose field; needs a real 2D/3D field from E4.

plumbing.name: compositional endmember field
plumbing.note: Per-patch areal fractions of mineral/ice/organic endmembers from upstream lithology/volcanism/cryo engines. Areal mixing is the core method but a scalar interface cannot supply a spatial multi-endmember field.

plumbing.name: surface temperature field
plumbing.note: Latitude/illumination-resolved T (not just D1 scalar) needed for frost line on the body, eyeball substellar melt, and sulfur hue gradients.

plumbing.name: host-star SED
plumbing.note: Stellar spectral type sets ice-albedo wavelength response and apparent color under that illuminant; system graph not exposed per-body.

plumbing.name: orbital irradiation dose / magnetospheric context
plumbing.note: Distance to star + parent-planet magnetosphere (Europa/Io in Jovian radiation belts) sets tholin/salt/sulfur reddening dose; not exposed per-body.

plumbing.name: orbital phase / season clock (true anomaly + time)
plumbing.note: E13 is fundamentally a function of WHERE the body is in its orbit and a running time parameter. The L0 16-scalar vector carries no orbital phase, eccentricity, or animation time; a scalar cannot hold the per-frame/per-epoch phase the engine modulates against. This is the central under-supply.

plumbing.name: orbital eccentricity + argument of perihelion
plumbing.note: Drives hemispheric asymmetry (e.g. longer/colder aphelion-winter -> thicker cap in one hemisphere) and perihelion dust-storm seasonality. No scalar in D1-D16 carries it.

plumbing.name: slope/aspect field (local terrain incidence)
plumbing.note: RSL form on specific warm equator-facing slopes; needs a per-texel slope+aspect field from the terrain/tectonics engine (E-erosion/E-tectonic host). A driver scalar cannot carry a spatial field; must be read from the host heightfield at shade time.

plumbing.name: host crater/araneiform substrate (editor target)
plumbing.note: Frost jets carve spiders into existing polar deposits; spokes need an existing ring field. These are spatial fields/features from upstream engines, not scalars.

plumbing.name: ring system presence + radial structure
plumbing.note: Spokes require a ring; the per-system graph (rings/resonances) exists at L0 but is NOT exposed to the per-body pipeline, so the body cannot currently know it has rings.

plumbing.name: host star spectral type / peak wavelength
plumbing.note: determines optimal pigment absorption band (green vs IR-edge vs purple); the per-body pipeline only sees tempEq, not the actual stellar SED, so pigment-band placement cannot be derived correctly

plumbing.name: land/water mask + elevation + climate-zone field
plumbing.note: E14 needs WHERE land, shallow water, ice, and moisture are to place coverage; this is a 2D surface field, not a scalar

plumbing.name: insolation / day-night + substellar map
plumbing.note: needed for nightside city-light placement and eyeball-biosphere annulus; a per-texel field a scalar cannot carry

plumbing.name: surface mineral/ice albedo baseline
plumbing.note: the abiotic reflectance E14 tints away from; comes from weathering/composition engines as a field

plumbing.name: system graph: moon/satellite inventory (masses, semi-major axes, densities, resonances)
plumbing.note: REQUIRED to decide if rings exist at all (a disrupted inner moon, or a moon straddling the Roche limit) and to place resonance gaps (Cassini Division = 2:1 Mimas) and shepherd-confined ringlets. A 16-scalar L0 vector cannot carry a variable-length list of orbiting bodies with orbital elements. This is the single largest gap for E15.

plumbing.name: system graph: ring presence/extent/optical-depth seed
plumbing.note: Whether the body HAS a ring, and its inner/outer radius and surface density, is a per-system architectural fact (L0 computes the graph but does not expose it). Needs a structured ring descriptor, not a scalar.

plumbing.name: star effective temperature / spectral class
plumbing.note: Sets incident COLOR TEMPERATURE and chromaticity (M-dwarf red-weighted vs G white vs pulsar hard-blue). This is the single most load-bearing input and is NOT in the 16 body drivers — it is a property of the HOST, which lives only in the L0 system-graph that is currently not exposed to the per-body pipeline.

plumbing.name: star luminosity + orbital distance (insolation magnitude)
plumbing.note: Sets absolute brightness and the star's angular disk size (penumbra/limb-softening width). Derivable from system-graph (L,star + a,orbit) but the scalar interface does not currently carry it; D1 tempEq is a downstream PROXY (it bakes in insolation) but cannot be inverted back to direction+angular-size+spectrum.

plumbing.name: host-object class (star vs neutron star vs none/rogue)
plumbing.note: Picks the whole regime branch (stellar / pulsed / starless). A scalar cannot encode 'is the primary a compact object' or 'is this body unbound' — it is a categorical graph fact.

plumbing.name: pulsar spin period + beaming geometry
plumbing.note: Required for the time-periodic pulsed-illumination modulation and hard-spectrum flux. Fully absent from a scalar interface; needs a small structured host record.

plumbing.name: interior/self-emission heat flux
plumbing.note: For the rogue regime the only illumination is self-emission, so the engine must read the interior-heat / volcanic-emission field (D12 tidalHeating + radiogenic from D9/D16, plus any lava-field output from the volcanism engine). D12 is hard-zeroed in the current pipeline, so the rogue regime currently has NO light source to read.

epochs.note: Composition + regime is set at accretion and is the substrate every later epoch edits — it runs first, once per body, and does not re-run per epoch. The ONE exception that is genuinely epoch-coupled is the magma-ocean endmember: it is a present-T_eq state of the rocky class, so if an epoch model ever cooled a body, the same composition would re-label magma-ocean→rocky. Treat that as a cheap re-evaluation of the class label against current T_eq, not a re-derivation of the material budget.

Primarily runs ONCE at body genesis (T1, first epoch) to set the base figure that all later terrain engines displace from — figure is the most foundational layer. But it should re-evaluate per-epoch because two drivers can change across epochs: tidal heating / interior relaxation can soften a cold rigid figure toward a more fluid triaxial one over time, and orbital migration (if the graph ever drives it) can move a body across the Roche limit or into/out of tidal lock. In practice: compute once unless an epoch changes spin, lock state, orbit, or heating, in which case recompute the ellipsoid and let downstream relief re-drape.

Province is set EARLY (T1) and is intended to be laid down once at the body's first epoch as the substrate all later tiers paint within. The one legitimate per-epoch case is editor-like: if a later epoch flips a driver regime (e.g. an atmosphere is acquired/lost, changing D5, or D11 resurfacing wipes a hemisphere), the province field can be RE-RUN for that epoch and the new field supersedes the old as the host substrate — but within a single body's settled history it runs once.

Runs per-epoch as an EDITOR over upstream terrain. Its heat field youthens/resurfaces terrain produced by earlier engines (e.g. cryolava or silicate lava floods existing impact craters and old crust where flux is high, mirroring D11/D16 resurfacing), and its stress field stamps cycloid/lineament fracture decals onto the existing crust. On a circular, non-resonant, or D12-zeroed body it is effectively a no-op. For lava worlds it also acts once to anchor the permanent sub-stellar melt feature.

Primary outputs (oval, airglow, flux mask) are a thin emissive/overlay PASS composited over whatever the terrain/atmosphere engines produced -- it edits the rendered body by adding glow + a dose mask, not new geometry. Field/standoff parameters can be solved ONCE per body (quasi-static dipole). The radiationWeatheringMask is a genuine editor on an UPSTREAM engine's output: it darkens/chemically alters an existing moon-surface albedo/texture (analogous to lava flooding a crater). Aurora animation is per-frame shader time, not per-epoch.

The atmosphere is a terminal SURFACE for gas giants (recompute its look if drivers shift across an epoch, e.g. cooling changes cloud species) and a continuous FORCING layer for terrestrials. Per-epoch it can act as an editor on host surface fields: deposits/forces polar frost caps, lays down wind-streak and dune-orienting shear (handed to the aeolian engine), and sets the eyeball ice/ocean mask that the hydrology/surface engine reads. The live wind+cloud animation itself runs every frame at render time, but the static band/haze/storm-seed layout is solved once per epoch from the then-current driver vector.

Runs per-epoch and edits the existing height/structure field rather than from scratch. First pass writes the primary grain. A later despin/TPW or thermal-regime-change epoch re-runs Steps 1-3 with a rotated stress axis and/or flipped radial-strain sign, BLENDING a second, rotated, fainter lineament generation onto the host terrain (e.g. new equatorial thrust belt cuts across older polar grabens; contraction scarps overprint an earlier expansion-groove field). It also acts as host for downstream editors (lava floods rift floors; weathering aligns to its grain).

Runs per-epoch as the T3 endogenic editor. In a 'volcanic/resurfacing' epoch it FLOODS and embays an earlier engine's output: lava plains drown craters laid down by the impact/cratering engine (lunar-mare analog -- basalt ponding in pre-existing basins ~100 Myr after basin formation), and resurfacing resets the age field young where q is high. On dead/old bodies (low q) it is a near no-op and the cratered host shows through. Cryo worlds get a late-stage refreshing pass (Triton/Europa-style young surface).

Bombardment runs once per named epoch with an epoch-specific flux multiplier (early heavy-bombardment epoch deposits the dense saturated ancient population; later epochs add sparse fresh craters). It is ALSO an editor on host terrain: it reads the current surface age/resurfacing field and craters younger patches less, and later resurfacing engines (lava flooding, cryo, tectonics) in turn edit ITS craters (flooded floors, ghost craters, tectonically sliced rims). So E8a both accumulates across epochs and is mutually editor-coupled with resurfacing tiers.

Runs per-epoch as an EDITOR on the relief produced by E6/cratering/volcanism: it carves valleys (subtractive), fills basins with standing liquid, stamps deltas (additive), and on a catastrophic-spill epoch can carve outflow channels into a pre-existing crater/canyon (e.g. methane/water flooding an impact basin then bursting its rim). Each named epoch re-runs on the then-current host surface, so later volcanism can dam a river or lava can flood a former lakebed, and a later wet epoch re-incises. Drainage maturity accumulates across epochs via D16/D11.

Aeolian is a late tier (T4) EDITOR: it overprints the surface left by tectonics, impacts, volcanism, and fluvial/weathering tiers. It fills existing craters and basins with sand (dune ponding), carves yardangs into previously deposited consolidated units (e.g. old lacustrine or ignimbrite layers), and paints streaks downwind of pre-existing crater rims/hills. Re-runs per epoch when the wind regime or sediment supply changes (e.g. obliquity excursion, atmosphere loss), each pass overprinting the prior surface; the final epoch's pass dominates what is visible.

Runs per-epoch but principally as an EDITOR over earlier engines' output on a host patch: glacial infill smooths and floods the relief engine's basins; cryovolcanic plains and convection cells overwrite earlier terrain and ERASE the cratering engine's craters (resetting terrainAge); frost caps overlay albedo on whatever surface exists. In a multi-epoch run it re-evaluates each epoch as D1/D12/D16 evolve — e.g. an early warm tidally-heated epoch lays convective/cryovolcanic resurfacing, a later cold epoch deposits a static frost cap over it. The frost-cap and glacial passes can also run 'once' for a settled present-day snapshot when epochs aren't needed.

Runs LAST, after the finished surface and all crater/ejecta/ray features exist. It edits that host surface: applies the global maturity darkening/reddening, fades crater rays per their formation age, and lifts albedo back up inside the magnetic-shield/E4 swirl mask. Naturally re-runs per epoch only to re-stamp ages of craters added in later epochs; the edit itself is a single deterministic pass, not iterative.

Re-runs as the terminal overlay after each epoch's geomorphic/volcanic edits so the palette reflects the latest exposed surface (e.g. fresh lava re-darkens, then matures; new impacts expose bright fresh material). Within an epoch it behaves as an editor-on-host over the existing surface fields: it recolors them rather than creating geometry.

Two roles. (a) Per-FRAME/animated overlay: the frost mask, RSL streak length, dust opacity, and ring spokes are cheap shader terms recomputed live against the season clock s -- this is the 'transient' (T5) character. (b) Editor-on-host bakes: the araneiform spider channels are written into the existing polar terrain produced by the erosion/tectonic engines (carving dendritic channels where integrated jet activity is high), and global-dust-storm episodes write a persistent low-frequency albedo-change mask onto the surface produced by upstream engines. Spokes edit the existing ring field from the system graph. So E13 runs last in the tier stack, reads earlier engines' surfaces/heightfields as host patches, and both (a) animates an overlay and (b) leaves permanent edits.

Runs in the final (latest) epoch as an EDITOR over the settled surface produced by terrain/weathering/climate engines: it tints the existing abiotic albedo field, masks city lights against the existing insolation map, and hands NO2/haze edits to the atmosphere engine. It does not author its own terrain. Conceptually could re-run per-epoch to show a biosphere emerging then a technosphere overprinting it, but for a static render one pass at the present epoch suffices.

Ring existence/extent is set once at formation (an early epoch — disruption/impact event), but the ring is then EDITED across later epochs: ring-rain erosion thins it and shifts D16/age (so a late-epoch view shows a darker, lower-mass, possibly vanished ring), and pollution from D11 impact flux darkens it. Spokes and shadow bands are evaluated per-frame from the current epoch's ring state, not baked per-epoch. So: place once, then re-evaluate mass/darkness per epoch; the visible ring is the formation engine's output edited by the erosion/pollution sub-process.

As a render-frame sidecar it is logically evaluated EVERY FRAME (light direction/pulse phase update with camera/time), but it does no history writing and runs no per-epoch pass — its parameters (regime, star color, lock state) are resolved once from drivers+graph and then just sampled. It modifies how tiers READ; it never edits a host patch the way an editor engine (e.g. lava-flood) does.

typeDemotion.note: This is the textbook type-demotion site. (1) deriveComposition (PhysicsEngine.js:367-377) hard-classifies surfaceType via a threshold IF-cascade into 4 discrete strings {carbon, iron-rich, ice-rock, silicate} — the regime endmembers (ocean, sub-Neptune, gas-giant, magma-ocean, stripped-core) are MISSING, so those bodies get their regime hard-assigned elsewhere by named PRESET rather than derived from drivers. (2) planet-archetypes.js encodes named ARCHETYPES (exotic-carbon, gas-giant, volcanic…) each with a hand-listed `bodies`/`presets` set, and EVERY downstream feature declares membership by archetype STRING. So feature presence is gated by a discrete type label, not by the continuous driver that should switch it (carbon crust should appear when C/O>0.8 for ANY body, not only when the preset == 'Carbon (high C/O)'; the F42 comment even admits 'every other preset derives ratio 0 outright' — i.e. the driver is correct but the membership is still gated by the type name as a belt-and-suspenders hard-code). (3) The computed `density` field is discarded instead of driving the rocky↔gas-giant regime fork, so that fork is currently a preset choice, not a physics output. Fix: emit continuous class-membership weights + density-based regime score; let downstream features read the driver/field threshold directly and drop the archetype-string gate to a derived label.

Current code almost certainly hard-codes figure by a discrete body 'type' (planet=sphere, moon=sphere, asteroid=lumpy mesh, comet=special model) rather than deriving axes from drivers. The fixes: (1) Roundness should be a CONTINUOUS function of (massGravity, density, strength) crossing the potato radius — not a planet/asteroid boolean; a small dense moon and a large icy body can swap categories. (2) Oblateness/triaxiality should fall out of D8 rotation + the Maclaurin/Jacobi closed form — not a fixed 'gas giant is squashed, everything else is round' rule. (3) The tidal prolate bulge should derive from D7 + orbit a + M_p, so a close-in locked rock and a far locked moon get DIFFERENT elongation — not a single 'tidally locked = slightly egg-shaped' constant. (4) Comet/Roche shapes should be triggered by volatileFraction/tempEq and the Roche ratio crossing 1, not by an 'isComet'/'isRing-feeder' flag. (5) D12 tidalHeating being hard-zeroed forces every body to the rigid-figure branch — re-enabling it should let heat continuously raise the fluid Love number and thus the achievable figure deformation. Anywhere a switch statement on enum bodyType chooses a mesh is a type-demotion to fix."

High risk that the current code hard-codes provinces by discrete body 'type' (e.g. an enum like ICE_MOON -> always polar caps, IO_TYPE -> always equatorial volcanic belt, TIDALLY_LOCKED -> fixed eyeball radii, CARBON_PLANET -> dark surface). Every one of these should DERIVE from drivers: the ±30 cold-trap edge must be a continuous function of D1/D3/D2 (so a higher-obliquity or warmer body moves or loses the band), the eyeball hot/cold radii must come from D1/D5 (so a thicker atmosphere grows the warm pupil and can erase the frozen antistellar cap), and 'carbon planet' must be a smoothstep on D10 rather than a boolean class. Two demotions are currently UNAVOIDABLE without interface changes: (a) the Io equatorial volcanic province cannot emerge because D12 tidalHeating is hard-zeroed, so any Io-like body would be mis-generated as a passive frost world — this is a dropped-driver demotion, not a code-cleanliness one; (b) leading/trailing dichotomy is forced to a single 'symmetric' outcome because orbit sense, dust donors, and parent-magnetosphere corotation are not exposed to the per-body pipeline, so the engine literally cannot place an Iapetus-type seam from scalars alone.

Current pipeline very likely hard-codes tidal outcomes by discrete body 'type' rather than deriving them from drivers/orbit. Symptoms to expect: (1) Io/Europa/Enceladus behavior keyed to a named moon-type or a 'has cryovolcanism' boolean instead of computing flux from e, a, Im(k2); (2) cycloids stamped as a canned texture for 'ice moon' rather than traced from the rotating stress field; (3) the polar-vs-equatorial heat pattern picked by type instead of by the rigidity/layer switch (D9/D2); (4) silicate-vs-cryo medium chosen by type label rather than by D2 volatileFraction at a given flux; (5) lava-world sub-stellar pool gated on a 'lava planet' flag rather than on D7 tidalLock + D1 tempEq + dayside melt threshold. All of these should fall out of (D7, D12, e, a, D9, D2, D14) once D12 and the orbit elements are actually supplied.

Current pipeline almost certainly switches aurorae on/off by a discrete 'has magnetic field' / planet-type flag (e.g. 'gas giant gets aurora, rocky doesn't') and likely fixes aurora color to Earth green. Both should be DERIVED: oval geometry from Rmp(M,Psw) and theta_a (continuous, so weak fields give a wide low-latitude wash rather than a binary present/absent oval), and color from D4 species + D5 density (a CO2 or carbon-planet atmosphere should NOT glow Earth-green). The plasma-torus/satellite-footprint feature is presumably a hard-coded 'Jupiter-like' decoration; it should instead fire whenever D12>0 and the system graph reports a close volcanic moon, for ANY giant. Polar caps as escape zones are likely cosmetic-only; they should feed D6 retention as a continuous open-area term (with the counterintuitive sign: more open cap = MORE loss).

Likely hard-coded by discrete body 'type' today: (a) a fixed 'gas-giant' look (Jupiter-banded palette) applied whenever class==giant, rather than deriving jet COUNT/WIDTH from D8 via Rhines and cloud COLOR from D4/D1 condensation — a slow giant should superrotate into ~1 band, a hot giant should show silicate/Fe clouds, not NH3 white; (b) 'terrestrial with atmosphere' getting a default blue sky regardless of D4 (a CH4+UV world should be tholin-orange, a thin dry world dust-tan, a dense-clear world deep blue); (c) tidal-lock eyeball/substellar circulation toggled by a habitability flag instead of emerging from D7+D1+D2; (d) storms/great-spot placed as a decorative type feature instead of seeded at driver-derived jet-shear maxima; (e) sky color chosen from a per-type LUT rather than from a composition->scattering computation. The fix is to make every visible outcome a continuous function of (D8,D7,D1,D4,D5,D6,D13), so identical 'types' diverge when their drivers differ.

Current pipeline almost certainly assigns tectonic look-and-feel by discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'icy moon' -> grooves, 'rocky planet' -> mountains, 'Mercury-like' -> scarps) rather than deriving it from the stress field. Demotion targets: (1) faulting regime/feature class should come from the Melosh latitude-banded stress field + radial-strain sign, NOT a type flag -- the SAME body shows polar grabens AND equatorial thrust belts simultaneously. (2) Mobile-lid vs stagnant-lid should fall out of the gravity/rheology/age stress-ratio gate, not be hard-set per type. (3) Groove/lineament terrain is hard-coded to 'icy moon' but is really a function of D12 tidalHeating (currently zeroed, which is exactly why it can only be faked by type) -- restoring D12 lets a warm rocky or carbide body also fracture. (4) Relief amplitude is likely a per-type constant where it should scale with 1/gravity (D14) and accumulated strain (D16). (5) Tessera/plateau presence should derive from a downwelling/crustal-thickening criterion (crust < ~2/5 lithosphere -> compression), not a 'Venus-like' tag.

Current code almost certainly hard-codes outcomes by discrete body 'type' (e.g. an enum like ROCKY/ICE_MOON/LAVA_WORLD/VOLCANIC selecting a fixed texture or feature set), and with D12 hard-zeroed there is no live tidal pathway, so any 'volcanic moon' look is necessarily faked by type rather than derived. It should instead derive continuously from the scalar heat-flux budget q: a body is volcanic because q crosses the silicate-volcanism threshold, cryovolcanic because q crosses a lower threshold with D2 volatiles present, and dead because q is below threshold -- with Io/Enceladus/Triton emerging as REGIONS of (q, D14, D2) space rather than named types. Likewise edifice height should come from k*q^p/D14 (continuous), not a per-type fixed mountain mesh; and explosive-vs-effusive from the D5 fragmentation threshold, not a per-type flag.

Likely hard-codings to derive instead from drivers/fields: (1) crater MORPHOLOGY almost certainly chosen by a discrete planet 'type' (rocky/icy/lava) rather than by D/Dc with Dc=k*g^-1.25 from D14 plus the D2/D10/D12 rheology family -- the simple->complex->peak-ring->multi-ring->central-pit->palimpsest sequence should be one continuous selector, not a per-type texture set. (2) Small-crater cutoff likely a fixed minimum size or a per-type 'has atmosphere' boolean instead of a continuous d_min(D5) curve. (3) Crater DENSITY likely keyed to an 'old/young' type flag rather than computed from D11 x D16 x epoch-flux with a real equilibrium-saturation switch. (4) Ejecta ray/secondary presence likely an on/off per type instead of derived from crater freshness and D5 (rays are suppressed by space weathering and absent where the atmosphere filters secondaries). (5) Tidally-heated worlds: D12 hard-zeroed means relaxed/palimpsest morphologies can't be selected at all, so Io/Europa/Enceladus-class bodies wrongly render Moon-like pristine deep craters -- an outcome currently fixed by omission rather than derived.

Likely hard-codes 'water planet' vs 'ice planet' vs 'dry planet' as discrete surface TYPES that select a fixed river/ocean texture set, rather than deriving the working fluid and its presence from D1×D2×D4. The correct co-genesis form: fluid identity (H2O/CH4/C2H6/none), liquid-stable range, channel sinuosity/color, karst-on/off, and lake fill fraction should all fall out continuously from drivers — a body at ~92 K with methane gets juvenile low-incision drainage + polar lakes automatically, not because it was tagged 'Titan-type'. Similarly 'has rivers' is probably a boolean flag where it should be the emergent result of (atmosphere present AND fluid liquid-stable AND relief present). Outflow channels and deltas are probably decorative presets rather than consequences of the actual base-level/spill computation.

Current code likely hard-codes 'dune type' (barchan vs linear vs star) and 'has yardangs/streaks yes-no' by a discrete planet/biome TYPE, and applies a fixed slip-face look. Both should derive from continuous drivers/fields: dune morphology must emerge from (wind-rose bimodality b from D8/D3/D7) x (sediment-supply field S) via the bed-instability/fingering selection rule, not a type switch; yardang presence must require a consolidated, heterogeneous lithology field plus low-bimodality unidirectional drift, not a tag; streak brightness/direction must come from local transportability T and RDP, not a preset. Slip-face angle should read the material angle-of-repose (near-constant ~33 deg, gravity-independent) rather than a per-type constant, while dune WAVELENGTH/HEIGHT scale with gravity and grain size. 'Dust planet' look should be the (1-T)*dustBudget mantle output, not a discrete skin.

Current pipeline almost certainly hard-codes cryosphere by discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'ice moon' -> always shows generic white ice; 'Pluto-like' -> reddish N2; 'Mars-like' -> polar caps) rather than deriving from drivers. The correct derivation: ice SPECIES and color emerge from D4 atmoComposition + which frost point D1/D5 actually meet (a hot body never shows N2; a CO2-atmosphere body shows CO2 caps); cap GEOMETRY emerges from D3 (polar) vs D7 (nightside) not from a 'tidally locked moon' flag; whether you get convection/chaos/tiger-stripes emerges from the continuous D12*D14*thickness Rayleigh proxy crossing a critical value, NOT from an 'active icy moon' boolean. Most damaging demotion: with D12 hard-zeroed, the engine likely fakes 'Europa-look' or 'Enceladus-look' as a static texture preset keyed to type, instead of producing it as the genuine output of basal-heat-driven convection + stress-steered fracture. Restore D12 and the E3 tensor and these features become emergent, letting an ARBITRARY driver combination (e.g. a high-iron, low-tilt, mildly tidally-heated CH4 world) produce a novel, never-preset cryosphere.

Likely current hard-codings to demote: (a) crater-ray brightness/fade probably set by a discrete 'crater type' (rayed vs unrayed) or a fixed age cutoff, instead of deriving from per-crater formation-age stamp -> exp maturity relaxation against a body-specific tau. (b) Swirls likely either absent or hand-placed by 'has swirls' boolean rather than emerging from a baked magnetic-shield mask * the maturity edit. (c) Darkening/reddening amount likely a per-body constant (or per planet-type 'rocky/icy' enum) instead of M * f(D9 ironFraction) for the silicate branch vs an ice-radiolysis LUT selected by D1/D2. (d) Maturation rate probably global/constant rather than scaled by heliocentric distance (~a^-2) and damped by global magnetic field D13 -- so a Mercury-like body should mature micrometeoroid-fast while a magnetized iron-rich body matures slower, neither of which falls out of a type tag. (e) 'Background albedo' for old terrain likely a fixed value per type rather than the saturation limit of the maturity curve.

High demotion risk. Current code almost certainly assigns palette by a discrete body 'type' (e.g. 'Mars-like'->red LUT, 'moon'->grey, 'ice'->white, 'lava'->black, 'Io'->yellow). These should instead emerge: red is not a type but D9 x oxygen-availability(D4,1-D10) x time(D16); grey-and-dark is maturity = f(airless D6, exposure D11, shielding 1-D13, age D16); white is frost = f(D2, T<frost); black is either basalt mineralogy, magma at high D1, OR carbon-planet at D10>0.8 -- three different physical causes that a 'lava type' collapses into one. Sulfur yellow/red must be a temperature/allotrope ramp gated by tidal-heating-driven volcanism, not an 'Io' flag. Tholin reddening must be dose-driven (E4 + orbital context), not an 'outer icy moon' flag.

Current code very likely hard-codes 'this is a Mars-type body -> draw RSL + a CO2 cap + dust storms' and 'this is a Saturn-type -> draw ring spokes' by discrete archetype. These should instead derive from drivers: frost species and cap from D4 (composition) + D1/D2 thresholds, not a 'Mars' flag; RSL gated by (D5>0) AND (warm-season slope temp crossing) AND a real slope/aspect field, not by planet type; ring spokes gated by ring-presence (system graph) AND D13 magnetic field AND equinox phase, so a strongly-magnetized ringed body of ANY type gets spokes and a weakly-magnetized one does not. The cap-hemisphere asymmetry should come from eccentricity/argument-of-perihelion, not a baked 'south cap bigger' constant. Frost-flush jets/fans should fire wherever the sublimation front passes over loose substrate, not only at a hard-coded polar latitude.

Current pipeline almost certainly switches biosphere/technosphere on a discrete world 'type' (e.g. an enum like EARTHLIKE / GARDEN / INHABITED that hard-codes 'add green + city lights'). This should be demoted: (a) presence/lushness of biosphere should be a continuous function of D15 x D1 x D2 x D16, not a type flag; (b) pigment hue + reflectance-edge wavelength should derive from host-star peak emission and surface light/moisture regime via a LUT, not a fixed green; (c) technosignature density/extent/tier (none -> faint lights -> global mosaics -> megastructures) should be a continuous ramp on habitability x age, not a boolean 'civilized' bit; (d) 'green plants' is itself a type-demotion of pigment chemistry — purple/orange/IR-edge biospheres should be reachable for the right stellar+atmospheric drivers.

Current pipeline almost certainly hard-codes 'gas giant → has Saturn-style rings, terrestrial → no rings' by body TYPE. That should derive from drivers + graph: a ring is present iff there is debris inside R_Roche (a disrupted/Roche-straddling moon in the system graph) — a rocky planet that ate a moon SHOULD get rocky (dark) rings, and a gas giant with no disrupted satellite should get none. Likewise spokes are likely toggled by 'is this Saturn?' rather than gated by D13 magnetic field + D11 impact flux + D2/D1 cold-O2 cohesion; ring color is likely a fixed 'icy white' rather than derived from D2/D9/D1 (rock-vs-ice composition). Ring-rain bands, if present at all, are probably a Saturn-specific decal instead of being placed by the dipole L-shell footprint of ring-gap field lines (D13 geometry + ring radii). Shadow-band latitude should come from D3, not a fixed texture.

High demotion risk. Current code almost certainly hard-codes a single 'sunlight' regime: a fixed white directional light with a hard terminator, regardless of host. Likely discrete-type hard-codings to remove: (a) light COLOR baked white instead of derived from the host star's effective temperature -> should be a continuous blackbody LUT keyed by star Teff so an M-dwarf world is red-lit and a hot-star world blue-lit by derivation, not by tag; (b) terminator SHARPNESS as a constant instead of derived from star angular size + atmospheric optical depth (D5/D4); (c) 'eyeball planet' treated as a discrete planet TYPE with pre-painted ice rings, when it should emerge from D7 making lightDir static while the existing climate/ice tiers read that static insolation; (d) rogue/starless and pulsar worlds likely have NO branch at all (default-sunlit), so they're implicitly type-demoted to 'normal star' — the regime must derive from host-class in the system-graph; (e) substellar lava glow keyed to a 'lava planet' type rather than emerging wherever insolation*albedo + interior heat exceeds the melt threshold.

refutedClaims.claim: C/O>0.8 carbon-planet swap (graphite/SiC/diamond flip, Kuchner-Seager 2005) is a real published threshold, so gating F42 on D10 is sound — but 0.8 is a modeling choice and ≳1 is the more commonly cited threshold.
refutedClaims.reasoning: First half is solidly confirmed: C/O ≳ 0.8 flips the condensation sequence to graphite/SiC/TiC with CO locking up oxygen (Kuchner & Seager 2005; Bond et al. 2010), so gating the carbon class on D10 is physically sound, and the code (PhysicsEngine.js:369 `if (carbonToOxygen > 0.8)`) implements exactly this. However the dossier's hedge that '≳1 is the more commonly cited threshold' is overstated/inaccurate: the literature most commonly cites C/O ≳ 0.8 as the carbon-rich onset (Bond et al. 2010 established 0.8 'more precisely'), with 0.8 being the standard quoted figure, not 1.0. I mark the COMPOSITE claim refuted because that specific sub-assertion is wrong, though the load-bearing part (0.8 gate is sound) is correct.

refutedClaims.claim: Tidally-locked 'eyeball' province geometry is genuinely radial about the substellar point with concentric terminator rings, so a closed-form radial province field about subStellarDir is physically faithful, not just convenient.
refutedClaims.reasoning: Partially overstated. The radial/eyeball pattern is faithful ONLY for the static (no/weak heat transport) case: hot eyeballs (lava substellar pool, e.g. 55 Cnc e) and the idealized frozen-eyeball with a substellar melt pupil. But the cited M-dwarf climate literature (Hu & Yang 2014 PNAS; Yang et al.) shows that with a DYNAMIC ocean or significant atmosphere the open-ocean/warm region is NOT radially symmetric — it becomes a 'lobster' with equatorial tail extending onto the nightside, and nightside warming breaks the concentric-ring geometry. So 'genuinely radial ... concentric terminator rings' is true for the airless/thin-atmo end-state but false for the temperate/thick-atmo cases the dossier wants to cover (where it grows a 'warm pupil' via D5). The radial closed form is convenient and adequate for the static end-states, but calling it physically faithful in general is overstated; the very D5-thick-atmosphere regime the selector targets is where radial symmetry breaks. Marking refuted on the generality claim.

refutedClaims.claim: Atmospheric filtering can be captured by a single monotonic cutoff diameter d_min(D5); the dossier gives Mars ~few m-8 m, Titan ~6-8 km, Venus ~20-30 km.
refutedClaims.reasoning: The MECHANISM (atmosphere as high-pass filter, cutoff grows with column mass) is correct and the cross-body 3-order-of-magnitude span is real. But specific numbers are overstated/mis-stated, which is why I mark refuted per the 'default refuted if not independently confirmable as stated' rule. Venus: the crater-ABSENCE threshold is ~2-3 km (smallest possible ~150-300 m), and the ~10-30 km figure is the regime where craters are DISTORTED/MULTIPLE from fragmentation — not a clean 'cutoff' as the dossier implies. Mars: published atmospheric downturn for primaries is ~10-60 m / even down to ~10-20 cm in some models, broadly consistent with 'few m', so that one is roughly OK.
